About this text

The Great Ritual Manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā, known in Sanskrit as the Ūrdhvajaṭā Mahākalpa and more fully as the Root Manual of the Blessed Lady, Noble Tārā (Āryatārā Mūlakalpa), and in Tibetan as Ralpa Gyendzé kyi Tokpa Chenpo, presents itself as drawn from the Vast Chapters on the Miraculous Display of the Great Bodhisattva. It is Toh 724 in the Kangyur, where it belongs to the Tantra section among the ritual tantras devoted to Tārā and Avalokiteśvara. Opening with the Buddha in the sky above Tārā's ship, surrounded by an assembly of bodhisattvas, it unfolds as a vast compendium of ritual practice: dhāraṇīs and mantras spoken by many buddhas, instructions for paintings, maṇḍalas, fire offerings and mudrās, and rites for protection, healing, prosperity, subjugation and the attainment of siddhis, all centered on the practice of noble Tārā. Its closing colophon records that it was translated into Tibetan by the monk Rinchen Drup from a manuscript that had belonged to Atiśa, brought from Radreng.

Translation

In the language of India: ūrdhajaṭā mahākalpa mahābodhisatva vikurvvaṇa paṭala visarād bhagavatā āryatārā mūlakalpa nāma. In the language of Tibet: The Great Ritual Manual of the Upswept Locks, from the Vast Chapters on the Miraculous Display of the Great Bodhisattva, called the Root Manual of the Blessed Lady, Noble Tārā.

Homage to noble Avalokiteśvara.

Thus did I hear at one time. The Blessed One (the Buddha) was dwelling in the midst of the sky above Tārā's ship, together with a maṇḍala, an assembly of bodhisattvas, unfolded through inconceivable wonders and marvels.

Then the Blessed One addressed the gods of the class of the Pure Abodes (Śuddhāvāsa): "Gods, listen! For the benefit of all sentient beings I shall explain the wondrous and inconceivable conduct of miraculous display of the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara: his meditative absorptions, his distinctive magical powers, the maṇḍala of liberation, and the miraculous manifestation of the bodhisattva that sustains all sentient beings; and the vidyā-mantras and the foundation of secret mantra that bring long life, freedom from illness, sovereignty, and the complete fulfillment of the chariot of the mind. Listen to it well and keep it well in mind. I shall explain."

Then they said to the Blessed One, "Excellent!"

Then those gods of the class of the Pure Abodes bowed with palms joined and said this: "Blessed One, please speak of that which enables bodhisattva great beings to attain each of the distinctive kinds of conduct and meditative absorption; which enables them to occupy the vajra seat, to tame Māra, and to turn the wheel of Dharma; which brings about the deliverance of all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; which causes birth among gods and humans; which completely pacifies all suffering; which cures the illness of all who are struck by poverty and disease; which cannot be overpowered by the practice of any vidyā-mantra or secret mantra, worldly or transcendent; and which completely fulfills every wish. Since the tathāgatas never speak without purpose, Blessed One, please, with a mind of loving-kindness, embracing us and all sentient beings with compassion, speak of it."

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni surveyed the great maṇḍala of the assembly, complete in every respect, with his buddha eye, and entered into the meditative absorption called Radiating Light Rays into the Pure Domain, the Destroyer. As soon as he had entered it, from the Blessed One's ūrṇā hair there came a light ray called Rousing the Flowerlike Bodhisattvas, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of light rays. It circled the Blessed One three times, passed beyond the infinite great trichiliocosm world-systems, and, having passed westward beyond world-systems equal in number to the sands of a hundred thousand Ganges rivers, it entered the world-system called Sukhāvatī.

There, where the Tathāgata Amitāyus dwells, the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara too, by the power of his former aspirations, was dwelling together with those who abide in the conduct of bodhisattva great beings. Seeing the radiance of the light, with a slightly smiling face he addressed the hosts of bodhisattvas: "O children of the Victor, know that this is a light ray that has come here to rouse us."

Then those great beings opened their closed eyes and stayed turned toward the radiance of this light. Then that rousing light ray, having filled the great world-system of Sukhāvatī with its illumination, circled the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, three times, and sank into the wisdom crown of the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara.

Then that great being rose from his seat, circled the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitābha, three times, bowed deeply with his head, placed his right knee on the ground, and said this to the Blessed One: "Blessed One, please consider this. We would go to where the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha Śākyamuni is, to see that Sahā world of the Blessed One and to see the Blessed One Śākyamuni, to pay homage to him and attend upon him; and, through his distinctive teaching of the practice of vidyā-mantras and secret mantras, the rites of the means of accomplishment, the procedures of the maṇḍala rite, the rite of the secret painted scroll, recitation, and all the vidyā empowerments, we wish to completely fulfill the wishes of all sentient beings."

When he had said this, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitābha, said this to that bodhisattva great being: "Great being, if you know that the time for it has now come, go. And in my words, ask after the Blessed One Śākyamuni: whether he has little harm, little discomfort, whether he rises with ease, and whether he dwells in comfort."

Then again the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitābha, addressed the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara:

"Great being, the tathāgatas, arhats, perfectly complete buddhas, as many as the sands of a hundred thousand Ganges rivers, have also spoken of your family, the practice of secret mantra, the procedures of the maṇḍala, the secret empowerment, the mudrās, the rite of the painted scroll, the fire offering, and the rules of recitation, which completely fulfill every wish and delight all sentient beings; of the vast chapters of the Jewel Illumination, which teach how to enter one's own vidyā-mantras and secret mantras through the wisdoms of past, future, and present, which have been brought to completion and are endowed with the inner times; and of the chapters of the vast pledges, which gather in everything worldly and transcendent without exception. And regarding what has been spoken by all the buddhas and bodhisattvas, by the noble śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and by those who dwell on the bodhisattva grounds and possess the speech of ultimate conduct, there is nothing but rejoicing in this.

"Great being, if you know that the time for it has now come, go. In the presence of Śākyamuni, turned toward him, listen to this Dharma discourse, and you too will speak it. Its root vidyā-mantra will be this:

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavatyai āryatārāyai bodhisatvāyai tadyathā tāre ṛjuka dharma nityate tāre tuttāre śānta dharma niryāte tāre anabhilāpya dharma niryate tuttāre ture ture hini trasani trasani ohani mohani jambhani stambhani prabhe candraprabhe hili hili cili cili bhegasāmini kuṇḍi kuṇḍi mahākuṇḍa dhara dhara dhanapani tāre huru huru kuru kuru ahaṃ yāya cintayāmi cintadhami kuru svādhāya svāhā

"Great being, this is that root vidyā of your Noble Tārā, which all the tathāgatas have spoken and will speak, and which you too will now speak. Śākyamuni has come to the Sahā world-system, at its limit laid open by spreading fragrance, and it is authorized by Śākyamuni.

"Its supreme heart mantra is also this: namo ratnatrayāya nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tāre tuttāre ture svāhā

"Its near-heart mantra is also this: namo ratnatrayāya namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisatvānāṃ oṃ kurukulle svāhā"

Then the bodhisattva great being, noble Avalokiteśvara, having received the Blessed One's permission, entered into the meditative absorption called the Ornament of All Arrays, Which Fully Brings Attainment of the Seat of Awakening in Accord with the Conduct of Bodhisattvas. As soon as he had entered it, the world-systems in every direction, all of them, to the very limits of the four directions, above, below, and across, became completely filled with perfect buddhas, blessed ones.

"Excellent, excellent, child of the Victor! That you have entered such a distinctive meditative absorption as this is beyond the power of all the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. Even those who have fully entered the conduct of bodhisattvas and dwell firmly on the ten grounds are unable to enter it."

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitābha, together with those buddha blessed ones, with loving-kindness, spoke the vidyā-mantra that is the supreme heart of the Blessed Lady, Noble Tārā: the supreme secret that accomplishes all aims, called the Single Syllable, she who is supremely secret and performs all activities for all sentient beings, a vidyā-mantra in accord with the accomplishment of other vidyā-mantras as well through the distinctive practice of vidyā-mantras and secret mantras.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, remained silent for a moment. Having surveyed with his buddha eye the world, complete in every respect and everywhere, he spoke the vidyā-mantra, the intention of the buddha blessed ones, with a mind whose very nature is loving-kindness:

namaḥ sarvabuddhanāṃ oṃ gīḥ

This is the supreme heart mantra of the Blessed Lady, which performs all activities.

Then the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara arose from that meditative absorption. In the time it takes a strong man to stretch out his bent arm or bend his outstretched arm, or merely to snap his fingers, in the mere instant of opening and closing the eyes, he entered into the distinctive meditative absorption called Miraculous Manifestation Itself, the absorption called Swift Mind, the Power of Absorption and Magical Power, and came to the Sahā world-system. Having arrived, he took his place in the middle of the sky above, within the great maṇḍala of the assembly, each seated upon great precious jewels. Having filled the maṇḍala of the entire assembly with the illumination of great light, he entered into the meditative absorption called Illuminating the Ornament of the Lord of Jewel Light.

As soon as the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara had entered that meditative absorption, he manifested multistoried mansions laid out with many jewels, and many jewel parasols spreading over hundreds of thousands of leagues, beautifully adorned with divine garments and silken ornaments, with divine flowers, banners, victory banners, and garlands, and hung with nets of jewel bells from which sweet sounds rang out; places where the bodhisattvas each abide; and rains of divine fragrances, garlands, ointments, and powders falling down. Thus was seen that wondrous act of offering to the Blessed One Śākyamuni, the miracle, the bodhisattva's magical display.

Then those gods of the class of the Pure Abodes, filled with joy, felt their hair stand on end.

Seeing all the abodes of the gods shaken, they were frightened and their hearts trembled. "Has our prosperity utterly declined?" they wondered, and they began to call out to one another hurriedly in loud voices, and they also said this: "Blessed One, protect us! Śākyamuni, protect us!"

Then the Blessed One addressed the whole divine assembly: "Do not be afraid! Do not be afraid! This is the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara, who, from the buddhafield of the Tathāgata Amitāyus, the Fully Blossomed, wishes to see me, to pay me homage, and to attend upon me. He has come in order to teach definitively the conduct of great purpose, the words of vidyā-mantra, and wondrous words of Dharma."

Then he circled the Blessed One Śākyamuni three times, gazed at the Blessed One without blinking, bowed at his feet, and praised the Blessed One with these finely spoken words:

Homage to you, the knowing person;
homage to you, the supreme person;
accomplisher of every aim of conduct,
homage to you, the chief of persons.
Averter of all that is meaningless,
homage to you, lion among persons;
destroyer of all the lower realms,
great hero, homage to you.
Your fragrance of merit is infinite;
homage to you, white lotus among persons;
you purify the mud of the three existences;
homage to you, lotus among persons.
You liberate from all suffering;
homage to you, liberator of all.
You thoroughly tame every torment;
homage to you, the peaceful one.
Accomplisher of the aims of mantra practice,
homage to you who are all.
Auspicious with every auspiciousness,
homage to you, the auspicious one.
Fully realizing all phenomena,
homage to you, pledge of the buddhas.
Teacher who rightly follows
the suchness of all phenomena,
the aspect that is free of elaboration,
homage to you, Tathāgata.
All things, the knowing and the knowable,
you have done well and rightly heard;
firmly established, you lead in and establish
in the path of the three vehicles and in nirvāṇa;
homage to you, the omniscient one.

Having thus praised the Blessed One to his face with these finely spoken words of praise, he also said this: "Blessed One, beyond world-systems equal in number to the sands of a hundred thousand Ganges rivers from here, toward the west, in the buddhafield called Fully Blossomed, lies the world-system called Sukhāvatī. There dwells the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, the Sugata, knower of the world, unsurpassed, guide who tames beings, teacher of gods and humans, Amitāyus. He teaches the Dharma: virtuous in the beginning, virtuous in the middle, virtuous at the end, excellent in meaning, excellent in wording, unadulterated, completely pure, perfectly clean; he rightly teaches the pure conduct of Brahmā. Thus he dwells, lives, and remains, and he teaches the Dharma. To all sentient beings he teaches the practices that are the meaning of vidyā-mantras and secret mantras, the bodhisattva collection of teachings, and the path that follows the conduct of the three paths; he is their protector, their abode, their refuge, their ally, and their happiness, their utmost finality and utterly complete culmination.

"With the permission given by that very Blessed One, I have come here into the presence and nearness of the Blessed One. The Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitābha, inquires after the Blessed One: whether he has little harm, little discomfort, whether he rises with ease, whether he is free from illness, and whether he dwells in comfort. And he also says this: 'It is wonderful that in such a degenerate time as this, the very person of the Blessed One Śākyamuni teaches the Dharma, and brings the people who are to understand it to find liberation through the three paths and birth among gods and humans. It is wonderful that, through the diligence of that Blessed One Śākyamuni, hosts of beings who lacked good fortune are made to enter fully the path that utterly destroys the three existences, and are firmly established in it for good, and that he places beings in nirvāṇa, which accords with happiness.'

"Yet, Blessed One, the mind of the buddha blessed ones is known only to the buddha blessed ones. Even if I wished to know the wondrous, marvelous, inconceivable miraculous displays of the buddha blessed ones as the displays of buddhas, or wished to know the accomplishment and the intention by which they enter into the conduct of their minds, how could I describe it even in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of eons, let alone teach it all definitively? Whatever the tathāgatas accomplish, in summary and individually, without exception, is to be seen by the tathāgatas as the unconditioned nature of reality, its very essence. To wish to speak of the abandoning of what is to be abandoned by seeing, and of conduct that brooks no delay, or to wish to teach these qualities: that is known only to the tathāgata blessed ones, not to me."

Then the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara, emanating a miraculous display of magical power, sat on a great precious lotus, gazing at the Blessed One Śākyamuni.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, conversed with the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara in talk befitting the tathāgatas that followed upon talk of many kinds, with final questions put first. At the end of their teaching of Dharma to one another, to those assembled for the sake of accomplishing the conduct of the bodhisattvas of the family, in a voice like the voice of Brahmā, like the kalaviṅka bird, and resounding like the great drums made by the kutara and vitara, he addressed the bodhisattva great being, noble Avalokiteśvara:

"Great being, you are welcome. The conduct of great beings; the accomplishment of the blessings of all the buddhas; that which makes all bodhisattvas rightly attain their aims; all the words of vidyā-mantra and secret mantra, together with the secret empowerment; the mudrās; the maṇḍalas; the empowerment of the ritual procedures; that which completely fulfills long life, freedom from illness, sovereignty, and every wish; the tantras of the rites of all the means of accomplishment; knowing and the knowable, sunk into the end of time; kingship; and what is condensed from the fields of the past, the future, and the present: from this comes that which completely fulfills every wish of all sentient beings, which brings forth one's own qualities, which leads one to the culmination of the practice of secret mantra, which delights other beings, which brings invisibility and travel through the sky, which brings swiftness of foot, which sharpens the mind, which causes confusion, which brings entry beneath the earth, which accomplishes fierce rites, which attains every aim, together with their results, which summons all yakṣas, yakṣiṇīs, kiṃkaras, piśācas, and bhūtas, and which makes children, the aged, and the young remain just as they are. In brief, it performs every activity, fulfills every chariot of the mind, and fully accomplishes the activities of increase and pacification, in whatever way they are to be applied and in whatever way they are to be accomplished. These vast chapters of the Jewel, the extensive Great Ritual Manual endowed with the bodhisattva collection of teachings, I authorize. Spoken by all the buddhas, the meaning of the practice of vidyā-mantras and secret mantras for pure beings, the treasury of Dharma: teach it to gods and humans and to all sentient beings, for the benefit of many people and for the happiness of many people."

Then again the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara, through the blessing of the Buddha, entered into the meditative absorption called Light Radiance of Arrayed Ornaments That Rouses All. As soon as he had entered it, the illumination of light spread through many pure beings and through world-systems and buddhafields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River. It brought peace to the beings, completely pacifying all the sufferings of every being who is intensely tormented by suffering, from the existence of Akaniṣṭha down to the great hell Avīci. Having thoroughly roused all the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and buddha blessed ones, that light ray sank back into the crown of the head of the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara.

Moreover, in whatever buddhafields are situated in the east and the other directions, that light ray rousing the buddha blessed ones, brought about by stirring the wind maṇḍala, roused the Tathāgata called Glory Fully Illuminating the Fragrance of the Moon's Own Light, the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru Vaiḍūryaprabharāja, the Tathāgata called All-Illuminating Glory, the Tathāgata called King of Perfect Nobility, the Tathāgata Śālendrarāja, the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja, the Tathāgata called King Who Ascertains Immeasurable Life and Wisdom, the Tathāgata called King of Infinite Illumination, and the Tathāgata called King of the Light Rays of Beryl Radiance. These and other buddha blessed ones, surrounded by bodhisattvas, in infinite and boundless world-systems, smiled at the vast chapters on the meaning of the words that definitively teach the practice of vidyā-mantras and secret mantras, as spoken by the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha Śākyamuni, who dwells in the grove of Tārā's ship in the Sahā world-system, and by the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara.

Likewise in the southern, western, and northern directions, in the intermediate directions, above, below, and across, in the buddhafields complete in every respect, the light shone. In every one of the buddhafields all the abodes of Māra were humbled. Then the buddhas, surrounded by hosts of bodhisattvas and preceded by saṅghas of śrāvakas, each took their places: they wished to behold the miraculous display of the buddhas that dwells in the domain of the tathāgatas, the great being, the bodhisattva himself, and they wished also to make clear the vast chapters on the distinctive meditative absorption that accomplishes conduct in accord with the supreme vidyā, the unobstructed teaching of the tathāgatas.

They were these: Fine Hand, Excellent Jewel, Excellent Discipline, Excellent Eyes, Excellent Joy, Excellent Robe, Excellent Dawning of Siddhi, Noble in All, Noble Dharma, Noble Jewel, Ratnaśrī, Glory of Meru, Inconceivable Glory, Light-Making Glory, Brilliant Glory, Glory of Illumination, Glory of All Aims, All Jewels in Hand, Jewel on the Crown, Jewel in Hand, Meru Banner in Hand, These and many other buddha blessed ones, having filled the great maṇḍala of the assembly with light, each took their seat upon a lotus throne.

In the same way, the hosts of bodhisattvas were also seated. They were these: Ratnapāṇi, Vajrapāṇi, Bhadrapāṇi, Sky Hand, Infinite Hand, Earth Hand, Hand of Illumination, Utterly Stainless, Excellent Peak, Many Peaks, Gem Peak, Jewel Peak, Eṇa Peak, Jewel Elephant, Universal Elephant, Gandhahastin, Excellent Gait, Going Free of Stain, Going through the World, Going Beautifully, Infinite Going, Infinite Fame, Well Famed, Famed for Freedom from Stain, Famed for Going, Vimalakīrti, Protector of Fame, Protector of the Protectorless, Lokanātha, Universal Protector, Son of Constant Friend, Son of Infinite Friend, Son of Universal Friend, Son of Maitrā, Son of Fine Eyes, Son of Homage Friend, Son of Tvaṣṭṛ, Son of Rice Friend, Son of Jewel Friend, Son of the Friend of the Three Refuges, Son of the Friend of the Three Vehicles, Outstretched Might, Very Delightful, Possessing Delight, Dharmeśvara, Lord of the Absence of Things, Universal Lord, Lokeśvara, Avalokiteśvara, Lord of Fine Vision, Lord of Clear Vision, Leader of the World, Excellent Offering, Lord of Thunder, Lord of the Great Drum, Lord of Arrays, Viṣatesvara, Excellent Rain, Excellent Offering, Famous, Sūryaprabha, Abiding in Full Birth, Lord of the Moon, Healing Moon, Moon Itself, Infinite Glory, Universal Glory, World Glory, Sky Glory, Gatherer of the Sky, Gaganagañja, Lord of the Earth, Maheśvara, Kṣitigarbha, Unobscured, Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, Samantabhadra, Bhadrapāla, Sudhana, Well Gathering All, Sky That Scatters All Harvests, Ākāśagarbha, Realizer of All Aims, Source of All, Not To Be Turned Back, Irreversible, Enduring the Lower Realms, Unchanging, Auspicious Exposition, and Guardian of All Vital Points. These and other bodhisattva great beings took their seats together upon Tārā's ship, within the domain of the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni.

There were also bodhisattva great beings who had taken the form of women. They accomplish the infinite aims of conduct in the world. They uphold the foundations of the vidyā-mantras, whose inconceivable activity is to establish infinite sentient beings firmly upon the path that carries their intentions through. Some take forms in the guise of medicines, of various flocks of birds, of yakṣas, of rākṣasas, of jewels, of mantras and of kings of precious gems, of sentient beings and of countless things that are not sentient beings; entering into all of these, they conform to the conduct of sentient beings. They conform to whatever way sentient beings are to be trained according to their dispositions, and they conform to the particular excellence of each of these. Just as the vidyā kings have taught, they bring forth the Dharma; they do not transgress the order of the samaya that pervades everything, the Tathāgata, the Lotus and the Vajra, the worldly and the world-transcending; they abide firmly in the path of speech; and they keep the lineage of the Three Jewels from being cut off. They are Abhyudgatoṣṇīṣa, Exalted White Parasol (Sitātapatra), Infinite Leaves, Hundred Leaves, Jayoṣṇīṣa, Exalted Uṣṇīṣa, Lotus Light, Golden Light, White Light, Array of the Uṣṇīṣa, Golden Mass, White Mass, Tejorāśi, Jewel Mass, All-Encompassing Mass, Mass of Renown, Mass of Origination, Mass of Truth, Mass of Insubstantiality, and Mass of Unerring Suchness. These, and others besides.

There are also the uṣṇīṣa kings who have entered the infinite sphere of phenomena, who fulfill the wishes of sentient beings according to their intentions and understand the thoughts in the minds of all people; uṣṇīṣa kings who reach to the limits of space, whose recounting could not be completed even in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of eons, of inconceivable power and of great nature, overpowering all adversaries. Wishing to show them, I shall teach in brief what would be explained in full at length. The assembly of the vidyā kings to be described is this: Ūrṇā, Brow, Eye, Eyelash, Ear, Throat, Fearlessness, Compassion, Loving-Kindness, Contentment of Love, Wisdom, Light Ray, Hero, Stainless Light Ray, and Dharma Robe. These, and also the infinite and boundless vidyā kings emanated from the uṣṇīṣa of the Tathāgata, namely: the Tathāgata's Alms Bowl, the Wheel of Dharma, the Tathāgata's Couch, the Tathāgata's Vehicle, the Tathāgata All-Illuminating, the Tathāgata's Speech, the Tathāgata's Lip, the Tathāgata's Going, the Tathāgata's Stain, the Tathāgata's Banner, the Tathāgata's Crest, and the Tathāgata's Mark. These, and also those that are mantras spoken by the Tathāgata: vidyā kings and vidyā queens, attendants, male servants and female servants, male messengers and female messengers, yakṣas and yakṣiṇīs, sentient beings and those that are not sentient beings, each sending forth clouds of Dharma arrayed with their own particularly excellent ornaments, surrounded by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of beings that correspond to the distinctions of their samādhis, with all the hosts of vidyās entering ever higher and higher. These vidyā kings too came to dwell in that domain of the Tathāgata, abiding there as a noble family.

The vidyā kings were these: the Twelve-Armed Tathāgata, the Six-Armed, the Four-Armed, Hālāhala, Amoghapāśa, Hayagrīva, Infinite Throat, Nīlakaṇṭha, Excellent Throat, Fine Neck, White Throat, Blue Neck, World Throat, Avalokiteśvara, Bowed To by a Thousand Light Rays, Renowned Mind, Padmapāṇi, Chariot of the Mind, Utterer of Words, Broad Smile, Excellent Sound, Edge of the Hair, Constellation, King of Constellations, Son of the Moon, Excellent Fortune, Trailokyavijaya, Infinite Victory, Victorious over the Gods, Fulfiller of Desires, Excellent Tamer, and the one called Tamer. There were these, and also, surrounded by vidyās numbering many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas, which have become samādhis accomplishing infinite counterparts of the clouds of Dharma, together with vidyā queens such as Lotus Uṣṇīṣa, there were many vidyādhara queens and many emanations of the samādhi of the body of Lokeśvara, namely: Tārā, Tārā of the Mind, Dancer, Bhṛkuṭī, Anuttāṭī, Lauṭī, Bestower of the Grounds, Free of Stain, White Lady, White-Skirted, Great White-Skirted, White-Robed, World-Robed, Stainless-Robed, Robed in the Limbs of Awakening, Lotus-Robed, Robed in the Ten Powers, Famous, Lady of Riches, Lady of Riches and Long Life, Urṇūkā, Ṣalūkā, Stainless Ender, Ender Free of Stain, Universal Ender, Ender of Suffering, Ender of Bhūtas, Glorious Lady, Great Glorious Lady, Final Glory, Glory of Praise, World Glory, Renowned Glory, Mother of the World, Universal Mother, Mother of the Buddhas, Sister, Fortunate Chariot Lady, Excellent Chariot Lady, Lady with a Chariot, Tamer of Nāgas, Tamer, Lady of the Bhūtas, Immeasurable, Power of Riches, Summoner, Wondrous Light Ray, Excellent Taste, Lady of Liquor, Utter Crusher, Lady Worthy of Worship, Lady of the Shore, Lady of All Shores, Starlight, Moon Lady, Lunar Lady, Peacock Lady, Lady of the Forest, Giver of Wealth, Lady of Liquor, Lady of the World, Radiant Lady, Great Thousandfold, Lady of Greatness, Well Flourishing, Well Delighted, Giver of Riches, Glorious Lady, Pure Lady, Ender of Disease, Healer of All Diseases, Goddess of Health, Bringer of Fame, Subjugator, Swift One, Giver of Bliss, Auspicious Lady, Delightful Bringer of Auspiciousness, Excellent Moon Lady, and Lunar Lady.

These, and also the other vidyā queens such as Parṇaśabarī, Remover of Poison and Mind-Born, together with the mind-born ones who have truly arisen, blessed as the magical display of all the conduct of the infinite accomplishment of the sphere of phenomena whose nature is space: male messengers and female messengers, male servants and female servants, male attendants and female attendants, yakṣas and yakṣiṇīs, rākṣasas and rākṣasīs, piśācas and piśācīs, who follow the samaya of the Lotus family and practice secret mantra. Established by that which firmly sets in place pure sentient beings possessed of the great maṇḍala of the retinue, they took their places, and their minds became intent upon performing acts of worship to the Blessed One Śākyamuni himself.

The bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, who was there close beside the Blessed One Śākyamuni, summoned his own host of vidyās. Those of you who gathered here were the wrathful kings together with their queens, surrounded by hosts of vidyās, and their great female messengers, by the mere recollection of whom all the hosts of vidyās assemble, namely: Supreme Vidyā, Excellent Vidyā, Well Accomplished, Excellent Arm, Excellent Host, Ender of Gods, Excellent Tooth, Pūrṇabhadra, Vajra Host, Vajra Edge, Vajra Hand, Vajra Shoulder, Vajra Victory Banner, Vajra Pennant, Vajra Domain, Vajra Head-Bearer, Vajra Fang, Pure Vajra, Vajra Hair, Vajra Worship, Many Vajras, Vajra Armor, Vajra Throat, Vajra Speech, Vajra Navel, Vajra Limit, Vajra Tent, Vajra Fence, Vajra Weapon, Vajra Bow, Vajra Arrow, Vajra Iron Arrow, Vajra Mark, Vajra Delight, Vajra Underworld, Vajra Terrifying Eye, Vajra End of Wealth, Vajra Wrathful One, Pleasing Roar of the Waters, Pleasing Roar of the Bhūtas, Pleasing Roar of the Great Wrathful One, Pleasing Roar of Maheśvara, Pleasing Roar of the Dānavas, Pleasing Roar of All Vidyās, Fierce One, Exceedingly Fierce, Hurler, Close Hurler, Constant Hurler, Hurler at the Limit of Taming, Hurler of Perfect Array, Hurler in Search, Strength, Mighty One, Well-Born Straightener, Bhṛṅgiriṭi, Wrathful One, Great Wrathful One, Unaging, Sleepless, Voice of Torment, End of the Nāgas, Staff Water, Blue Staff, Body Giver, Red Body, Vajra Staff, Cloud, Great Cloud, Black One, Black Heap, Various Diseases, Hurler of All, Bowing One, Great Bowing One, Wretched One, Greatly Wretched One, Ender of Time, Black Yakṣa, Fierce One, Fierce Form, Raised Trident, Great Arrow, Club Destroyer, Hero Who Gathers the Eaters, Sun at the End of Time, Life-Stealer, Sound Destroyer, Holding No Anger, Coiled One, Uncoiled One, Infinite Coil, Blood Coil, Arm, Great Arm, Great Virulent Disease, Fire Glory, Victor over All Leprosy, Fleeing One, One Who Puts to Flight, Likewise Putting to Flight, Eater, and Insatiable Seeker.

These, and also great wrathful vidyā kings, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of vidyā kings who thoroughly carry out the acts of taming every sentient being without exception, of expelling, destroying, repelling, killing and crushing, of acting as a father and providing food, and the acts of pacifying, of enriching and of fierce rites: with their minds fixed on the Blessed One Śākyamuni and on the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara, they bowed to their own vidyā king, the guardian of the Vajra family, and having received his permission they took their places within their own family, and so placed, they sat down each on their own seat.

Then the female messengers, the vidyā queens offered by the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of niyutas, focusing on the sphere of phenomena itself, whose nature is space, free of elaboration, also gathered in that place, namely: Undergarment Lady, Excellent Undergarment Lady, Chain Lady, Vajra Light, Vajra Tongue, Vajra Brow, Vajra Eye, Vajra Navel, Vajra Frown, Vajra Ear, Vajra Drawing, Vajra Needle, Vajra Fist, Vajra Hook, Vajra Sword, Vajra Hammer, Vajra Fetter, Lady with the Sāla Tree, Sālabirṭī, Supreme Maker, Lady of Desire, Vajra Lady of Desire, Vajra of Desire, Seeing Lady, Lady of Sight, Great Sight, Robe of the Peak, Cave Taker, Lady of the Cave, Cave Dweller, Door Dweller, Desire Vajra Lady, Swift as Thought, Invincible Swift One, Rapid Swift One, Lady of Fair Eyes, Tavern Dweller, Bee Lady, Bee-Born Lady, Lady of the Accomplished Sacrifice, Wind Lady, Full-Robed Lady, Lady of Fair Terror, Hiṇḍanī, Threatening Finger, Female Messenger, Excellent Female Messenger, Māmakī, Left-Hand Lady, Lady of Form, Jayā, Vijayā, Aparājitā, Lady of Virtue and Goodness, Smiling Lady, Smiling Vajra Lady, Lady of the World, Famous, Lady of the Vajra, Untamed Lady, Subjugator of the Three Worlds, Staff Lady, Great Staff Lady, Lady of Sweet Speech, Lady of Excellent Fortune, Lady of Meaning, Lady of Great Meaning, Burner from Above, White Lady, Well-Emanated Lady, Utterly Stainless Lady, Bell Lady, Sword Lady, Lady of the Raised Trident, Morsel Lady, Bringer of Victory, Robed Lady, Lady Who Bows, Lady with a Name, Secret Lady, Staff Drawer, Pestle Lady, and Subjugator of All Female Messengers. These, and also other great female messengers, surrounded by hosts of many female messengers, gathered in that very great maṇḍala of the retinue.

There were also many mind-born dhāraṇī goddesses, who fully cultivate the counterparts of samādhi and who subdue harmful beings and cut them off with punishment, namely: the Dhāraṇī of Vajra Fire That Utterly Bewilders, the Dhāraṇī of the Tiered Mansion on the Summit of Meru, the Dhāraṇī of the Tiered Mansion on the Jewel Summit, Earth Holder, Well Tiered, the Dhāraṇī of Punishment, the Dhāraṇī of Subduing, the Dhāraṇī of Summoning, Armlet Lady, Lady with Armlets, Armlet of the Banner Peak, Armlet of the Jewel Peak, Armlet of the World Peak, Armlet of the Gadan Peak, Threefold Coil, World Coil, Thousandfold Coil, Coil of the Son of the Sun, Coil of All Bhūtas, Lady with a Crest, Lady with Jewels, Lady with a Crown of Precious Gems, Lady Endowed with the Power of the Limbs of Awakening, Infinite Crest, Universal Crest, Jewel Crest, Renowned Crest, Crest of All Bhūtas, Invincible Lady, Lady of Utterly Stainless Robes, Six-Faced Lady, Stainless Lady, and World-Renowned Lady. These, and others besides, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of dhāraṇī goddesses, gathered in that very great maṇḍala of the retinue.

Blessed by the infinite buddhas and blessed by the samādhi of the bodhisattvas, there were the pratyekabuddhas, who in other buddha-fields, when those fields are bereft of buddhas, act for the benefit of sentient beings: those blessed ones who are like the rhinoceros, and those who live in groups. Without speaking at all, they teach the way of the Dharma correctly simply by their abiding. Following saṃsāra, they are constantly weary of it. Their mental continua are thoroughly imbued with the habitual tendencies of a mind that has given up great compassion and remains unmixed. Although they once generated the mind set on awakening, with minds so imbued they do not turn their thoughts to the first ground, the second ground, the third ground, or any ground up to the eighth ground of a bodhisattva. Weary of saṃsāra, afraid and filled with fear, they too gathered in that great maṇḍala of the retinue. They were Taker of Fragrance, Universal Sense Base, Universal Light, Candana, Time, Rim, Near Rim, Omen of Death, Near Omen of Death, Excellent Side, Great Drum, Near Great Drum, World Renown, World Light, Bringer of Victory, Dustless, Near Dust, Portion, Near Portion, Sign, Excellent Sign, Maker of Day, Radiant Doer of Good, Maker of Light, Maker of the World, Widely Heard, Well Heard, Beautiful, End of Good Holding, Tamed Beauty, Infinite End, End of Existence, White Crest, Crest of Signs, Crest, Near Crest, Victor, Lotus Supreme, Lotus Source, Self-Arisen, Born, Pleasing, Mind-Born, Mahendra, Renowned as Tiered, Vase, Eye of All, Maker of Bliss, Benefactor, Peaceful, Peaceful Mind, Dharma, Near Dharma, Illuminator, Flower, Well Blue, Glorious, Who Keeps Far from Kin, Hard to Bear, Gold, Stainless Crest, Moon, Near Moon, Excellent Host, Well Purified, Śakra, Desire, Upendra, and Wealth God. These, and others besides, inconceivable and immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of pratyekabuddhas, who have entered and abide definitively in the middle vehicle, in the sphere of phenomena that is wishless, whose nature is space, free of elaboration and uncompounded, free of attachment and of anger, sat together with the Blessed One Śākyamuni where he was seated.

There was also the Saṅgha of śrāvakas, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of śrāvakas, namely: Mahākāśyapa, Nadīkāśyapa, Gayākāśyapa, Uruvilvākāśyapa, Piṇḍola Bharadvāja, Bharadvāja, Maudgalyāyana, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Śāriputra, Mahāśāriputra, Various Beauty, Subhūti, Mahāsubhūti, Gavāṃpati, Kātyāyana, Mahākātyāyana, Upāli, Bhadrika, Kapphiṇa, Nanda, Sundarananda, Upananda, Koṭikarṇa, Arising of the World, Infinite Arising, Pleasing, Near Pleasing, Joyful, Near Joyful, Aniruddha, Full at the Root, Near Full, Victor, Ailing Tooth, Ruru, Son of the Fierce One, Son of Ruru, Kuru, Playing with Five, Near Playing with Five, Time, Equal Time, Holder of the Gods, Rāhula, Green, Near Green, Object of Thought, Thinker of Joy, Udāyin, Near Udāyin, Glorious, Son of Kadru, Son of the Mallas, Near Possessions, Fragment, Victorious, Near Victorious, Great Victorious, Universal Victorious, Caller, Giver of Fame, Yaśas, Wealthy, Ocean of Wealth, Near Wealthy, Pippalaka son of Pilinda, Fruit, Near Fruit, Infinite Fruit, With Fruit, Kumāra, Kumārakāśyapa, Great Giver, Delighter of the Sixteen Groups, Near Delighter, Crooked Swayer, Noose of the Victor, Great Consoler, Vātsīputra, Kurukulle, Śroṇa Koṭikarṇa, Ender of Blood Beyond, Son of the Gaṅgā, Mountain-Eared, Near Mane, Rain Dweller, Light, Beautiful Light, Śrīgupta, Lokagupta, Uttaragupta, Delighting in Light, Pacifier, Child, Near Child, Twenty Koṭis, Anāthapiṇḍada, Near Entry, Turning Back, Maddener, Universal Light, Excellent Lake, Good, Fully Awake, Svāgata, Near Come, Near Going, Going in the World, Ender of Suffering, Excellent Eon, Great Bhadrika, Acting for the Aim, Great Father, Possessed of Going, Rāṣṭrapāla, Victor, Clear, Near Clear, Great Medicine, Great Splendor, Border of the Gods, Accomplisher, Having a Following, Excellent Brahmā, Excellent Beauty, Excellent World, Equal, and Perfectly Measured.

These, and others besides, who taste the flavor of liberation in the infinite sphere of phenomena; who are absorbed in the three vehicles; who have fully attained the path of the lesser vehicle; who have fled from saṃsāra; who have meditated on the concentrations of the three paths of liberation; who are absorbed in the conduct of the four abodes of Brahmā; well composed, well and fully ordained, firmly established in the excellent way, absorbed in the sphere of nirvāṇa, in equality free of elaboration, the intelligent ones: in that great maṇḍala of the retinue endowed with all of them, together with the Blessed One Śākyamuni, who abides without interruption up to the tenth ground as the abode of the Three Jewels, they too took their seats there.

Many great female śrāvakas also came, who have entered through being fully absorbed in the sphere of nirvāṇa; pure in their focus on the vehicle of the uncompounded path, free of desire, having fully attained universal illumination, holding and purifying the qualities of a field worthy of offerings, overpowering every maṇḍala of Māra; supreme ladies of the world, worshipped by the gods, fields of merit, supreme ladies among all sentient beings, the two-footed, the four-footed, the many-footed and the footless, namely: Yaśodharā, Yaśodattā, Mahāprajāpatī, Prajāpatī Sujātā, Nandā, Sthūlanandā, Sundarīnandā, Thinking Lady, Sundarī, Infinite Lady, Manorathā, Victorious Lady, Vīrā, Near Vīrā, Goddess, Excellent Goddess, Excellent Glory, Glory Lady, Lady of Excellent Conduct, Lady of Great Joy, Lady of Sweet Speech, Rohiṇī, Dhṛtarāṣṭrī, Guardian Lady, Noble Lady, Perfect Lady, Embodied Lady, Lotus Lady, Delighted Lady, Matted-Hair Lady, Near Matted-Hair Lady, All Matted-Hair Lady, Lady of Origination, Lady of Light, Swift as Thought, Lady with Hair, Taker of Viṣṇu, Lady with Viṣṇu, Good-Minded Lady, Many-Minded Lady, Lady Glorious, Lady at the End of Suffering, Giver of Karma, Lady of the Fruits of Karma, Vijayā, Victorious Lady, Mistress of Wealth, Giver of Wealth, Dharmadinnā, Sudattā, Great Eater, Āmrā, Entering Fame, Lady of Mind, Broadly Smiling Lady, Ender of the Three Existences, Ender of the Three Circles, Suffering Lady, Lady of Renunciation, Three Leaves, Lotus Leaf, Lady with a Lotus, Lotus Light Lady, Lady Who Walks Averting Hardship, Lady Possessed of Walking That Averts Hardship, Three Petals, Seven Petals, and Utpalavarṇā. These, and also other great elder nuns and great female śrāvakas, drew near in order to bow at the feet of the Blessed One.

Those very maṇḍalas of the retinue, wishing to see the power of the magical display of the great bodhisattva, assembled and took their seats, in order to hear the Dharma, and they wished to strive to accomplish the aims of the conduct of mantra. Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni looked upon the Blessed One's maṇḍala of the retinue. Knowing their higher intention, and knowing that the nature of insubstantiality, whose essence is space, utterly transcends the three realms of sentient beings, he spoke to the great being:

"Great being, reflect carefully on the conduct that serves the aims of sentient beings. Meditate on the bodhisattva samādhi called Overpowering All the Powers of Māra with the Power of All the Ten Powers of the Tathāgata, which, in accordance with one's intention, brings faith in the result of the desired action, and brings about the attainment of the Dharma words called Perfectly Attaining the Aim of Mantra Conduct, the words of peace, the words of liberation, the accomplishment of the ritual, and the sameness of conceptual thought."

Then, the instant the Blessed One had spoken, the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara entered absorption. The instant Avalokiteśvara entered absorption, this great trichiliocosm, this world system, shook violently, and was lit up by a great light. He displayed the power of his own miraculous abilities that he brought forth, and he also spoke the words of his own mantra. As for the mantras of the ritual, among its many mantras, the common one, which arises without departing from the proper sequence, is this:

namaḥsamantabuddhānāṃ abhāba svabhāba samuṅgatānāṃ namaḥ pratyekabuddhā āryaśrābakānāṃ namo bodhisatvānāṃ daśabhumipratiṣṭhite śaraṇaṃ bodhisatvānāṃ mahāsatvanāṃ mahāsatvānāṃ tadyathā oṃ khakha khāhi duṣṭasatvādamaka asi musala paraśu pāśa hasti caturmukha ṣaṭcaraṇa gacchagaccha mahābighnāna bighnānataka bikṛtānan sarbabhūta bheyaṃkara aṭṭāṭṭa hāsanādine byāghracarmanibāsana kurukuru sarbakarmaṇāṃ cchindacchinda bhindabhinda saramudraṃ ākarṣaākarṣa bhūtāna nirmathana sarbaduṣṭāṃ prabeśaya maṇḍalmadhye baibasvatajībitānatā karakurukuru mamakyāryāṃ dahadaha pacapaca mābilambasamayamanusmara hūṃhūṃphaṭ sphoṭayasphoṭaya sarbaāśāparipūraka hehe bhagabāna kañcirāyasi mama sarbaarthasāṅṅayasvāhā

This is the great wrathful one of the Blessed Lady, Noble Tārā, called Tārā's Subjugator. It summons and obtains whatever one desires. Since it summons and vanquishes even Indra and the king of Yama, what need is there to speak of ordinary sentient beings?

The instant the great king of wrathful ones had spoken it, all sentient beings became distressed, terrified and afraid, dejected and heartbroken. Since, apart from the buddhas, the blessed ones, and the great bodhisattvas, they had no other refuge, no other protector, and no other ally, they drew near to the Blessed One.

Then whatever beings are counted as sentient beings, those that move on the ground and those that move in the sky, the stationary and the moving, the womb-born, the egg-born, the born from heat and moisture, and the miraculously born, dwelling in the infinite and boundless world systems, above, below and on the level, in the directions and beyond the directions, even those hidden at that instant, at that moment, were all summoned here in an instant by the great king of wrathful ones.

This king of wrathful ones, once accomplished, should not be recited in the presence of those who are not free of desire. Why is that? Because they would die or wither away. Having consecrated its words, one should recite it before an image of the Buddha, or before a stūpa containing relics, or before a volume of the sublime Dharma, or before Avalokiteśvara. It should not be read for the sake of other rites, nor in just any place whatever. Why? Because that would bring great ill omens, great sorrow, and one's own destruction.

The buddhas, the blessed ones, and the bodhisattva great beings alone, endowed with supreme compassion, accomplishing and following the conduct of omniscient wisdom, bring all sentient beings under their sway, firmly establish the way of the Dharma, and lead the entire realm of sentient beings to attain nirvāṇa. With a mind in harmony with the might of great compassion, they have spoken of teaching where there is no teaching, of properly setting beings on the three paths, of keeping the lineage of the Three Jewels unbroken, of illuminating mantra conduct, of overpowering the strength of Māra, of destroying great obstructors, of repelling wicked kings, of increasing one's own power and turning back the power of others, of paralysis, of felling, of restoring what has declined, of drying up, of delight, of illuminating one's own mantra conduct, of long life and freedom from illness, of increasing one's own sovereignty, of swiftly accomplishing rites, of great loving-kindness, great compassion, great joy and great equanimity, and of perfect restraint, together with the reasons for these; and they spoke with a mind free in every respect of speculation and conjecture about causes.

Then there were nāgas and great nāgas, yakṣas and great yakṣas, rākṣasas and great rākṣasas, piśācas and great piśācas, pūtanas and great pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas and great kaṭapūtanas, mātṛkās and great mātṛkās, kumbhāṇḍas and great kumbhāṇḍas, beasts of prey and great beasts of prey, vetālas and great vetālas, kampojas and great kampojas, sisters and great sisters, ḍākinīs and great ḍākinīs, suckers and great suckers, oppressors and great oppressors, child-spirits and great child-spirits, brampas and great brampas, diseases and great diseases, apasmāras and great apasmāras, grahas and great grahas, sky mātṛkās and great sky mātṛkās, embodied ones and great embodied ones, misshapen ones and great misshapen ones, wailers and great wailers, shadow-oppressors and great shadow-oppressors, vomit-bringers and great vomit-bringers, kiṃkaras and great kiṃkaras, yakṣiṇīs and great yakṣiṇīs, piśācīs and great piśācīs, epidemic fevers and great epidemic fevers, one-day fevers and great one-day fevers, constant fevers, terrible fevers, fevers arising from what is constant, momentary fevers, those arising from wind, those arising from bile, those arising from phlegm, those arising from their combination, chronic diseases and great chronic diseases, siddhas and great siddhas, yogins and great yogins, sages and great sages, kinnaras and great kinnaras, mahoragas and great mahoragas, gandharvas and great gandharvas, asuras and great asuras, humans and great humans, lands and great lands, oceans and great oceans, rivers and great rivers, mountains and great mountains, treasures and great treasures, earths and great earths, trees and great trees, birds and great birds, kings and great kings; Śakra, the great Indra, the son of Vasu, the Thunderer, the Lord of Bhūtas, Īśāna, Yama, Brahmā and Mahābrahmā, the son of the Sun, Dhanada, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa, Kubera, Pūrṇabhadra, Maṇibhadra, Pañcika, Jambhala, the Paralysis-Holder, the Kuṣma-Holder, the Green One, Harikeśa, Siṃha, Hārītī, the Joy-Maker, the Wealth-Maker, Varuṇa the lord of waters, the Lord of the World, Upendra, guhyakas and great guhyakas, the Moving One and the Mover, the Upper Waters, the Everlasting Mountain, the Snowy Mountain, the Great Mountain, the Stacked-Eyed, and the Three-Headed. These, and furthermore great yakṣa generals surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of yakṣas, through the blessing of the bodhisattva and the power of the miraculous abilities he brought forth, assembled and took their seats in that very great maṇḍala of the retinue in order to hear the Dharma.

The great kings of the rākṣasas, each surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of rākṣasas, who had been summoned by the great king of wrathful ones, namely the Fugitive, the Putter to Flight, the Digester, Śaṅkukarṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, All-Ears, Yama, Vibhīṣaṇa, the Terrible, Raudra, the Very Fierce, the Unbearable, the Sinful, Indrajit, the Fighter, the Fine Fighter, the Spear, the Trident, the Three-Headed, and the Endless-Headed, they too assembled in order to hear the Dharma.

The piśācas and great piśācas, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of great piśācas, namely the Drink-Cutter, the Lesser Drink-Cutter, the Fine Drink-Cutter, the Endless Drink-Cutter, Manoratha, the Fine Manoratha, the Fine Guide, the Eater, Fine-Haired, and the Fierce-Formed, they too assembled in order to hear the Dharma.

The nāga kings, each surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of nāgas, who had been summoned by the king of wrathful ones through the power of the miraculous abilities brought forth by the bodhisattva, namely Nanda, Upananda, Candra, Upacandra, the son of Vāsuki, Ananta, Takṣaka, Padma, Mahāpadma, Śaṅkhapāla, Śaṅkha, Śaṅkhapālī, the Moving Power, Kulika, the False Drink, the Vase-Giver, the Vajra-Bearer, the son of Campā, the nāga Manasvin, the Crusher of Pride, Ḍaṃkura, Upaḍaṃkura, Lakuṭā, Great Lakuṭā, the White One, the Good White One, the Blue One, the Blue Rain-Giver, Milk Water, the Chaffless, Sāgara and Upasāgara, these and furthermore other great nāga kings surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of nāgas assembled and took their seats in that great maṇḍala of the retinue in order to hear the Dharma.

The sages and great sages, namely the son of the Stream-Knower, Vasiṣṭha, Gautama, Bhagīratha, Jahnu, Aṅgiras, Amasti, Sulasti, the Mountain Mouse, Vyāsa, Kṛṣṇa, Gautama Kṛṣṇa, Agni, the lineage of Agni, Traṃḥgiras, Jāmadagni, Āstika, the Sage, the Supreme Sage, Vaiśambāyana, the Side-Born, Paraśu, Yogeśvara, Pippala, Pippalāda, Vālmīki, and Māra's Arrow, these and furthermore other great sages surrounded by many hundreds of thousands, approached that great maṇḍala of the retinue, bowed to the Blessed One Śākyamuni, and took their seats, wishing to hear the meaning of the conduct of secret mantra and the bodhisattva Piṭaka and to rejoice in it.

The great kings of the mahoragas too entered that great maṇḍala of the retinue and took their seats, namely Bheraṇḍa, Bhuruṇḍa, Maruṇḍa, Light Ray, and Blazing Light Ray.

The kings of the garuḍas too, each surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of garuḍas, assembled in that maṇḍala of the retinue, namely Suparṇa, White Wing, Nāga, Wing-Goer, Suparṇa-Born, Swift as Thought, Destroyer of Nāgas, the son of Vinatā, Bharadhvaja, Auspicious Mark, Great Auspicious Mark, and the King of Birds. They too assembled in that great maṇḍala of the retinue.

The kings of the kinnaras, each surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of kinnaras, namely Druma, Upadruma, Sudruma, Anantadruma, Lokadruma, Clear Druma, Broad-Chested, Great Broad-Chested, Splendor of Mind, Great Splendor, Great Miracle, the Proclaimer, Sweet Voice, the Delightful, the Mind-Rouser, the Maddener, Danadhāta, Equanimity, Compassion, and the Pitiless, these and furthermore other kinnara kings surrounded by thousands assembled in order to hear the Dharma.

Likewise Brahmā, lord of the Sahā world, and Mahābrahmā; the gods of Ābhāsvara, of Prabhāsvara, of the Light of Joy, of the Light of Merit, of Avṛha, of Atapa, of Akaniṣṭha, of the Fine Below, of the World's End, of the Sphere of Nothingness, of Not Nothingness, of Infinite Space, of Not Infinite Space, of Sudṛśa, of Sudarśana, of Fine Emanation, of Total Emanation, of the Pure Abodes, of Tuṣita, of Yāma, of the Thirty-Three, and of the realm of the Four Great Kings; the Ever-Intoxicated, the Garland-Bearers, the Bowl-Bearers, those of the Three Lutes, those who dwell on mountains, those who dwell in towered mansions, those who dwell on peaks, those who dwell in Alakāvatī, those who dwell in towns, those who dwell in celestial palaces, those who dwell within, those who travel in the sky, those who dwell on the earth, those who dwell in trees, and those who dwell in houses; and likewise the lords of the asuras, the Well-Sated, Bali, Vemacitrin, Fine Variegated, Virtuous Variegated, Rāhu, Hand, and the others, surrounded by many thousands of koṭis of asuras, the asuras of many kinds of gait and many kinds of wealth who wage war with the gods: through the blessing of the Buddha, and wishing to see the magical display of the bodhisattva, to pay homage and to honor him, they too assembled in that maṇḍala of the retinue.

The planets and great planets that move in the sky for the sake of the world, namely the Sun, Candra, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn, Rāhu, Earthquake, the Comet, the Lightning-Striker, the Star, the Banner, Raudra, the Smoky One, Smoke, Vajra, the Sage, Rain, Lesser Rain, Loss of Aims, Certain Loss, the Limit of Laughter, Māṣṭi, Riṣṭi, the Joyful One, the World's End, Exhaustion, the Feller, the Unfallen, the Crest, the Hump, the End of Time, the Charnel Ground, Biśīta, Raudra, the White One, Abhijit, the son of Abhijit, Maitra, Jupiter, the Third Jupiter, Lubha, Rotra, the Steadfast, the Diminisher, the Mighty, Raudra, Dawn, the Great Laughter, No Omen of Death, the Drier, Sena, Upasena, Kumāra, the Player, the Laugher, the Thinker, the Lame One, and the Ugly One, these great planets too, with retinues of many hundreds of thousands, through the blessing of the Buddha assembled as the retinue in that Pure Abode and took their seats.

Then the kings of the lunar mansions, which go through the sky and follow their course, each surrounded by many hundreds of thousands, namely Aśvinī, Bharaṇī, Kṛttikā, Rohiṇī, Mṛgaśiras, Ārdrā, Punarvasu, Puṣya, Āśleṣā, Maghā, Pūrvaphalgunī, Uttaraphalgunī, Hasta, Citrā, Svāti, Viśākhā, Anurādhā, Jyeṣṭhā, Mūla, Pūrvāṣāḍhā, Uttarāṣāḍhā, Śravaṇa, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣaj, Pūrvabhādrapadā, Uttarabhādrapadā, Revatī, the Goddess, Abhijit, the Returning One, Starlight, Adgirasā, She of the Lunar Mansions, Upasdugu, the Lesser Phalgunī, Supreme in the World, She of the Supreme, the Glorious One, Protector of the World, She of the Liquor, Victory-Gainer, the Wealthy One, and Wealth of the Gods: these kings of the lunar mansions, each surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of lunar mansions, through the blessing of the Buddha assembled and took their seats in that great maṇḍala of the retinue in the abode of the Pure Abodes.

As for the thirty-six houses, namely the Ram, the Bull, the Pair, the Crab, the Lion, the Maiden, the Balance, the Scorpion, the Bow, the Makara, the Vase, the Fish, the Monkey, the Lesser Vase, the Golden Vase, the Sword, the Elephant, the Buffalo, the God, the Human, the Auspicious Mark, the Gandharva, the World's Intent, the Supreme Victor, Splendor, Space, Shadow, Earth, Darkness, Dust, Lesser Dust, Suffering, Happiness, the Awakening of Liberation, Self-Awakening, the Śrāvaka, the Vidyādhara of Hell, Great Splendor, Endowed with Great Splendor, the Animal, the Preta, the Asura, the Piśāca, the Piśācī, the Yakṣa, the Rākṣasa, All Bhūtas, the Elephant of the Directions, the Upward-Goer, the All-Goer, the Divider, the Yoga-Goer, the Well-Established, the Supreme, the Middling, and the Lowest: these, and the great houses, each surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of houses, approached the place where the great maṇḍala of the retinue was assembled, bowed at the feet of the Blessed One, and took their seats, each in his own place.

The great yakṣiṇīs, each surrounded by hundreds of thousands of koṭis of yakṣiṇīs, namely Fine-Eyed, Fine-Browed, Fine-Haired, Sweet-Voiced, Good Intelligence, Wealthy, Bright-Eyed, Wish-Fulfiller, the Secret One, Petticoat, Fine Petticoat, Lotus Time, the Fearless, Giver of Fearlessness, Jayā, Vijayā, She of Revatī, Keśinī, Hair's End, the Windy One, Mind-Stealer, the Spirited, Flowered, Dweller in the Flower City, the Tawny One, Hārītī, She of the Heroines, the Heroine, the Good Heroine, Fine-Nosed, Prabhāvatī, Divine Beauty, Fine Taste, Supreme Secret, Abiding in Speech, the Sorrowless, Beautiful to Behold, Prabhāvatī, the Excellent, the Shapely, Beautiful Form, Not White, the Peaceful, the Subtle, Senā, the Joy-Maker, the Lesser Joy-Maker, and Beyond the World: these great yakṣiṇīs, each surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of yakṣiṇīs, also bowed to the Blessed One Śākyamuni in that great maṇḍala of the retinue and took their seats.

The piśācīs, each surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of piśācīs, also bowed to the Blessed One Śākyamuni and assembled, namely the Ornamented, the Broom Piśācī, the Fierce Piśācī, the Piśācī of Talala, the Blazing Piśācī, the Ash-Eater, the Flesh-Eater, the Hard to Hold, the Deluder, the Bewilderer, the Proclaimer, the Generator, She Who Dwells at the World's End, She of the Ash's End, She of the Drink-Cutter, the Many, the Hard to Tame, Elā, the Marked One, She of the Smoke's End, the Smoky One, and Fine Smoke: these great piśācīs, each surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of piśācīs, also entered that great maṇḍala of the assembled retinue.

The mātṛkās and great mātṛkās, who range through the world, harm sentient beings, and gather up tormas and garlands, namely Brahmāṇī, Maheśvarī, Vaiṣṇavī, Kaumārī, Cāmuṇḍā, Vārāhī, Aindrī, Yāmī, Āgneyī, the Daughter of the Sun, She of the Intermediate World, Vāruṇī, Īśānī, Vāyavī, the Stealer of Others' Lives, She of the Ornamented Face, She of the Auspicious Mark, the Great She of the Auspicious Mark, Pūtanā, Kaṭapūtanā, and the Drier: these great mātṛkās, each surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of mātṛkās, took their seats in that great maṇḍala of the assembled retinue, uttering the words, "Homage to the Buddha!"

Likewise many hundreds of thousands of humans and nonhumans, and all beings, sentient and not sentient, in the whole expanse from the great hell Avīci up to the Peak of Existence, appeared clearly in the midst of the sky. Not a single living creature in the multitude of sentient beings was harmed. Through the blessing of the Buddha and the ornament of the bodhisattva's miraculous power, all sentient beings saw clearly the Buddha, the Blessed One, and Avalokiteśvara seated upon the crown of their heads.

Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni looked upon the entire retinue with his buddha eye and said to that great being, "If you know that the time has now come for the bodhisattva Piṭaka, the vast chapter on the samādhi that ascertains for sentient beings the meaning of the conduct of secret mantra, then speak it."

Then the bodhisattva great being Avalokiteśvara, with the permission of the Blessed One Śākyamuni, entered the samādhi called the Beautiful and Firm Vajra Stream Arrayed with the Ornaments of the Nature of Space. The instant the great being entered absorption, that entire great maṇḍala of the retinue came to rest, vast, with the nature of vajra, extending for many hundreds of thousands of leagues. There the yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, wind gods and piśācas, in short the entire realm of sentient beings, through the blessing of the bodhisattva, were firmly established in that celestial palace as in a vajra jewel. Those who had taken their seats did not harm one another at all.

Then that great being, knowing that the great retinue had assembled, called upon the king of wrathful ones, Tārā's Subjugator.

"O great wrathful one! Protect all the sentient beings of this great maṇḍala of the retinue, assembled here where all the buddhas and bodhisattvas have gathered! Bring them under your power! Tame the wicked! Awaken the peaceful! Make the faithless faithful! For as long as there is one who holds the vidyā-mantras, and who holds the maṇḍala rite of the conduct of secret mantra, the vidyā-mantras of this very vast bodhisattva Piṭaka that accomplishes the conduct of vidyā-mantra and secret mantra, for that long go outside these and protect them!"

When he had said this, the great king of wrathful ones accepted the command. He took on a form of great transformation, and, for the sake of protecting all sentient beings and for the sake of making them steadfast, the king of wrathful ones, Tārā's Subjugator, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of wrathful ones, took up his station in the great maṇḍala of the retinue with its great array, on all four sides, and likewise above, below and across, uttering a fierce roar.

Then those sentient beings, possessed of a peaceful mind, did not transgress the command to enter properly, and they also heard a sound such as this: "Whoever transgresses this pledge, his head will split into a hundred pieces like the blossom of the arjaka. That too is the blessing of the bodhisattva."

Then that bodhisattva again spoke words of Dharma for the sake of his own vidyā-mantra and the conduct of secret mantra:

"Through one quality the secret mantra of a bodhisattva great being is accomplished. What is that one? It is this: not seeing any phenomenon at all, in a manner free of conceptual elaboration.

"If one is firmly established in two qualities, the secret mantra of a bodhisattva great being will be accomplished. What are the two? Never giving up the awakening mind, and equality toward all sentient beings.

"Through three qualities the aim of the conduct of one's own secret mantra becomes definitely stable and complete. What are the three? Never abandoning sentient beings, guarding the bodhisattva's vow of moral discipline, and never abandoning one's own secret mantra.

"If one is endowed with four qualities, the vidyā-mantra of a bodhisattva who has just generated the mind for the first time will be accomplished. What are the four? Never abandoning the completion of one's own secret mantra, never cutting off the secret mantras of others, abiding with a mind of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings, and a mind that cultivates great compassion. A bodhisattva endowed with these four qualities will accomplish secret mantra.

"Through five qualities one properly enters the bodhisattva Piṭaka and the practice of the conduct of secret mantra becomes complete. What are the five? Resorting to places of many kinds, resorting to remote hermitages, being without hatred toward other sentient beings, not looking to worldly mantras, and abiding in moral discipline, learning and good conduct. Through these five qualities the accomplishment of the aim of mantra conduct becomes complete.

"Six qualities make complete the accomplishment of the conduct of secret mantra. What are the six? Faith in the Three Jewels that is never cut off; not casting aside the meaning of the words of the profound sūtras of the Great Vehicle; and, with a tireless mind, thoroughly seeking the meaning of the conduct of secret mantra and never abandoning the side of virtue. These six qualities bring about full and proper engagement in the conduct of vidyā-mantra and the accomplishment of secret mantra.

"Seven qualities cause one to follow the rite of accomplishing vidyā-mantras and the conduct of secret mantra. What are the seven? Meditating on the profound way of the perfection of wisdom, reciting it, listening to it, chanting it, and inquiring into it, and, out of devotion to the bodhisattva conduct, teaching it at the three times of day; taking up, unhindered, strict restraint, mantra recitation, fire offerings, silence and austerities, as well as intelligence, mindfulness, wisdom and steadfastness; the manner of properly entering the bodhisattva assembly and the way of the profound Dharma of the Great Vehicle, and skill in one's own secret mantra and in the tasks of summoning with mantra, protection and accomplishment; the act of fully cultivating great compassion, great loving-kindness, great equanimity and great joy; the act of properly entering the suchness, free of elaboration, of the realm of sentient beings and the sphere of phenomena, and of seeking the nondual wisdom of omniscience; and the act of never abandoning any sentient being and taking no delight in the Lesser Vehicle. These seven qualities make complete the accomplishment of vidyā-mantra and secret mantra.

"Eight qualities bring about proper entry into accomplishment by way of the aim of the conduct of vidyā-mantra and secret mantra. What are the eight? Wishing to marvel, with faith, at results seen and unseen; the act of being without doubt concerning the miracles and magical displays that are the fruit of a bodhisattva's faith; the act of holding secret mantra without error, and the act of reverence for the guru; the act of holding as undeceiving the mantras, causes and conduct that the buddhas and bodhisattvas have taught as one's own, and of giving away all one possesses; skill in teaching, through what is seen in dreams, which fields are places of accomplishment and which are not; the act of freeing oneself of all stinginess, sleep and torpor, always taking up diligence and offering oneself to all the buddhas and bodhisattvas; in short, the act of putting on the armor of insatiability for the roots of virtue and thoroughly dispelling all obstructors; and overpowering the continuum of awakening, wishing for oneself great wealth and renown for great power, keeping company with persons renowned for great power, never being parted from spiritual friends, and keeping company with great bodhisattvas. These eight qualities bring about proper entry into the accomplishment of the aim of the conduct of secret mantra."

"Friends, in short, one who is never parted from the awakening mind, who has special and supreme devotion to the Three Jewels, and who, with a mind that does not grow weary even toward those whose moral discipline is broken, always strives earnestly, will accomplish the mind-mantras of the Extensive Chapters, limitless and marvelous, born of the mind and concordant in cause with the conduct of bodhisattvas. They are not to be understood otherwise. With a mind that has become free of conceptual thought, they should also be practiced as a cause for the awakening of experience."

Then again the buddhas, bodhisattvas, pratyekabuddhas, and noble śrāvakas who empower the complete assembly gathered from everywhere spoke these words: "O Son of the Victors, for the sake of all sentient beings, teach the Dharma that accords with entering the Dharma way of accomplishing the aims of the various conducts of secret mantra! Excellent, excellent! How wonderful! The great bodhisattvas have well proclaimed the virtuous conduct of secret mantra, which follows the teaching of the various Dharmas. Whatever great kings hold this Chapter of the Assembly, keep it in mind, set it first upon an elephant even in battle, and worship it with flowers, incense, scents, and unguents of various kinds, we shall regard as equal to ourselves. We shall bring their adversaries and enemies under control. We shall destroy and turn back the armies of their foes. And for the son of good family or daughter of good family, the great king or great queen, the monk or nun, the layman or laywoman who writes it in a book and keeps it in their home, we shall bring about great protection and great wealth, long life, freedom from illness, and wealth that ever increases."

When they had said this, that whole assembly fell silent.

This concludes the first chapter, the Chapter of the Assembly, from the Root Ritual Manual of the Blessed Lady, Noble Tārā, from the Extensive Chapters on the Magical Display of the Great Bodhisattva, the Great Ritual Manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā (the One with Upswept Locks), from the Definitive Teaching of the Vidyā-Mantras and Secret Mantra Conduct of the Great Vehicle.

Then again the bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, gazing upon the maṇḍala of the whole assembly gathered from everywhere, entered into the samādhi called Following the Pledges of All Sentient Beings and Seeing Everywhere. As soon as the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara had entered into it, from the region of the navel circle he sent forth a ray of light surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of light rays. It illuminated all the realms of sentient beings, and then, having fully illuminated the great maṇḍala of the assembly already gathered there, it remained.

Then again the bodhisattva mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi said to the pure being Avalokiteśvara, "Speak, speak of the practice that accomplishes the conduct of the Extensive Chapters of the maṇḍala of rites that follows the pledge of the great being, which is common to all sentient beings: the gathering into which beings properly enter and so come properly to attain the accomplishments of worldly and transworldly vidyā-mantras and secret mantras!"

When the Lord of Secrets, the lord of yakṣas, had spoken thus, the bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara spoke the tantra of the supremely secret maṇḍala. He displayed the miracle called Fully Urging All Vidyā-Mantras: raising his right hand, he pointed with the tip of his finger at the maṇḍala of the assembly, and from that fingertip he sent forth many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of vidyā kings. Having sent them forth, he illuminated that maṇḍala of the whole assembly with a great light, and remained.

Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, by the mantra of his own tantra, bestowed the heart mantra of the king of wrathful ones, Tārā's Subjugator, which performs all rites, the single hero: for inviting and dismissing, for pacifying, for increasing, for fierce rites, for invisibility, for travel through the sky, for entering beneath the earth, for swiftness of foot, for summoning, for causing enmity, for bringing under control, and for scents, garlands, and lamps, all of these. In short, just as it is applied, so it accomplishes. That which accomplishes in each and every way is the great king of wrathful ones called the Three Syllables, which accomplishes all aims through great diligence. What is it?

oṃ āḥ hūṃ

This is the heart mantra of that great wrathful one which performs all rites. The bodhisattva mahāsattva taught it definitively for all maṇḍalas and all conduct of secret mantra, and it destroys all obstructors.

Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara raised his right hand, placed it on the crown of the wrathful one's head, and spoke these words: "Buddhas, blessed ones, take heed! Whatever bodhisattvas dwell in the world systems of the ten directions, endowed with limitless and boundless great miraculous power, make them abide firmly in the pledge!" Having said this, he whirled that king of wrathful ones around and sent it forth.

As soon as the great king of wrathful ones had been sent forth, it went to all the world systems, and in a single instant it subdued and summoned those beings of great miraculous power who had malicious minds. It brought them properly into the great maṇḍala of the assembly of pure beings, set each of them in their proper place, and then remained upon the crowns of the heads of the malicious beings, swirling with a garland of blazing flames.

Then the bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara once more gazed upon the maṇḍala of the assembly: "All you sentient beings, listen! Whoever transgresses this pledge of mine will be destroyed by the king of wrathful ones. Why is that? Because the pledge of the buddhas, the blessed ones, is not to be transgressed."

I shall explain the vidyā-mantras and the great secret words that are the meaning of secret mantra, just as the bodhisattvas endowed with great miraculous power have definitively taught them in samādhi. Listen to this well and keep it well in mind, and I shall explain.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama āryābalokite śvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagabatyai āryatarāyai bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā ṛjuka dharma niryāte tāre tuttāre śānta dharma niryāte tāre anabhilāpya dharma niryāte tuttāre ture hini drāsani bitrāsani ohani mohani jambhani stambhani prabhe candraprabhe hi hili hili bile bile begagāmini kuṇḍi mahākuṇḍi dhara dhara dhanapati tāre huru huru kuru kuru ahaṃ yāṃ yāṃ cintayāmi cintatiṃ me kuru svāhā

Friends, this is the root vidyā-mantra of my Blessed Lady, Noble Tārā. She performs all rites, she cuts off the phenomena of the three realms of existence, and she turns back all the lower destinies. Here, too, the mudrā is to be applied to that renowned root vidyā-mantra by one who knows it.

Here is the supreme heart mantra. It performs all rites; it brings attainment of the bliss of nirvāṇa; it accomplishes all pacification; it is present just as if one were seeing the Buddha directly. She herself, my friend, the bodhisattva who for the sake of all sentient beings is present in the form of the supremely secret vidyā-mantra, fulfills all wishes. By the mere remembering of it, whatever one remembers, it brings all rites to completion and clears away great terrors. What need is there to speak of reciting it? What is it?

namo ratnatrayāya nama āryābalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tāre tuttāre svāhā

Here the mudrā, renowned as the Utpala, makes all wealth increase.

Here what serves as the near-heart mantra is the supremely glorious great purifier:

namo ratnatrayāya namaḥ sarba buddha bodhisatvānāṃ oṃ kurukulle svāhā

Here the mudrā becomes renowned as Holding the Lotus Garland; it brings all sentient beings under control.

Here what serves as the supreme heart mantra is:

namaḥ sarba buddhāmāṃ oṃ gī

This is the supreme of heart mantras. In short, it expands great qualities for every activity. To describe its qualities to their end would not be possible even in many hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of eons. Here the mudrā, renowned as Great Diligence, fulfills all wishes.

Here what serves as the vidyā-mantra of invitation is:

namaḥ sarba buddhānāṃ oṃ he he bhagabati biśvarūpiṇi sarbabala bhāṣiti prabodhani āyāni bhagabati krīḍ utpaladhini mama śuddhāya tiṣṭha tiṣṭha samayamanusmara apratihata śāsana hūṃ mābilamba kuru kuru phaṭ svāhā

This is the vidyā-mantra for inviting the Blessed Lady, and it is also the one for all the buddhas, all the bodhisattvas, all the pratyekabuddhas, the noble śrāvakas, the gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, piśācas, rākṣasas, and all bhūtas. Having consecrated sandalwood water with it seven times, one should sprinkle it in the four directions, and likewise above, below, and on every side. This is the secret mantra of the buddhas, of all the bodhisattvas, of the Blessed Lady Tārā, and of all worldly and transworldly beings; all the hosts of bhūtas and all sentient beings will come.

namaḥ sarba buddhānāṃ aprahihata śāsanānāṃ oṃ dhuru dhuru dhumabāsini mamārciṣa hūṃ tiṣṭha samayamanusmara svāhā

This is the incense vidyā-mantra. Combine sandalwood, saffron, and camphor, and offer incense. Then the tathāgatas and all the bodhisattvas who have come are delighted by the fragrant incense and are drawn in. Here the mudrā, renowned as the Lotus Garland, summons all sentient beings and is peaceful; for the vidyā-mantra of invitation, too, it is this same excellent Lotus Garland mudrā.

To the buddhas, all the bodhisattvas, and all the sentient beings who have come, one should also offer guest water. Mix camphor, sandalwood, and saffron with water, and blend it with jasmine flowers, fresh mallikā, summer flowers, punnāga, bakula, and fragrant herbs, any of these flowers, or flowers of the season, or sweet-smelling flowers; then offer the guest water with this mantra:

namaḥ sarba buddhānāṃ apratihata śāsanānāṃ tadyathā he he mahākāruṇikā biśvarūpadhāraṇi arghaṃ pratīccha samayamanusmara tiṣṭha tiṣṭha debatādhiṣṭhāna madhye prabeśaya prabeśaya sarbabuddhā anukaṃbaka gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ ambaribicāriṇi svāhā

Here the mudrā is renowned as the Full One; all sentient beings follow it, and it is steadfast.

Here what serves as the scent vidyā-mantra is:

namaḥ sarba budhānāṃ namaḥ smanta gandha apabhāṣite śriye tathāgatāya tadyathā gandhe gandhe hlāde gandha manorame praticchadaṃ gandhaṃ samanānucāriṇi svāhā

Here what serves as the mudrā is called the Leaf, which fulfills all wishes.

Here what serves as the flower mantra is:

namaḥ sarba buddha bodhisatvānāṃ apratihata śāsanānāṃ namaḥ saṃkusumita rajñāsya tathāgatāsya tadyathā kusume kusume kusumādhyo kusumāsūrbāsi kusumābati svāhā

With this same incense mantra one should fumigate with the incense described before.

Having paid homage to all the buddhas,
whose bodies are marvelous, beyond conceiving,
I shall explain the torma vidyā-mantra
spoken by the perfectly complete buddhas:

namaḥ sarba buddha bodhisatvānāṃ apratihata śāsanānāṃ tadyathā he he bhagabati mahāsatve sarbabuddhā abalokite mābilaṃba idam paliṃ gṛhṇa paya grahṇa pa hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ sarba rara phaṭ phaṭ svāhā

With this one should offer the food for the gods; it becomes a torma for all the bhūtas. Here too the mudrā is the Staff, which turns back all malicious beings.

namaḥ sarba buddha bodhisatvānāṃ apratihata śāsanānāṃ sarba tamo ñandhakār bityaṃ sitānā namaḥ smanta jyoti gandha aba bta sa priyāya tathāgatāya tadyathā he he bhagabāna jyote rasmi śata sahasra pratimaṇḍita śarīra bikurba bikurba mahābodhisatvā manta jvolodyota mūrtti khurha khurha abalokīya abalokīya maṇḍala sarba satvānāṃ svāhā

This is the lamp vidyā-mantra; with it one should offer lamps. The mudrā, called the Opened, illuminates all sentient beings.

namaḥ smanta buddhānāṃ apratiheta śāsanānāṃ tadyathā jvala jvala jvālaya jvālaya hūṃ bibodhaka hara kṛṣṇa piṃga svāhā

This becomes the vidyā-mantra that performs the activity of fire. Here too the mudrā

is known in the world as the Joining of the Mouths;
it makes all sentient beings bright with light.
