Finally, having presented torma offerings for three nights according to the rite, and having made protection for himself or for a good companion, he should press it down with both hands and recite until the three kinds of accomplishment occur.

With the first accomplishment, whomever one looks upon, and whoever sees one, they become delighted and come under one's power. With the second, merely by wiping dust from the ground of the painting one becomes invisible; one has the strength of nine thousand elephants, is swift as the wind, seizes six shares, travels at will, brings down rain, illuminates, and becomes greatly powerful. With the third, one becomes like the rising sun, lives ten thousand years, and leads even a universal monarch. One roams about with the vajra in hand; and likewise by the rites of the lotus in hand and the axe in hand.

Then, if he wishes to accomplish pills, having first done the approach, he should take the index finger of a one-year-old. Having made a stūpa by the earlier rite and made vast offerings in the charnel ground, he should sit facing east and, pressing the finger down with the gesture of teaching, recite until rays of light shine from the vajra. By day he should guard it from the wind of the sky, and by night, without sleeping, he should draw in the fingers until dawn. In the place where they have been drawn in, he should keep a fast for three nights. Taking the milk of a cow of good repute whose calf is of the same stock, he should make a sandalwood maṇḍala for the Blessed One, the Buddha, light lamps of ghee, sit on a mat of kuśa grass, and consecrate it eight thousand times with the mantra. He should pour the milk into an earthen vessel and mark out a maṇḍala with ash. At dawn, having bathed, he should take the butter churned beforehand from this very milk, make offerings to the Blessed One, consecrate it eight thousand times, and eat it without touching it. This is called Seeing, and it grants every desire.

If he wishes for release, he should buy at the hero's price all the fragrances and other things beneficial to the place, keep a fast for three nights, make vast offerings to the Blessed One, the Buddha, light lamps of ghee, and himself recite the mantra and examine. Then, making an effigy, he should place it on seven leaves of the aśvattha tree and, in front of the Blessed One, recite for as long as his knowledge mantra lasts. Then he should grind it into powder: whoever is touched by that powder comes under his power. By this same rite, if he makes an effigy from nāgakesara powder and makes eight hundred fire offerings of it in pieces, with incense, whoever he thinks of comes under his power. By this same rite he should perform the fire offering with kindling sticks of apāmārga.

If one wants wealth, one should go to a cattle pen and, in the presence of the Blessed One, the Buddha, make a stūpa, not shaped by hand, out of cow dung that has not fallen to the ground. Having worshipped it according to the rite, one should burn guggulu and recite a hundred thousand times. One will obtain a thousand cattle, or wealth. By this same rite one should burn ghee, honey, and the like and recite a hundred thousand times; one will obtain a domain encircled by twelve villages. By this same rite, having made a stūpa, one should offer lotus seats smeared with sandalwood and a hundred thousand food offerings; one will become the governor of a province. By this same rite, burning guggulu incense, one should offer a hundred thousand campaka flowers; one will obtain a thousand pieces of gold. By this same rite one should offer a hundred thousand nāgakesara flowers; one will obtain a thousand garments of fine cloth.

Likewise, for all the rites in which flowers of every kind are desired: taking ash from a burned corpse in the charnel ground, one should keep a fast, day and night, at the full moon. Making a circle with blood from the ring finger, one should draw an effigy, press it down with the left foot, and recite eight thousand times. First one obtains seven garments, and in short, one obtains everything together with its kind. Having made a stūpa, one should make eight thousand fire offerings of adhibalaja wood smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. Whatever girl one points out, that girl will be given to one; if she is not given, the one who refuses will die.

Making an effigy from the bark of the sāla tree, filling it with mustard oil, piercing it with an iron spike, and smearing it with hot sesame oil, one should recite eight thousand times in the charnel ground. A woman on her own, or a śūdra, comes under one's power. With the second, vaiśya and kṣatriya women; with the third, monks and brahmin women. In short, even without having accomplished it, it performs these rites.

Having consecrated bezoar seven times and marked oneself with it, whatever one sees and whoever sees one, all become delighted. Likewise with eye ointment. If, rising at dawn, one bathes at ease in water consecrated seven times, whoever one looks upon gives to one and even becomes one's subject. Likewise, by eating sesame oil without its touching the teeth, and by drinking water carried at will that has been consecrated seven times, one obtains food even without seeking it. Entering the royal palace, one should take hold of the hem of one's Dharma robe, recite fully twenty-one times, and tie a knot with the left hand. If one goes without looking back, one becomes supreme among all speakers. On going among bandits, by reciting over the very things that would be stolen, one makes them safe. So too the mantras for cutting, piercing, and the like.

Making an effigy from grains of śāli rice, white karavīra, siddhārtha, and kāba, pressing it with the left hand, and reciting eight thousand times, one makes it rise up. If one wishes to destroy fever, one should recite eight thousand times over the flowers of girikarṇikā; within seven days it overcomes the fever of the piśācas. If one makes eight thousand fire offerings with kindling sticks of khadira wood, it destroys all the grahas. Reciting seven times over ash binds the mantras of others; reciting once over water releases them. Such are these rites and others like them.

Then once again the Blessed One Śākyamuni looked out over that great maṇḍala of the assembly and said to the great bodhisattva: "Great being, there is one called Fulfiller of Desires. He is the lord of the family. This king of ritual manuals, rejoiced in by all the buddhas, the rite of the means of accomplishment that is the great secret of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā, should without fail be kept in mind by the practitioner. That, great being, I shall explain to you."

When he had said this, the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, requested the Blessed One to speak the lord of the family for the sake of accomplishing the Blessed Lady:

"O Fulfiller of Desires,
Blessed One, freed from passion and darkness,
Fully at peace from attachment,
Who leads out from evil to awakening:
To the moon who gazes on all,
The noble Avalokiteśvara,
Destroyer of the seed of existence,
I bow, I make offering, and I rely on you.
If what is to be taught is brought forth,
It will come forth again in the world."

tadyathā śvete śveteṃ ge śve bhu je śve ta mā lye rā laṃ kṛ te ja ye bi ja ye a ji te a pa rā ji te svā hā

By mere recollection of it, the accomplishment of this mantra comes swiftly. As for its mantra: rising at dawn, the practitioner of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā, having become clean, should enter a river seven times, join the palms, recite it fully, and, facing east, scatter the water. All obstructors will be pacified, and the accomplishment of rites will come as well. If one places the thumb at the heart and recites once, one will be blessed by the gods, and one will also become purified. Its mudrā too should be applied here. All obstructors will cease to be, and the accomplishment of rites will come as well. If one places the thumb at the heart and recites once, one will be blessed by the gods, and one will also become purified. Its mudrā too should be applied here.

Then there is the rite of its means of accomplishment. On undamaged cloth free of hair and with a fringe, a painter who keeps the poṣadha vows should draw the noble Avalokiteśvara with unmixed colors. He is seated on the heart of a lotus, wears a lower garment of tiger skin, and his hair is bound up high and hanging down. In his hand he holds a water pot, or else he holds white lotus petals. On his left side the goddess, the noble Mahāśvetā, is seated on a lion seat; her hands hold a lotus and make the gesture of granting boons. The practitioner is as before. Then the vidyādhara, eating milk and barley meal, should perform the preliminary approach in front of the painting.

The vidyādhara should likewise make offerings with handfuls of fragrant flowers, and should offer lamps of butter, incense of aloeswood and of turuṣka, and torma.

namo buddhāsya namo dharmāsya namaḥ saṃghasya nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo āryāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā surume suruma kuru kuru surume karmasādhāya buddhasadyena dharmasatyena saṃghasatyena āgaccha śīghrāṃ devadatte svāhā

This is the vidyā for invoking.

tadyathā dame dase svāhā

This is the vidyā of fragrance.

tadyathā hu hu hura hu mahāmede svare svāhā

This is the vidyā of flowers.

tadyathā meghavihrate svāhā

This is the vidyā of incense.

tadyathā tu tu tu tu turu mahāturuṇe svāhā

This is the vidyā of the torma.

With these very vidyās, seated close upon a mat of kuśa grass in front of the painting, before which a garland of seven lamps has been set, one should perform a fire offering of lotuses smeared with curd, honey and butter, up to seven hundred thousand times. One's own body will tremble, and one will see the noble Avalokiteśvara directly. One will obtain whatever one desires. If, by this same rite, one performs a fire offering of a hundred thousand sticks of bilva wood, whatever one desires will be completely fulfilled.

On the bank of the river Ganges, in a place free of harm and without people, one should build stūpas in the sand, offer fragrances, flowers, incense and so forth, and recite eight thousand times. One should build a stūpa each and every day.

This concludes the twelfth of the extensive chapters from the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā, a Great Vehicle sūtra of the Avataṃsaka of the Bodhisattva Piṭaka.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being, the noble Avalokiteśvara, surveyed the entire world system with his divine eye and entered the samādhi called Endowed with Vastness. Then, rising from that samādhi, he spoke this great king of mantras called Endowed with Vastness:

namo ratnatrayāya nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā vimale vimale vipulaprabhe vipulapriye vipulamati samayamanusmara tvame varusāṃ sādhaya sādhaya garja garja hana hana vipulamati hṛdaya manusmara buddhasatyena dharmasatyena saṃghasatyena bodhisatvāsatyena vipulamatisatyena vajrapāṇisatyena satyavātisatyena le le le le oṃ oṃ oṃ bhuva bhuva bhuva ga ga ga matha matha matha hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ avalokite muce svāhā

This is the great king of vidyās called Endowed with Vastness, which has attained great power, arisen from the samādhi of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā, and accomplished simply by being read. It protects oneself, protects others and protects the village; and the danger of mountains, the danger of the vicious, the danger of piśācas, in short all dangers, it dispels merely by being read.

Further, the mantra rites that follow from this are these:

namo ratnatrayāya nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā dade śānte prasannacite svāhā

This is the mantra for invoking.

namo ratnatrayāya nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā śvete samayetyethā viśuddhavasti svāhā

This is the mantra for putting on garments.

namo ratnatrayāya nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā mune mune śānte viśuddhe gaganatale pugandhe gandha udakabaliṃ ca hara hara kara kara vibhu svāhā

Having consecrated all the flowers, fragrances, incense and lamps by reciting this mantra over them seven times, one should recite it once, or else offer them. One should always purify oneself with balls of white clay. To the Blessed One one should offer saffron water, sandalwood, the fragrance of camphor, turuṣka and the like, incense of aloeswood, garlands of mallikā or campaka flowers, and milk in thirty-two portions, together with tormas of barley meal and lamps of cow's butter.

Next, its painting is described. On a cloth of whatever kind can be found, free of hair and with its fringe left uncut, one should draw the Blessed One Avalokiteśvara in saffron. He should be drawn like this: on a seat of a water-born lotus, holding a lotus in his hand and adorned with a garland of lotuses, clad in white garments, holding it up for the sake of worship, his hand granting fearlessness, his hair bound up high.

Having invited the Blessed One to reside in the painting, set facing east in the place described before, one should recite a million times. When the recitation is complete, one should kindle a fire and, with honey and butter mixed together, perform the fire offering at the three times of day until a hundred thousand are completed; then one will obtain whatever one longs for. If one wishes for the enjoyments of kingship, one should mix together saffron, sandalwood, hundred-petaled flowers and puffed rice, smear them with butter and honey, and perform the fire offering in three sessions. On the last day of the fire offering he grants a vision of himself. He also grants these signs: one's crown lock will stand straight up. He bestows or speaks of a flawless banner of light and a painting of blazing garlands. The vidyādhara should recite mentally. If one hears a divine voice in the sky, it is accomplished. Then, if one regains the kingdom, one should have it governed in accordance with the Dharma.

Then, once more cultivating that same samādhi, he spoke the great king of vidyās called One-Footed, the great king of the ritual manual of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

namo ratnatrayāya nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya namo buddha abhiṣekasya prajvalitadīptanepra bhujāya prajvalitaṃ dīptahapukamaṇḍalāya tadyathā hṛdayamāvartayiṣyamighuṭa bandha dhuṃ dhaṃ dhaṃ dhaṃ dhaṃ cara cara varaya śasma oṃ karaṃ prata vidyāteja yamahā vidyāyaya svayaska pravartaya haraṇe raṇe rakaruṇe muni muni vimuni śānta cinta svāhā

This is the king of vidyās called One-Footed, which has attained great power. It is unobstructed; merely by being recited it crushes all fighting, quarrels, disputes and the like. It is a king of vidyās that overpowers opponents with immeasurable strength. A son of good family, having generated the mind set on awakening, should undertake the practice, bathe three times, and recite eight thousand times in three sessions. Until the full moon, having made great offerings before the Blessed One, one should recite it countless times. All minor rites will be accomplished.

These are the mantras that form its retinue:

namo ratnatrayāya nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā vibhuri vibhuri bhumi ākāma bhumi ākāma bhumi ākāma tiṣṭha tiṣṭha vijaya varta śa śa śa śa śa śa tha tha tha tha tha tha tha tha akantha akndha padmahastāya svāhā

This is the mantra for consecrating the painting.

First comes the painter's work, and after it the rite of the painting. One should have Avalokiteśvara painted in unmixed colors, standing on one foot. He holds up a garland of jasmine flowers as an offering, is adorned with the radiance of flower garlands, and holds in his hands a staff and a round water pitcher; a black antelope skin should hang all about his shoulder. Having had painted a painting in which his right hand seems to be giving consolation, one should give a feast to the community of monks in front of it, and also offer a gift according to one's means.

namo ratnatrayāṃya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā jaladhara vimuktayathāya svāhā

This is the mantra for anointing.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā sugandha vimukta vijaya svāhā

This is the mantra of fragrance.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā sumanaśriye sasaṃdarśana sosomana sosomana svāhā

This is the mantra of flowers.

namo ratnatrayāya nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā dhumra varcasi ra ra ra ra lalāya mune svāhā

This is the mantra of incense.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namaḥ priyaṃkara pritivijaye oṃ jaye vijaye saṃkalpa svāhā

This is the mantra of the torma.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namaḥ śucini mati vimali viśuddhagati svāhā

This is the mantra for rinsing with water.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namaḥ tadyathā śvete paṇḍavāsini rakṣa rakṣa māṃ svāhā

With this one should protect oneself in every circumstance.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dhara dhariścitte javari śupaci vati svāhā

With this one should take up earth.

namo ratnatrayāya namo ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya nama jali jali calārale vavare rarare svāhā

With this mantra one should bathe.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā namaḥ śulambi vastraṃ tadhārāri phavane svāhā

This is the mantra of garments. One should recite it over one's garments and then put them on, and likewise offer garments to the Blessed One.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā nama ucchuṣma parama daśa śodhana śodhaya svāhā

If urine, excrement, spittle and every impurity are wiped away with this, one becomes clean. This is the mantra of cleanliness.

Two measures of Indian incense, two of sandalwood, two of leafy rumru, and two of saffron: these fragrances should be offered to the Blessed One. The incense is of camphor and sandalwood. By a rite such as this, having invited the Blessed One into the painting, set facing east in the place described, one should bathe three times, change one's clothes three times, and, constantly keeping the poṣadha vows, recite six hundred thousand times. At the end one should strew white lotuses one at a time at the feet of the Blessed One as an offering, eight thousand over three days. Then, keeping a fast for three nights and not speaking the whole night through, one should perform a fire offering with lotuses smeared with butter.

The characteristic sign of accomplishment is this: the vidyādhara, fully liberated, will move about in three ways. Then the Blessed One will be accomplished. If one wishes to be a vidyādhara, one will become a vidyādhara. If one wishes to be an asura, one will become an asura. If one wishes for kingship, one will attain a great kingship over all. One will obtain everything that one wishes for. The samādhi Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of the Blessed Lady Tārā, will certainly arise.

This completes the king of vidyās called One-Footed.

Then again the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, while cultivating that same king of samādhis, spoke the great king of vidyās called Entering the Ritual Manual of the Blessed Lady, the Queen of Vidyās.

Here these become the great words of the mantra:

namo ratnatrayāya nama āryāvajiyaśrīgarbhasya samyaksaṃbuddhesya namo maheśvaresva bodhisatvasya namaḥ īśaprabhasya bodhisatvasya namaḥ ākāśagarbhasya bodhisatvasya namo vajramatesya bodhisatvasya nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā bhagavate hṛdaya māvāhayiṣyāmi oṃ tara tara oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ bhuva abhaya abhaya varade ucuṣmati ucuṣmati sukhāvati sukhāvati ra ra ra ra la la la la culuṣka khaga khaga āgaccha āgaccha bhagavate mama varaṃ dāsyasi abhasvara maprāpta vipulamati samādhi vijate svāhā

The great king of vidyās called Entering is accomplished merely by being read. It protects from all fears and performs rites in every field.

Next comes the rite of its painting. The Blessed One, the noble Avalokiteśvara, entirely white, with the features of the painting described before, is seated on a jeweled lotus, holding a white lotus in his hand, his crown lock loosened, and holding a round water pitcher in his hand. On the right and left are figures as appropriate. On the left side one should have painted a white youth holding a lotus in his hand and paying homage to the Blessed One. On the right side one should have painted the Blessed Lady Mahāśrī holding a lotus in her hand and seated upon a lotus. On the left side is the earth goddess Pṛthivī, holding in her hand a basin of the four kinds of jewels. In the sky one should have painted the white bodhisattva of clear light, holding a garland of flowers. On the right side is the practitioner holding a censer, as before.

Having made a painting of this kind and installed it in the place described before, one should make vast offerings and, eating milk and barley meal, invite the deity with the root mantra.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisatvebhyaḥ tadyathā paṇḍa paṇḍalaghu śuci vimale svāhā

This is the mantra of the maṇḍala.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisatvebhyaḥ tadyathā agni julu julu hu ramame svāhā

This is the mantra of fragrance.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisatvebhyaḥ tadyathā dhuva siddhi brahmatejo svāhā

This is the mantra of flowers.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisatvebhyaḥ tadyathā vipulateja prahmaśvara svāhā

This is the mantra of incense.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisatvebhyaḥ nidhi vipuni abhayaprada svāhā

This is the mantra of the torma. This same one is the mantra of the lamps.

A garland of fragrance made of equal parts of bushel-tsé, bālaka and camphor; red karavīra flowers and handfuls of jasmine flowers; incense compounded of śrīveṣṭaka, sarjarasa resin, gum, śallakī and molasses; torma of the three white substances; and lamps of cow's butter: having arranged things in this way, one should recite six hundred thousand times.

At the end, at the full moon, observing a fast for three nights, one should perform a fire offering of eight thousand karavīra flowers smeared with curd, honey and butter at the three times of day, and one should do this for three days. Then, on the third day, having made vast offerings according to the rite as described, with twelve bowls in all, of curd and honey, and ten bowls of milk porridge, one should sit on a mat of kuśa grass and, beginning at dusk, recite until a sign of accomplishment appears. A rain of divine flowers will fall, thunder and great drums will resound, the painting will tremble, and the flames of the lamps will grow tall. Then it is accomplished, and one will become a king with power over the whole earth. Whatever one longs for, one will obtain it all.

This completes the great king of vidyās called Entering the Root Ritual Manual of the King of Samādhis Endowed with Vastness of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, in order to care for beings, once more cultivating that same king of samādhis, spoke the vidyā of Mahāśvetā within the great king of ritual manuals of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā, in order to care for poor people. Here these are the words of the vidyā mantra that accomplishes all aims:

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya kṛṣṇajinaṃ varadhara kamalāya tīkṣaṃ padma asanasthaṃ abhayaprad magrahataṃ bhāṣasvajjaṭamakuṭadhari ṇau padmavarṇa ārya avalokiteśvari mahaṃ saraṇaṃ prapadya tadyathā śvete vijaye śvetavastra śvetabhuje śvetapadma alaṃkīrta jaye vijaye abhaye śvetaṃ aṃśumabhayaprate śvetaṃ ca gaganaśuddhaṃ śvetaṃ vidyā samapra samaprabhe śvetebhyaḥ bhavasya śaklāṃśuraṃ bhavāntare paṇḍara paṭa paṭāya ra ra ra ra raya vijaye svāhā pariklīvale vare varāya svāhā

This is the queen of vidyās called Mahāśvetā, who has attained great power. She performs all rites, completely pacifies poverty and disease, accomplishes all aims, and brings all aims to fulfillment. Whatever son or daughter of good family, having generated the mind set on awakening, constantly keeps her in mind and worships her will protect people, and all people will rejoice in them.

Then her rite is this. Following the rite described before, one should have a cloth ten cubits long made, with its fringe cut off, and press it smooth with sandalwood water. Then one should paint the Blessed One in unmixed colors, with a brush and fragrant liquid.

He is white like an autumn cloud, holds a round water pitcher in his hand, and holds a lotus in his right hand. His hair is bound up high; he has a lotus seat and white garments, is adorned with ornaments of white garlands, and is adorned with sixteen garlands of lotuses. Everything is white, with all things white.

Sixteen bodhisattvas should be drawn below. The four world guardians are in the surrounding directions. The earth goddess Pṛthivī should be drawn holding a basket in her right hand. At the crown of the noble Avalokiteśvara's head is the Tathāgata Padmāvataṃsaka. On the left is the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, granting fearlessness, holding his Dharma robe with his left hand, golden in color, with rays of light streaming from his hand. All the bodhisattvas too have garlands of light, their bodies adorned with every kind of brilliant ornament. One should also have the practitioner painted on the right side, with his attire and appearance just as they are.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā svete svete svete svetabhuje parākrame vijaya vicedhute svāhā

With water of white fragrance one should anoint the maṇḍala.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya ablokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya namo mahāsvahāya svetagandha viśuddhaya sugandhāya svāhā

This is the mantra of fragrance.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya namo mahāsvetāya jyotisma tījyetipara svāhā

This is the vidyā of flowers.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya namo mahāsvetāya svetaparāya dhupaparāya svāhā

One should offer incense mixed with white substances.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya namo mahāsvetāya valavīryapravara vara śukllaṃ śukllodna varapriyāya vara vara vara vara śukle śuklā śukle svāhā

This is the mantra of the torma; the rest should be offered with the root vidyā itself.

One should perform a fire offering with flowers, incense, fragrances and garlands, all of them white, smeared with curd, honey and butter. Beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight and continuing until the full moon, there are eight thousand fire offerings with sesame oil; the vidyādhara, wearing white clothes, eating a meal of caru, wearing a white sacred thread, and seated close upon a mat of kuśa grass, should perform the fire offerings and the rest. Having made great offerings, one should make torma offerings and so forth day and night. Beginning at dusk, one should recite until a sign of accomplishment appears. The sound of great divine drums will ring out, the earth will quake, a rain of flowers will fall from the sky, and rays of light will stream forth from the painting. At this juncture the Blessed One, the bodhisattva, arrives, and in that instant the hells, the hungry ghosts and the animals are soothed. When he has arrived, one should offer him arghya water. Then the Blessed One will speak and grant whatever is desired. Whether one wishes to become a vidyādhara, or a king of vidyādharas, or to exchange one's body for a great kingdom, or to enter the underworld, or for eye ointment, realgar or bezoar, or for the power to retain what one has heard, or for the five superknowledges, one will obtain whatever one seeks.

This completes the ritual manual of Mahāśvetā, the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, from the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, having surveyed all beings by means of the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, spoke the king of vidyās called the Blessed One Who Follows All Kings of Vidyās. Here these are the rites of the accomplished mantra:

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya vimukticetapāya vijaya parākramaya apratihata glīyāya aparimita dharmmadeśahanāya duḥkhviśodhanāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya arttaparidranahṛdayamādhayiṣyamimiti tadyathā lave ālaṃve lamba pramukta lamba sthire lamba vidyāyate namaḥ kāruni kāruṇe kāruṇayati vo mune kuruṇāndha hṛdaye kāruṇanhra namastute śānta mukte ca śāneka yavivo stata śānta prabhāte nityaṃ vagavatya namastute suru suru āgaccha āgaccha bhagavāna mama varaṃ dīsyasi duḥkhitānāma saradriṇikaraṃ svāhā

This is the great king of vidyās that has attained great power and keeps all beings from going to ruin. Merely by being remembered it follows one closely behind; it protects the afflicted, turns back the lower realms, and is accomplished by being read. In short, in every danger, merely by its being remembered, its eight companions are set to protecting one. Whoever recites this king of vidyās, practices it and fully engages in it will never fall into the lower realms. Whatever son of good family who is poor, having generated the mind set on awakening, reads it, recites it, practices it and holds it dear in his mind will, after he dies and passes on, be born in Sukhāvatī.

Next, the rite of its sādhana is this. One should draw the Blessed One Avalokiteśvara as he arrives: granting fearlessness, his hair bound up high, his body adorned with the marks of a great being, three-eyed, his body ablaze with the rays of moonlight, protecting from all the eight fears, the Blessed One Amitābha seated upon his head, and wearing a white sacred thread. The practitioner is as before.

Having drawn a painting of this kind, one should make great offerings, and with this very mantra offer fragrances, flowers, incense and torma according to the rite. Whoever undertakes it, single-mindedly heroic and remaining wholly absorbed in this great king of vidyās even outside the proper times, should sit close upon a mat of kuśa grass and, with a nature of pure loving-kindness that reaches out to all beings, recite it eight thousand times. Then it will be accomplished, and it will do everything one wishes, as well as the minor rites and the like. With water it destroys poison. By sprinkling with kuśa grass it destroys fevers that come every day, every second day, every fourth day and so forth. When the mantra is recited over a flower, whoever it is given to comes under one's power. In short, by applying it one destroys all diseases.

As for its sādhana: having invited the deity into the painting in the place described before, one recites a hundred thousand times. At the end, keeping a fast for one night, one should offer torma to the guardians of the directions; the torma consists of the three white substances. Having performed the rite of offering, one should sit close upon a mat of kuśa grass and, beginning at dusk, recite until a sign of accomplishment appears. If the painting shakes strongly and the flames of the lamps grow tall, one will become a king with power over all. Even if it is not accomplished, one will obtain a land. It grants every kind of fearlessness. By recitation one brings all beings under one's power. It completely pacifies all diseases. It cuts through all bonds. Or else, by remembering it, one is able to travel.

This completes the great king of vidyās called Who Causes All Beings to Follow, in the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness of the root ritual manual of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then again the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, while cultivating the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, spoke the great king of ritual manuals of the great vidyā called Golden Light, as a further great king of ritual manuals of the Blessed Lady:

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahākāruṇikāya prajvalitahastakamaṇḍalupriyāya tadyathā surasya amṛta apratihatai veve cacare carṭhare veve ruru veruru dhve the the sara dhve sara sara dhvi gu gu meghane ghana ghane apratihaste buddhasatyaṃ dharmmasatyaṃ saṃghasatyaṃ uparisatyena bhagavāna samayamanusmara padmagarbha svāhā padmasuvarṇati svāhā padmaja svāhā padmapriyāya svāhā padmasutritiṣṭhatacaraṇāya svāhā sarvabhayadada svāhā ārya amitābha samājñāpayati svāhā

This is the great king of vidyās called Golden Light, which has attained great power. It is sanctioned by many buddhas, sustains all beings like gold, and is accomplished by being read. It frees one from all yakṣas and drives them away, and merely by being recited it dispels disease.

Next comes the rite of its painting. The Blessed One, the noble Avalokiteśvara, appears golden in color, his hair bound up high, his right hand granting fearlessness, adorned here and there with garlands of lotuses, holding a round water pitcher in his hand, wearing white garments, his face broadly smiling, and both his feet resting on a lotus. The practitioner holds a censer in his hand, as before. Having carried out the rite of the painting in this way and installed it in the place described before, one should recite five hundred thousand times.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya bodhisatvāya mahāsasvāya jale jale da śuci durvace aprade śucini prabhute svāhā

This is the mantra for anointing.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya padmagarbhe sugandhaya muru suru svāhā

This is the mantra of fragrance.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya bhuvaḥ bhurbhuva vidyācandra cale cale svāhā

This is the mantra of flowers.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya padmaśriye varvarile svāhā

This is the mantra of incense.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya amṛte amṛte gahvare sumukhe svāhā

This is the mantra of the torma.

Having done this as before, by a fire offering of aloeswood one obtains whatever one wishes. By a fire offering of sandalwood one summons. By a fire offering of jasmine flowers all people will be delighted. Beginning on the first day of the fortnight of miracles, one should recite eight thousand times in three sessions before the painting, with the rite of offering, until the full moon. Keeping a fast for three nights, one should install the painting on the bank of a river that flows to the ocean, or on an island, and perform the rite of offering; beginning at dusk, one should recite until a sign of accomplishment appears. The painting may shake strongly, or the flames of the lamps may grow tall, or a rain of flowers may fall from the sky, or the sound of thunder may be heard. If the painting shakes, one will become a great king. If the lamps grow, one will become the lord of a town. If flowers fall, one will become the master of a land. With the sound of thunder one will obtain sixteen towns. Even if it is not accomplished, all one's work and requisites will be fully provided, and all one's diseases will be cast off.

This completes the great king of vidyās called Golden Light, of the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, once again meditating on the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, in order fully to reveal the power of the Blessed Lady's great king of vidyās, her great king of ritual manuals, brought to mind the king of vidyās called Empowered by the Twelve Buddhas, and spoke:

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā saṭā saṭa sara sarāṇi śuddha bitri mukhe bijaye svāhā

This is the great king of vidyās called the Vidyā Empowerment, which has attained great power. Whoever reads it or recites it will have paid homage to twelve koṭis of buddhas. By reciting it constantly, one will not fall into any of the evil destinies. One will remember one's births through twelve hundred births. At all times one will remember the five higher knowledges and the three junctures of the day. None of one's diseases, nor piśācas and the like, nor rākṣasas, will pass into one's body, and so it will be even for hundreds of koṭis of eons.

The rite of the painting for this is as follows. On undamaged cloth having the characteristics stated before, one should draw the noble Avalokiteśvara in full: white, his matted locks piled upward, Padmapāṇi, with the right hand granting boons and the left hand holding a lotus. Above him one should draw twelve perfectly complete buddhas, golden in color, granting fearlessness. Namely, one should draw in full these perfectly complete buddhas: Padmottara, Guṇottara, Jñāneśvara, Ever Melodious, Vipaśyin, Śikhin, Viśvabhū, Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, Kāśyapa, Śākyamuni, Amitābha, and Akṣobhya.

Having had such a painting made, and having seated oneself in the place described before, one should do three hundred thousand recitations. With this very vidyā one should offer scent, flowers, incense and so forth. Whatever one is doing, with single-minded heroism one should recite it a hundred thousand times. Then one should keep a fast for three nights, make a great offering to the painting, and take eye ointment, or realgar, or gorocanā, recited over a thousand times. Wrapping it in a leaf of the aśvattha tree in front of the painting, according to the rite as described, one should sit on a mat of kuśa grass and, beginning at dusk, recite until it grows warm, gives off smoke, and blazes. If one makes a tilaka with it while it is growing warm, one brings everyone under one's power. With it while it is smoking, one becomes invisible. With it blazing, one travels through the sky. If the painting shakes strongly, one will come to kingship.

This completes the great king of vidyās called Empowered by the Twelve Buddhas, arisen from the samādhi Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, once again meditating on the samādhi Endowed with Vastness, and fully considering the world systems endowed with everything, spoke this great king of ritual manuals of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā, called the Garland of Devotion, which was spoken by the buddhas:

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya namo namaḥ sarba bodhisatvāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā maṇḍa biśāla kīrti sarba bidyā svāhā

This is the great queen of vidyās called the Garland of Devotion, which has attained great power, which many buddhas have sanctioned, and which fully generates the samādhis of many bodhisattvas. It should be accomplished. For any poor person who would accomplish it, within a month of the painting his prosperity will increase. For any poor person who obtains it, this vidyā, since it bestows great benefit, will become an object of worship. It is the rite that brings about worldly prosperity.

Then, as for the means of accomplishment: one should draw the painting of the Blessed Avalokiteśvara described before. Beginning it on the ninth day, one should have it completed on the full moon of the bright fortnight. He is seated on a seat of white lotus, his matted locks piled upward. Above, as a second figure, is the noble Amitābha, and at his side Śākyamuni as well. To the right of the noble Avalokiteśvara one should draw Mahāśrī. On the left side one should draw Vajrasena, white in color, white like an autumn cloud, holding in his hands a round flask and a water vessel. On the crown of the noble Avalokiteśvara there should be atimuktaka flowers; for the noble Amitābha, a garland of varṣa flowers; for Śākyamuni, a garland of jasmine flowers; for Mahāśrī, a garland of nāgakesara flowers; and for Vajrasena, a garland of white flowers. One should offer these, and fragrant incense, as far as one's means allow. Having installed the painting in the place described before, one should do three hundred thousand recitations.

Then, on the full moon, having made a great offering to the painting of garlands of flowers and the like, one should sit on a mat of kuśa grass, and whatever one does with this vidyā, one should do it all with single-minded heroism. One should recite the great queen of vidyās until the sign appears of all the garlands shaking. When the mark of accomplishment appears, one will obtain everything one desires. If in every respect one performs before the painting six hundred thousand fire offerings mixed with sesame, one will gain a kingdom. If one desires the riches of a land, by performing before the painting three hundred thousand fire offerings of white mustard seed, sesame and cekata, one will gain a land. If before the painting one makes seven hundred thousand fire offerings of saffron, resin incense, black pepper and costus mixed with butter and honey, one will gain a great kingdom. If it is not accomplished, one will gain a land and become a great lord of wealth.

This completes the king of vidyās called the Garland of Devotion, of the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then once more the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, once again meditating on the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, spoke to the bodhisattva, the great being Vajrapāṇi: "In order to summon constantly the deities of your family, who have many different forms, the yakṣas, the yakṣiṇīs, the great yakṣa generals, Divine Flower, Moon herself, and those means endowed with the wish for peace, this mantra will be made sovereign."

Here, the words of the great mantra that summons all yakṣas are these:

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya namaḥ sarba sena sataye nama āryābalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahasatvaya mahākāruṇikāya yakṣa jrimbhana muktāya sarbaṃ yakṣaṃ hṛdayaṃ guhya adhipatāya bhagabān āryābalokiteśvarāya hṛdaya manu smara satya manusāla tadyathā śīle śīlabati dāni praye śante satvā darṣanan tathāgata sarba jñā jñāna darṣana mama saraṃ prayacche sarba satvā hitārthāya svāhā

When this secret mantra that overcomes adversaries with great strength had been spoken, and all who dwell in the great trichiliocosm world system had been summoned, then through the power of the bodhisattva, Vajrapāṇi, the lord of all yakṣas, the Lord of Secrets, who is no trifling being and is endowed with great miraculous power, spoke these words: "Whoever, with a mind intent on the welfare of beings, accomplishes Tārā, to him you must surely grant accomplishment! Each of you, doing your share, should always act to help him. When beings call to mind this goddess Tārā, you are to protect, guard and shelter those embodied beings. Whoever does not carry out my command will have his head split into seven pieces by Vajrapāṇi, the Lord of Secrets, Vajradhara of great strength."

This king of vidyās called the Summoner of All Yakṣas, which is preceded by the wisdom of omniscience and has attained great power, protects from all malignant beings and all fears merely by being read.

Now I shall explain the means of accomplishing it. Following the rite of the painting taught before, one should have the noble Avalokiteśvara painted: his matted locks piled upward, holding a lotus stem in his hand, Padmapāṇi, with a black antelope skin hanging from him, wearing white garments and seated cross-legged; so one should have him painted. On the right side one should draw the great yakṣa generals, namely Jaya, Vijaya, Sātāgiri, the Son of the Secret One, Maṇibhadra, the Son of Fair Gait, the Son of the Loving One, the Son of the Noble Hero, Brahmā, and Mindful of Water. One should have many yakṣa kings such as these painted, and the yakṣa generals, holding in their hands sacks filled with seeds, should be placed close by. On the left side are the yakṣa generals called End of Victory, Trunk, Attainer of Victory, Aniruddha, and King of Garuḍas; all of these are green in color, as before. On the right of the Blessed One there is also a vidyādhara, holding a censer in his hand, as before. One should have it painted under the lunar mansion Āśleṣā.

Then, having installed the painting in a stūpa that contains relics or in some other clean place, one should invite the deities with this mantra:

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya namaḥ yakṣa senāpataye nama ārya abalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā jaye bijaye aguru ehi ehi sthānāṃ ākrama bijaye baha śāntikara svāhā

With this mantra one should invite the Blessed One and all the yakṣas.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya namaḥ sarba yakṣa sena pataye namo nama ārya abalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya ra ra ra ra śānti bijaye svāhā

With this one should offer all the scents, incense and so forth. Likewise one should do three hundred thousand recitations before the painting. On the full moon, keeping a fast day and night, one should offer the Blessed One a torma of curd and milk porridge. To the great yakṣa generals on the right side one should offer curd and molasses. To those drawn on the left side one should offer sesame and sesame soup. To Avalokiteśvara one offers aloeswood incense, one offers sandalwood scent, and one should offer garlands of jasmine flowers. To the generals on the right side one offers incense of the five resins and white karavīra flowers. To those on the left side one should offer resin incense and atimuktaka flowers.

Having made offerings in this way, as far as one is able, one should recite eight thousand times. Then at the three times of day one should make offerings in the same way, eating milk and barley porridge; and reciting over each white lotus in full, one should offer it to the Blessed One before the painting. When one has done this up to the completion of one hundred thousand, all the yakṣas that were drawn display miracles. At the junctures between sessions one sees the painting move and the flowers stir. Then it is accomplished, and all the yakṣas come under one's power. In the sky, too, one hears the sound "It is accomplished!" They bestow the supreme state of a vidyādhara. Whatever one seeks, the yakṣas will carry it out as commanded. If it is not accomplished, one becomes a king of all rites. Constantly, in dreams, the yakṣas grant visions of what is virtuous and what is nonvirtuous.

This completes the great king of vidyās called the Coming of All Yakṣas, arisen from the samādhi Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then once more the bodhisattva, the great being, the noble Avalokiteśvara, spoke to the lord of bhūtas, the son of the gods Īśāna: "Son of the gods, you of great miraculous power, I shall explain the Blessed Lady's great queen of vidyās, the great king of ritual manuals, into which you will duly enter. Its mantra words are rightly held to be the vidyā mantra of all worldly beings:

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya abalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā īśana kula ma batu yiṣyami bhagabate ārya abalokiteśvara tejana ra ra ra ra ra bipuci bipuci bramathā prama pramatha pramathā garja garja garja ṭi ṭi ṭi sa sa sa u u u la la la ca ca ca āgaccha agaccha bhagabāna āryābalokiteśvarāya parama hṛdayaṃ dhārayiṣyati iśvorāsya bipomati tvāṃ prasāṃtha baraṃ ṅeyaṃ sarba satvā hiti dhutaṃ bara yakṣaya sarkara muni muni apratihata bītyokṛta hatikṛta yakṣakṛta nama ārya abalokiteśvarāya svāhā"

This is the mantra that draws forth the entire family of Īśāna, spoken from the mouths of the bodhisattvas, the great beings. The sons of the gods of great miraculous power said: "This mantra has been proclaimed in order to fulfill the wishes of people on earth who desire the welfare of beings."

"Whatever practitioner accomplishes this and desires accomplishment, to him you are to grant the supreme. For the hundred million whose minds are intent on the welfare of beings, and for those who on earth accomplish the mantras you yourselves have proclaimed, this mantra, proclaimed for summoning the gods, accomplishes great power; and you are to bestow the splendor and strength of Tārā, the great vidyā of many forms. All you hosts of bhūtas, protect them!"

Then comes the rite for accomplishing this. Following the rite described before, on cloth one should draw the Blessed One, the noble Avalokiteśvara, appearing golden in color, Padmapāṇi, his right hand granting boons and his left hand holding a lotus, with a crown of matted locks hanging down, and the Blessed Amitābha seated on the crown of his head. To the right of the noble Avalokiteśvara one should draw the bodhisattva who embodies the samādhi called Endowed with Vastness, surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas. On the left side one should draw the great beings Īśāna and the rest; he is three-eyed.

Having set this painting up high in the place described before, one should perform the rite of offering beginning on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, and with this very mantra one should recite a hundred thousand times; thus the preliminary approach will have been done. Keeping a fast day and night, on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight one should offer a white torma to all the bodhisattvas and offer incense of aloeswood and olibanum. To the noble Avalokiteśvara one should offer incense together with milk; and to the family of the one who appears in every color and desires everything, one should offer food of curd and molasses and incense of guggulu. Outside the painting one offers a torma for all the bhūtas, and one offers the monks a feast together with gifts. One should offer curd and rice to the Pāśupatas and so gain their peace.

Until the full moon one should recite eight thousand times at the three times of day. Then, beginning at dusk, one should recite until the sign of accomplishment appears: the eyes of Īśāna flashing. When the sign of accomplishment has appeared here, one should offer garlands of flowers and offer guggulu incense. When the ascetics have eaten whatever there is, one should offer them gifts. Then it accomplishes everything. Whoever is given flowers, fruit, scent, clothing or the like over which the mantra has been spoken will stay close by as one's servant.

If one desires the enjoyments of a kingdom, one should make fire offerings of curd, butter and milk soup before the painting; at the end of one hundred thousand, the crest of a vidyādhara will blaze. If one wishes to bring the agents of punishment under one's power, one makes fire offerings of sesame and sesame soup before the painting for three nights in three sessions, and they come under one's power. If one wishes to bring a maiden under one's power, by making eight thousand fire offerings of the milk of a cow that has calved for the first time, before the painting for three nights in three sessions, one will win her. If one wishes to bring the Pāśupatas under one's power, by making fire offerings of ash they come under one's power. If one recites eight thousand times in three sessions for seven days, it brings about all the samādhis, of every kind, of people on earth, as far as those that transcend worldly activity. There is no doubt about this mantra.

This completes the great king of vidyās, the Coming of the Whole Family of Īśāna, arisen from the samādhi Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the noble Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, once again meditating on the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, out of compassion for beings recollected the king of vidyās called Entering, which leads into the Blessed Lady's great king of ritual manuals, and spoke:

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya abalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bidyārājāya tadyathā biśuddha praba karṣa karṣa bhaśiṣe bidyādhara guhyeka manusmāra buddha satyena dharma satvāna saṃgha satyena ārya abalokiteśvara satvena sidhyantā me mantra padā phaṭ phaṭ yā muni munāya samatha samāya uddharaṃ te kokarānte manusmāraṭa hṛdata sakārā ṭoṭaṃ kaṭaṭe svāhā

This great king of vidyās called Entering, which has attained great power, when recited terrifies all malignant beings, turns back all grahas and hostile vidyās, and in short fulfills every hope.

Next comes its accomplishment. One should have the Blessed Avalokiteśvara painted: white in color, with smoke-colored matted locks, his face broadly smiling, his right hand granting boons and his left hand holding a lotus; he should be drawn stepping onto a fine golden staircase.

One should draw much-praised birds such as geese, ospreys, ruddy shelducks, partridges and parrots, circling him, moving to the right. One should draw two kinnaras singing, and draw them covering their ears with the left hand. The practitioner too, facing down from below, holding a censer in his hand, gazing at the Blessed One who is entering, kneeling, should be drawn below on the right, overwhelmed by the light from the bodhisattva's body. Having had a painting of this kind made, and having installed the painting in the place described before, one should begin properly.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya abalokiteśvaraya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahāsatvāya jāti huti mama abatādya svāhā

This is the maṇḍala mantra.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya abalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mune mune svāhā

With this one does everything. One should recite it five hundred thousand times; thus the preliminary approach will have been done. At the end one should make fire offerings of a hundred thousand lotuses smeared with curd, honey and butter. At the end one keeps a fast day and night, and recites countless times. If, as the sign of accomplishment, the painting shakes strongly, one will become lord of a great land. If it does not shake, one will become lord of a district. Through constant recitation one will come to see treasures. One should offer a million lotuses before the painting, and one gains a town. One should offer thirty thousand, and one will gain five towns. If, through the practice of the king of vidyās, one constantly longs for it and keeps it in mind, one will not become poor.

This completes the great king of vidyās, Entering, arisen from the samādhi Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then once more the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, meditating on the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, spoke to the Blessed One, within the great king of ritual manuals, the great king of mantras that forms the great king of vidyās called Ten Syllables: of great and wondrous benefit, rejoiced in by ten koṭis of buddhas, dispelling all subtle harms, and protecting all beings.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya abalokiteśvaraya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikaya tadyathā oṃ ghaṭṭani phumatana svāhā

This great king of vidyās called Ten Syllables, which has attained great power, is unobstructed and serves for every rite. Sanctioned by ten koṭis of buddhas, it is beautiful and protects. One should worship it at all times.

Then comes the offering for accomplishing it. Having made offerings, as far as one's means allow, to a stūpa that contains relics, and having offered scent, incense and the like with this very mantra, one should recite it ten million times. One gains a great kingdom. If one recites it a million times, one gains a thousand pieces of gold. If one smears a thousand maṇḍalas near a stūpa, offers scent, incense and the like, and recites it a hundred thousand times, whatever king one wishes will come under one's power. At a great river, at an island, or at a stūpa of the Sugata one span in height, one should do three hundred thousand recitations. One gains a great kingdom, and great benefit is truly realized. Whoever constantly keeps this mantra in mind is rejoiced in by ten koṭis of buddhas, is highly praised, and reaches everything.

This completes the great king of vidyās called Ten Syllables, arisen from the samādhi Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, once again meditating on the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, spoke the great king of vidyās called Consecration on the Crown, the great king of ritual manuals of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā:

namo ratnatrayāya namo akṣobhyaya tadyathā namo bimukta darṣanāya tathāgatāya namo gambhira ghoṣaya tathāgatāya nama ārya abalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā kumāri kumāri manojabeṣu nājaye śarada bijayāya duṃdubhi svarāya debi debi debi pūjitāya nama skṛta garjatāya ra ra la la khagāya svāhā baruṇāya svāhā apratihata badanāya svāhā brahma śvara ghoṣa rutraya svāhā bisati sati rājāya svāhā ārya abalokiteśvarāya mūrdhānā baraṇa svāhā mama karyaṃ kuru svāhā

This is the great king of vidyās called Consecration on the Crown, which has attained great power. It arose on my crown, was spoken by many koṭis of buddhas, was conferred in the consecration by the hands of many buddhas, and has become the abode of the Tathāgata Amitābha. Merely by reading it, one quickly accomplishes all minor rites.

Then comes the rite of its means of accomplishment. Observing the poṣadha vows near a stūpa that contains relics, one recites it a hundred thousand times. One will be freed from all who seek an opening to do harm. On the day of the lunar mansion Viśākhā, having offered scent, flowers and the like to a stūpa that contains relics, one should have the noble Avalokiteśvara painted on cloth whose edges have not been cut: his matted locks piled upward, seated on a lotus, joining his palms and bowing to the Blessed Amitābha, the Sage; so he should be drawn. A vidyādhara holding a censer in his hand gazes at the Blessed One. In this form it should be painted within a fortnight or twelve days. Having had a painting of this kind made, and having installed the painting near the stūpa, one should do everything there with this very mantra and recite it five hundred thousand times. At the end, keeping a fast through the night, one should make a great offering to the painting, recite over each of eight thousand jasmine flowers in full, and cast them at the feet of the Blessed One.

When one has done a hundred thousand in this way, in three sessions, at the end the Blessed One will grant the supreme. If the vidyādhara's own body blazes, or the painting moves and sways and the tip of the lamp flame grows, it means kingship. If one wishes to perform an accomplishment, whether retention of what one has heard, or supremacy in speech, or one performed on eye ointment, realgar and gorocanā, and one accomplishes it all before the painting, there will be three kinds of accomplishment.

This completes the great king of ritual manuals called Consecration on the Crown, arisen from the samādhi Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, having once again spoken of the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, spoke this great king of vidyās called Characterized by Light, within the Blessed Lady's great king of ritual manuals:

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya namo bipaśyāṃ śikhī biśvabhuḥ nma ārya abalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya mahāśānta prabhāya pramudita kāpacanāya nityotāba cittaya bhagabāna hṛdaya manusmara aciśmatyaṃ lokādhāto sarba bodhisatvā sarṣatma dhye bhāṣitaṃ buṇḍha satyaṃ dharma satyaṃ saṃgha satyaṃ anāghami satyaṃ srota ābanni satyaṃ yakṣa satyaṃ kuśmāṇḍā satyaṃ būrba bodhisatvāṃ hṛdaya manusmara he he he he he tve tve tve tve tve ra ra ra ra ra la la la la la oṃkāra prabhe bhebhyaṃ pañcaya bhaśritaṃ kalpa sarba buddha sarājataṃ tvameba rakṣaṃ baṃ datvā sira sva praṇāmya haṃ khaga khaga bija asara jatiya svāhā abalokiteśvarā bijaya svāhā

This great king of vidyās called Endowed with Rays, which has attained great power, accomplishes all minor rites by being read.

Then comes its means of accomplishment. Near a stūpa that contains relics, or on a mountain peak, or on the bank of a river flowing to the ocean, or in the middle of water, or on an island, eating milk and porridge, one should do everything with this very mantra and recite it a hundred thousand times; thus the preliminary approach will have been done. Then one should combine eye ointment, realgar and gorocanā, wrap them in a leaf of the aśvattha tree, and make offerings to a stūpa that contains relics. Sitting on a mat of kuśa grass in three sessions, one should recite over the substances for exactly twenty-one days. If they grow warm, give off smoke and blaze, it is accomplished. With the first, one brings others under one's power. With the second, one becomes invisible. With the third, one travels through the sky. If the painting shakes strongly, one gains a kingdom.

This completes the great king of ritual manuals called Endowed with Rays, arisen from the samādhi Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, once again meditating on the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, spoke the great king of vidyās called Lotus All-Illuminating, within the Blessed Lady's great queen of vidyās, the king of ritual manuals:

namaḥ subarna babhasāya tathāgatāya arhate sammyaksaṃbuddhāya beṣṭi koṭi yakṣa paribritiya nama ārya abalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā utddha jjaṭa prajvalitaya padma abhāsaḥ tthāgatā bacanena tvaya bhaśītaṃ kalpaṃ sarba kṣāya kīrtanāya sarba satvā hita anukarta sarba satvā parajitāya sarba satvā hitārthāya sarba siddhā catāya ganiḥ nma ārya abalokiteśvarāya tadyathā dhamani dhamani bhurbhuba oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ bipuriri pune svāhā bijaya paṭa paṭa kāra svāhā mahāyaśa anumune svāhā apratihata pacane svāhā

This is the great king of vidyās called Lotus All-Illuminating, which has attained great power. Just as the lotus illuminates all, so too with this heart essence of mine: merely by recalling it, all great fears will cease for one. Whoever performs it three times by day and night will purify all the five acts of immediate retribution committed over a long time. One will see dreams of many kinds.

The rite of the means of accomplishment is this. Having offered scent, incense and the like to a stūpa that contains relics, one should recite three hundred thousand times. At the end, keeping a fast through the night, for twelve months one should offer twelve portions of milk, twelve of curd, twelve full vases, twelve vases of honey, twelve vases of sesame and soup, incense in twelve gourd bowls, and lotuses in twelve bowls, and one should eat twelve meals of alms food. Then that evening, having performed such a rite of offering, one should smear saffron and offer there garlands of jasmine flowers like the color of the blue utpala. Before the stūpa, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight or on the full moon, holding a sword in the right hand and sitting on a mat of kuśa grass, one should recite eight thousand times. At the end, as the sign of accomplishment, one will hear from the sky the words "Excellent! Excellent!" Then the sword will blaze, and in that very instant one will have a divine body, together with a retinue. One lives for a great eon. Then, if the sword moves or the stūpa shakes, one will become a king of men. Or else whatever one desires and pursues is accomplished, and one gains the domain of accomplishment.

This completes the great king of vidyās called Lotus All-Illuminating, arisen from the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, once again meditating on the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, spoke the great king of vidyās called Conforming to the Eighty Minor Marks, within the Blessed Lady's great king of vidyās, the great king of ritual manuals.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya oṃ drijaṭāya namaḥ kmaṇḍaluhastāya namaḥ padmavibhuṣitāya namaḥ padmayānāyā namaḥ padmahastāyā namo maṇḍalaśikhāya namo aśītyanūbyaṃjana lakṣaṇāya namo asurā rekuñcitāya svāhā

This is the great king of vidyās called Conforming to the Eighty Minor Marks, which has attained great power, the ritual of Tārā that bestows great benefit. Whoever keeps it in mind will accomplish all their aims.

Next, the rite for its means of accomplishment. On the bank of a river that flows to the ocean, or on an island, or on an island in the ocean, wherever is convenient, one should make stūpas of sand, each the size of a sugata-span. Having set up the central life-pole, with scents, incense and so forth, as one's means allow, one should recite eight thousand times before each one. This continues until the eight thousand stūpas are complete. If afterward a stūpa blazes, one becomes a great lord. Then, when it blazes, one will be accomplished. From then on it serves for all rites.

If one wishes to bring under one's control a king, a king's minister, a woman or a man, one should offer scents and the like before the stūpa and recite eight thousand times. If this is done for seven days in three sessions, that person will become delighted. Whatever one asks for, one obtains. In time of fear, if one recites while keeping the sacred commitments, one will become free of fear. Minor rites are accomplished merely by reciting it; it performs all rites.

This completes the king of vidyās called Conforming to the Eighty Minor Marks, arisen from the samādhi Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, meditating on the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, spoke the great king of vidyās called Ornament of Qualities, within the Blessed Lady's great king of ritual manuals.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā vimuktiteje abhayadharma rasigunasāgarapadmemanasi prahmendrapratipannamahotyana tadyathā dāmana dāmani turu turu tiṣtha tiṣtha madhu madhu maddhi maddhi sarvakātyaṃ kuru svāhā

This is the one called Ornament of Qualities, which has attained great power and bestows every aim that all sentient beings desire. Whoever constantly keeps in mind this king of vidyās, Ornament of Qualities, will before long be able to perform all rites.

Next comes the rite for its means of accomplishment. Following the rite described earlier, one should have a painting made of the Blessed One Amitābha, the Sage. He should be painted seated in the cross-legged posture on a thousand-petaled lotus, teaching the Dharma. At his right side is the noble Avalokiteśvara, seated on a lotus, white in color, wearing a crown of matted locks, paying homage to the Blessed One. Below him is the practitioner, holding a censer in his hand, kneeling, as before.

Having installed the painting at a stūpa that contains relics, on a day when the lunar date, the karaṇa and the hour are auspicious, keeping the eight-branched restoration observance (poṣadha) and abiding in loving-kindness, one should make vast offerings and, on the full moon, recite ten thousand times. Having first done the approach with this, at that same stūpa one should recite over each lotus and offer it before the painting. One should offer a thousand each day, beginning on the first day of the month and continuing until the twelfth. Fasting for three nights, one should make vast offerings to the painting and then make a fire offering of three thousand white lotuses smeared with curd, honey and ghee. If the garland on the painting stirs, and the butter lamp swells and its light streams out elsewhere, this is the sign of accomplishment: one will obtain a great kingdom. If one does not succeed, one will obtain a province.

This fully completes the great king of vidyās called Ornament of Qualities, arisen from the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being, the noble Avalokiteśvara, once again meditating on the great king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, spoke the king of vidyās called Array of Sukhāvatī, within that great king of ritual manuals of the Blessed Lady.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya podhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya uddhaprajvalitajaṭāya sukhābatyaṃ pramocate tadyathā bhagabato amitābhāsāya pādāmūle mamaca hṛdaya pratigṛhṇa bhagabāna mama anu kampamusatāya tadyathā sādhu sadhuṃ suṣṭhu pariṣyamitilaṃghalaṅghajyotiṣpapati bibhudhapadmahastaya sume sume bisuma giri giriṇi svāhā

This great king of vidyās called Array of Sukhāvatī, which has attained great power, protects from all fears merely by being recited.

Its rite is as follows. In the open, with no roof overhead, beneath a single tree, one should make a stūpa about the size of a vase, and before it make a fire offering of a hundred thousand pieces of aloeswood. Whatever one makes the fire offering for, one obtains the best of it.

One who wishes to bring a king or a king's minister under control should make an effigy of salt before the stūpa and offer it into a fire of palāśa wood seven times at each of the three junctures of the day for three days; that person will then come under one's control.

If one wishes to bring a woman under control, then in an open field one should make a fire offering, into a fire of khadira wood, of white mustard seeds smeared with blood, together with smeared mustard seed and khadira, one thousand and eight times at each of the three junctures of the day for three days; she will then come under one's control.

On the sand of a river that flows to the ocean, one should make one thousand and eight stūpas, each about four finger-widths high, or about a span, or about the measure of a sugata-span. Having set up the life-pole in each, and with an assortment of offerings and the like, one should recite one thousand and eight times before each one. For as long as the one thousand and eight remain standing, one will obtain a thousand coins at a time.

If, on the shore of the ocean, before each stūpa, with the rite performed first, one recites a hundred thousand times, one will see the Blessed One, the noble Avalokiteśvara, who will grant whatever supreme boon one desires, and one will obtain whatever one seeks.

This completes the great king of vidyās called Array of Sukhāvatī, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, once again meditating on that same samādhi, spoke the king of vidyās called Endowed with Heroism, within the Blessed Lady's great king of ritual manuals.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā śiri bisiri smṛti bacane tejobadhani hara hara amukaṃ me basamāgacchaturamani biramaṇi birabāsi minisau tamutakhepātibarṇa svāhā

This, together with the great power it has attained, is the great queen of vidyās called Endowed with Heroism, which protects all sentient beings. Whoever constantly keeps in mind this vidyā, endowed with the heroism of the supreme sons of the Victor, will surely attain the accomplishment of wealth, in keeping with their effort and their wishes.

Next comes the rite for its means of accomplishment. One should have the Blessed One, the noble Avalokiteśvara, painted: Padmapāṇi on a lotus seat, his right hand granting fearlessness, adorned with every ornament. To his right is the practitioner, as before. Having offered scents, incense and garlands to that painting at a stūpa containing relics, and fasting day and night, on the full moon one should offer twelve bowls of milk porridge and present aloeswood incense. Then, seated on a mat of kuśa grass, one should recite one thousand and eight times. This will constitute the preliminary approach.

For the accomplishment of all rites, one should recite a hundred thousand times following this same rite. Afterward, having smeared a maṇḍala close before the painting, one should recite over each jasmine flower and scatter it on the maṇḍala. If one does this for seven days, in three sessions, until one thousand and eight are complete, then on the seventh day whomever one wishes will come under one's control. If one makes a fire offering of three hundred thousand pieces of black aloeswood before the painting, one will obtain a kingdom; if one does not succeed, a village.

This fully completes the great queen of vidyās called Endowed with Heroism, arisen from the samādhi Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of Ūrdhvajaṭā of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā.

Then again the bodhisattva, the great being Avalokiteśvara, meditating on that same king of samādhis, spoke the great king of vidyās called Perfect Bestowal of Fearlessness, within the Blessed Lady's great king of ritual manuals.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya dīptapiṅgale haripiṅgale asonitādhadrāle hi ehi mama paraṃ prayaccha svāhā

This, together with the great power it has attained, is the king of vidyās called Perfect Bestowal of Fearlessness.

Next, its rite. On cloth or on a panel, one should paint the noble Avalokiteśvara with lac dye, on a lotus seat, holding a lotus in his hand, perfectly bestowing fearlessness. The practitioner, too, is as before. If, before him, in three sessions, one makes a fire offering of a hundred thousand pieces of red sandalwood smeared with ghee, one will obtain a hundred pieces of gold. If one makes a fire offering seven hundred thousand times, one will obtain a kingdom.

Here is the mantra for producing rubies:

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā yige cchitve ca paripraṇa aiśratyaṃ dadāti me bajriṇi ghiṇi mohani mohaja jaṃbhani staṃbhani abhayapradi abhayapradi la la la la la la la la svāhā

This, which has attained great power, is the mantra that bestows rubies. Its rite: one should draw the noble Avalokiteśvara with red sandalwood. If, before him, one makes a fire offering of a hundred thousand red flowers smeared with ghee and honey, one will obtain eight rubies.

The rite of the food mantra is as follows:

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā prabyākarī prabhakāri jyotiṣmati sucibimucāya svāhā

This, together with the great power it has attained, is the mantra that bestows food and clothing. Its rite: one should draw the noble Avalokiteśvara with blood and cow bezoar. If, before him, one makes a fire offering of milk porridge smeared with ghee, up to a hundred thousand times, one will obtain food and clothing wherever one is.

This one bestows silver:

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā jvala jvala prajvala bhana ghana haṭāya sādaya sādaya ehi ehi phu phu phu phu ghu ghu phura svāhā

This, together with the great power it has attained, is the mantra that bestows silver. Its rite: one should paint the noble Avalokiteśvara with saffron. If, before him, one makes a fire offering of a hundred thousand nāgakesara blossoms smeared with curd, honey, and honey and ghee, one will obtain a hundred pieces of silver.

Also here is the mantra that abundantly bestows gold:

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bobhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā garuru phara bara barili svāhā

This, together with the great power it has attained, is the mantra that bestows gold. Its rite: at a stūpa containing relics, one should recite over each mallikā flower and scatter it at the foot of the stūpa. If one scatters eight thousand in three sessions, within a month one will obtain a hundred pieces of gold.

The rite of the painting is as follows. On cloth one should paint the Blessed One, the noble Avalokiteśvara, with his matted locks piled high, holding a water flask in his hand, seated on a lotus seat.

If one installs the painting in a town or in a hermitage in the wilds, beneath an aśvattha tree, in a clean place, and makes a fire offering of seven hundred thousand oblations of resin incense, the Blessed One will swiftly grant a kingdom.

With these five, then, this completes Perfect Bestowal of Fearlessness, arisen from the samādhi Endowed with Vastness, of the root ritual manual of the Blessed Lady Tārā.

Then the bodhisattva, the great being, the noble Avalokiteśvara, having once again meditated on the king of samādhis Endowed with Vastness, spoke the great king of vidyās called Arising of the Syllable Oṃ, within the Blessed Lady's great king of ritual manuals.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhyāsya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhasya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā amukte amukte cacchadane mādheni mādheni surudhi rutamāya dharī huhu huhu matha matha matha oṃ rapramukha pāla pāla mahāpāripāla teja namastute sarbaduṣṭatvaṃ bāsisātāṇimāne svāhā

This, together with the great power it has attained, is the great king of vidyās called Releasing the Tether of Saṃsāra. Whoever constantly keeps it in mind will not wander long in saṃsāra. By mere recitation it purifies the five acts of immediate retribution.

Next, the rite for its means of accomplishment. On cloth, as described before, one should paint the Blessed One, the noble Avalokiteśvara, moving through the sky, blazing with light on all sides, holding a lotus in his hand, his right hand granting fearlessness. The practitioner should be painted in his true bodily likeness, burning incense, his dress and appearance exactly as they are.

Then, having installed that painting in the place described before, and offering scents, flowers, incense and so forth with this very mantra, one should recite three hundred thousand times. This will constitute the preliminary approach. It purifies the five acts of immediate retribution. By reciting six hundred thousand times one will obtain what one has vowed.

If one wishes to bind malevolent piśācas and rākṣasas, one should encircle them with a cord of kuśa grass consecrated with eight thousand recitations, and wind it around the tree, house or other place where the malevolent ones dwell. All the malevolent ones will be bound. Malicious minds and malicious beings will be overpowered.

If one wishes to prepare an eye salve, one should make a full thousand oblations before the painting, place the salve within seven aśvattha leaves, and fumigate it with smoke; then those eyes will become equal to the eyes of a Victor, and one will live for three thousand years.
