In a charnel ground, if one performs ten thousand fire offerings of human flesh, all the piśācas, too, come under one's power. If one performs eight thousand fire offerings of mongoose hair, all the bhūtas, too, come under one's power. In a charnel ground, if one performs a fire offering of excrement, those seized by pūtanas are freed even by one's mind alone. If one performs a fire offering with blood, the ḍākinīs come under one's power. In a charnel ground, if one performs a fire offering of boḍḍaka, the piśācas will not come. If one performs a fire offering of snake sloughs, snakes flee.

Then the practitioner should make a torma and perform eight thousand fire offerings with kindling sticks of arka. A yakṣiṇī of fearsome, changing form will come. One should not be afraid, but, keeping the vidyā in mind, say, "Stay! Stay!" At that she grants a choice of one among three supreme boons: to become one's mother, sister, or wife. As a mother, she does everything that is to be done for a son. As a sister, she gives one coin each day. As a wife, she sports with him, and he will live for five hundred years.

When a vidyādhara's practice has failed, he should do this. At night, clean and dressed in clean clothes, having made protection, he makes offerings to the Buddha, the Blessed One, to the noble Avalokiteśvara, to Vajrapāṇi, and to the Blessed Lady (Tārā). Then, facing east, he offers incense to all the deities of the vidyā, and the vidyādhara should perform eight thousand fire offerings of poison mixed with blood. He lies down on a spread of kuśa grass. If he sees a youth holding a short spear, then the gandharvas have spoiled his substances. When he sees a brahmin, then the gods have spoiled them. When he sees Vajrasena, then the vajra family has spoiled the substances. When he sees Nanda, then the garuḍas have spoiled them. When the asuras have spoiled them, then no cause is seen. When the nāgas have spoiled them, then he sees a king of scent elephants. When the ancestors have spoiled them, then he sees them. When impurity has spoiled them, then he sees Maheśvara wearing an elephant hide. When the yakṣas have spoiled them, then he sees Maṇibhadra. When the piśācas have spoiled them, then he sees a naked man. When the bhūtas have spoiled them, then he sees a cloud. Kindling a fire with kindling sticks of arka, he should perform eight thousand fire offerings smeared with ghee and honey. When the fire offering is complete, the substances come back into his hands.

The fire offering for the gandharvas is this: in a secluded place one smears a maṇḍala with cow dung and also offers a torma to the Blessed One. Then, sitting on a mat of kuśa grass, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of kindling sticks of kāmāja smeared with curd, honey and ghee. When the fire offering is complete, the substances come back into one's hands.

The fire offering for the vajra family, too, is this: one worships a stūpa containing relics with scents, flowers, incense and the like, and also performs the torma rite for the Blessed One. Then, if the practitioner, facing east, performs eight thousand fire offerings with pellets of guggulu, the substances come back into his hands.

For the garuḍas, one smears a maṇḍala in a charnel ground and makes offerings, and also a torma, as far as one's means allow. If one performs eight thousand fire offerings of karavīra flowers and the like smeared with ghee, the substances come back into one's hands.

The fire offering for the asuras is this: one worships Maheśvara with various scents and also makes a torma for the Blessed One. Then, with the right side of the body turned toward the east, if one performs eight thousand fire offerings with kindling sticks of karavīra, the substances come back into one's hands.

The fire offering for the mātṛkās is this: having offered cooked food and a torma of meat, if one performs eight thousand fire offerings of rotten pork mixed with liquor, the substances come back into one's hands.

The fire offering for the yakṣas is this: in the presence of Vajrapāṇi one offers tormas of various kinds, and then, facing east, if one performs eight thousand fire offerings of arka flowers, the substances come back into one's hands.

The fire offering for the piśācas is this: in a charnel ground one smears a maṇḍala, and if one performs eight thousand fire offerings of nimba flowers smeared with sesame oil, the substances come back into one's hands.

The fire offering for the bhūtas is this: one smears a maṇḍala with charnel-ground ash and also offers a torma as far as one's means allow, and if one performs eight thousand fire offerings of beef, the substances come back into one's hands.

For the pretas, if one performs eight thousand fire offerings of nīmala, the substances come back into one's hands.

This completes the tenth chapter of the Blessed Lady, the Great Queen of Vidyās, the chapter on the characteristics taught by all the mātṛkās, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas and piśācas.

Even without having accomplished the vidyā, it serves for rites. When rain has not fallen, if one enters the water and recites the vidyā, rain will fall within seven days. For binding semen, it is done with a thread. For overcoming intoxication, with charnel-ground ash. For those who are bewitched, with lac. For one tormented by stabbing pain, one removes the pain with arjuna. With sesame oil, a vulture, and a cutting water knife, these three, one makes the fangs go in. With guggulu incense one drives them from their place. These things one can do even without accomplishment. Everything should be accomplished through this very Blessed Lady.

For instance, just as one keeps this as a master copy and reads it, so too this should be read by one wearing clean clothes, sitting on a mat of kuśa grass. If one reads this rite for seven days, there will be peace. If there is too much rain, one climbs onto an anthill and recites the Blessed Lady eight thousand times, and then it subsides.

The scents, flowers and incense that one offers summon all vidyās; they bind, paralyze, and cut; they slay all vidyās, terrify malicious minds, and bind mouths. With this one performs its rites. With saffron water one causes stupefaction. With a yellow substance one summons snakes. With white mustard seed, with what grows from the lotus root, and with fine flowers, one draws spirits out. With incense one makes them speak. With karavīra flowers one makes them enter the maṇḍala. Fumigating at once with agaru incense, one should apply these one thousand and eight rites of the Blessed Lady.

I shall explain the characteristics of the kindling sticks: root, middle, and tip. For the purpose of expulsion, one performs the fire offering with the trunk and the root. With the middle part, one who desires wealth does so. With the tip, it is for pacifying and enriching rites. For one who desires wealth: at the time of dawn the yakṣas roam about, and so it becomes the accomplishment of the rite of bestowing their wealth. One who wishes to expel, staying in the interval, should perform the fire offering of roots in the first part of the night. With sticks the length of a forefinger, smeared with poison and blood, one should perform the fire offering in a charnel-ground fire. After midnight the pretas roam about, and so from that one should accomplish fierce rites.

For the great accomplishment, one should perform the fire offering facing east, with kindling sticks a cubit long smeared with curd, honey and ghee. By that, the practitioner achieves his great accomplishment. For subjugation, one should perform the fire offering with kindling sticks of the bodhi tree, of this same forefinger length. If, for seven days at sunrise, one performs a fire offering of apāmārga kindling sticks smeared with blood, the person will die; it will not be otherwise. If one wishes to cause illness, performing a fire offering of pānāya pellets for seven days causes illness. It is accomplished by naming the person by name, and so it should be applied.

This is the eleventh chapter of the Blessed Lady, the Great Queen of Vidyās.

Then Vemacitrin, Lord of the Asuras, taught a rite of the Blessed Lady. At the entrance of a cave, in a charnel ground, the practitioner, wearing clean clothes, sits on a mat of kuśa grass facing the entrance of the cave and should recite the heart mantra of the Blessed Lady, She Who Goes in Equality, eight thousand times. Everything will open from its place. One should enter without hesitation and, keeping in mind the vidyā called Dispeller of Asuras, should take what is there. Having recited over a woman with delight, one should touch her, and she comes under one's power.

Then the practitioner who wishes to do this with the three should climb to a mountain peak and recite She Who Goes in Equality three hundred thousand times. Then he smears a maṇḍala the size of a cowhide with red sandalwood, makes protection, sits on a mat of kuśa grass facing the entrance of the cave, and, with the vidyā She Who Goes in Equality, should perform ten thousand fire offerings of apāmārga kindling sticks smeared with poison and blood. Then, when the fire offering is complete, he should recite over the ash and scatter it. The three will come here. He should enter without hesitation, and when the asura maiden sees him, she comes under his power. Then he should take the substances of accomplishment: whatever he desires, he should consecrate with the vidyā and take. With the wheel he becomes the universal monarch over all beings and all vidyādharas, and this lasts as long as the sun, the moon and the stars remain. Likewise, with realgar, a veda, an axe, a paṭṭaka, a śakti, that is, a short spear, a sword, a sword hilt, sandals, a knife, a thread, an implement carried for worship, a rosary, a Dharma seal and so on, he lives as long as the moon, the sun and the stars. He bows to no one except the Blessed Lady, the tathāgatas, the bodhisattvas abiding on the ten grounds, and the saṅgha of the Blessed One's śrāvakas, and he becomes a divine universal monarch.

Then, another method: what blocks all these mantras of the Blessed Lady is white mustard seed.

Then Vemacitrin, Lord of the Asuras, taught the sublime, supreme secret. Going to the mouth of an asura cavern and living on milk and barley meal, one should recite the heart mantra of the Blessed Lady, She Who Goes in Equality, a hundred thousand times. One will see the asura maidens. They give a sword or reveal some other accomplished substance, and by taking it one becomes a vidyādhara just as one wishes.

This is the twelfth chapter of the Blessed Lady, the Great Queen of Vidyās, taught by Vemacitrin, Lord of the Asuras.

From the great Avataṃsaka of the Bodhisattva Piṭaka, this is called "The Great Secret that Generates the Blessed Lady, Queen of Vidyās."

Then once more the great being looked upon the maṇḍala of the assembly endowed with everything, and with a completely pure intention, here in the King of Ritual Manuals, for the sake of accomplishing the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā, he spoke the great king of mantras, the vidyā mantra called Trailokyavijaya (Victorious over the Three Worlds). At that moment a ray of light called Perfectly Uniting All Nectars came forth from the heart of the great bodhisattva. That ray of light encircled hundreds of thousands of koṭis of niyutas of world systems endowed with everything, illuminated the beings there, and dissolved back into the body of the great bodhisattva.

What was it that was spoken at that moment?

namo ratna trayāya nama ārya abalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya ārolika

This is the supreme heart mantra called Trailokyavijaya. The practitioner should certainly and without fail apply it in the rite of accomplishing the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā. It turns back all that is harmful, exhausts all evil, brings in auspiciousness, and is praised by all the buddhas. That is its mantra.

At dawn, rising from one's seat and having become clean, one should consecrate a handful of water seven times and drink it facing east. One's karmic obscurations will be purified. In the King of Ritual Manuals of the Blessed Lady, all rites are accomplished through pacifying. One will remember without being harmed, and one will be powerful, majestic, and blessed by the gods. Likewise, for enriching rites, one should do these things on another day. In between, for fierce rites, when undertaking the varṇata, one should consecrate the ring finger seven times; so too for pacifying and enriching rites. For fierce rites, one should begin it by reciting on the forefinger. Whoever performs a rite in this way will gain accomplishment. At the time of recitation, one should consecrate one's own heart with this. Its accomplishment is declared to be certain. The practice for the sake of Tārā should be done just as it has been taught, and it is certainly swift.

For the intelligent practitioner, as for all vidyās, I, the king of vidyās of great power, have joyfully proclaimed my supremely virtuous mantra vidyā. The practitioner, too, should make protection and purification for himself, and then, constantly, here in this great king of vidyās, here in this great King of Ritual Manuals, I shall explain some rites of the sādhana procedure of the great Trailokyavijaya, the method by which the Blessed Lady Tārā is accomplished.

Those who undertake the practice must, as vidyādharas, generate the mind set on awakening and proceed with clear faith in the Three Jewels.

Further, this is its rite. At a stūpa containing relics, on a mountain peak, or anywhere else, in a clean place, before an image, eating milk and barley meal, or entirely giving up the feast foods of the practices of the individual vidyās, making complete offerings, whether keeping the poṣadha vows or not keeping them, one should recite two hundred and fifty thousand times. Then the preliminary practice will have been done. Having made offerings, for the approach one should, on the full moon of Vaiśākha or the full moon of the month of miracles, make offerings and recite eight thousand times. The heart mantra will be accomplished.

Then come the rites. On the full moon of the month of miracles one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of agaru kindling sticks smeared with curd, honey and ghee. With eight thousand flowers one will see the Blessed One. One should strike the image with the eight thousand flowers. Or else, if one again recites throughout the whole night, one will see the Blessed One. Then, having seen, one will always obtain five coins.

If for seven nights, at the three junctures of the day, one performs eight thousand fire offerings smeared with ghee, the king comes under one's power.

One makes an effigy of madana wood and adorns it with every ornament. Kindling a fire with kindling sticks of the royal tree, one pierces its feet with a skewer, and if one performs the fire offering eight hundred times at the three junctures, on the second day the person comes on foot.

One makes a śālabhañjikā figure six finger-widths tall out of aśoka wood. Staying on a mountain peak and eating milk and barley meal, one should recite three hundred thousand times. At the end, on the full moon, one makes offerings, fasts for three nights, places the figure on aśvattha leaves at a stūpa containing relics, and recites for as long as it takes until she comes. One should say, "Welcome!" If she says, "I shall grant a boon," she may become one's wife, sister, or companion. She provides food, clothing and coins for oneself and twelve others, and one will live for a thousand years.

When the moon is seized by the eclipse, one takes fresh butter from a cow of uniform breed and makes an effigy six finger-widths tall. Keeping to the prescribed food and fasting, one places it on aśvattha leaves and recites until the moon is released. For this there are three kinds of accomplishment. When it grows warm, one roams freely on foot, gains a life of five hundred years, and travels five hundred yojanas. One will certainly become invisible everywhere. When it smokes, one becomes invisible, does not touch the ground by twenty-four finger-widths, lives for a thousand years, and travels a thousand yojanas. The strength of ten men blazes forth, and one lives for two thousand years. Vidyādharas cannot overcome one.

One should perform ten thousand fire offerings of lotuses smeared with curd, honey and ghee. In the middle of the embers the form of Śrī (Lakṣmī), holding a lotus in her hand, appears. She grants a boon, and one should say, "Be my mother, sister, or companion." She will grant a thousand coins, and all illnesses will be completely pacified.

Observing the poṣadha vows and eating milk and barley meal, beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of barley and kindling sticks as before. All illnesses will subside.

Entering water up to the navel, one should recite three hundred thousand times. Then one sees all treasures. It shatters all magical devices. It paralyzes. It protects. It summons people as well. It revives the dead. It removes poison. It also pacifies. It summons. It gives a son to a barren woman. If one consecrates with it eight thousand times, one cannot be overcome by any other foe. If one makes protection at the king's gate, a boundary is sealed against enemies.

One should recite six hundred thousand times near a stūpa containing relics. Having clothed oneself in white cloth, one should recite until it blazes. One will fly together with a retinue of a thousand. One may perform rites of various kinds.

Bowing to the noble Avalokiteśvara, white as an autumn cloud, adorned with every ornament, wearing a crown of matted locks, and holding a white water pot, one should make great offerings to him and recite three hundred thousand times. It is accomplished by the mind.

In a clean place on the bank of a river, observing the poṣadha vows, one makes a stūpa containing the heart of dependent origination, makes offerings to it, and recites the heart mantra. In between, one makes stūpas again, and from sunset one recites until eight thousand recitations are reached. Then, by this rite, one becomes a universal monarch of vidyādharas. One goes to Sukhāvatī together with the noble Avalokiteśvara and sees the Buddha. One will remain for an eon.

If a vidyādhara wishes to bring a king or a king's minister under his power, let him perform eight thousand fire offerings of apāmārga kindling sticks smeared with ghee and honey, and the king comes under his power. To bring women and men under one's power, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of guggulu pellets in the three sessions, and they come under one's power. One should perform eight thousand fire offerings with pellets of agaru, and all people will be pleased. Even in Rājagṛha one will become the foremost of speakers.

Placing sweet flag in the mouth, one should recite until the three kinds of accomplishment occur. When it grows warm, it makes one keen of mind and courageous. When it smokes, it brings invisibility and radiance.

The vidyādhara should recite one million six hundred thousand times before the noble Avalokiteśvara. Living on alms, bathing at the three times of day, and sitting in the hero's posture, one should recite five hundred thousand times. Then the accomplishment one wishes for in one's mind arises: one dwells together with the gods and obtains whatever one desires.

Then, placing realgar in a white casket wrapped round with letters, one should recite until the three kinds of accomplishment occur. When it grows warm, one becomes keen of mind. When it smokes, one becomes invisible and radiant.

The vidyādhara should recite one million six hundred thousand times before the noble Avalokiteśvara. Living on alms, keeping silence, and lying on a spread of kuśa grass, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of nāgakesara. On the seventh day one obtains the maiden one desires. One should perform eight thousand fire offerings smeared with ghee; on the seventh day one becomes supremely keen of mind and courageous. If one performs eight thousand fire offerings with nandyāvarta flowers, women and men are roused.

To bring someone under one's power, one fasts day and night on the full moon, kindles a fire with kindling sticks of the bodhi tree before the noble Avalokiteśvara, and performs eight thousand fire offerings of sesame; then the person comes under one's power. Having made pegs of khadira wood four finger-widths long, one plants them in the four directions, and the boundary is sealed.

One who wishes to accomplish an eye salve of realgar should eat milk and barley meal for a month, and on the eighth day of the dark fortnight fast for three nights. At a stūpa containing relics, before the image, one places it on four aśvattha leaves, pressing it down with the fourth, and recites until the three kinds of accomplishment occur. In a lawsuit, by reciting the vidyā and reciting it facing the opponent, one wins. If one recites in front of an angry person, he becomes thoroughly cowed.

If one wishes to bring a widow under one's power, one fasts for three nights on the eighth day of the dark fortnight and performs eight thousand fire offerings of white flowers before the noble Avalokiteśvara; she then grants whatever boon one seeks.

Binding the circle of all fanged creatures with white mustard seed: when one goes among lions, tigers, robbers or elephants, one should call it to mind. Observing the poṣadha vows, bathing at the three times of day, generating the mind set on awakening, abiding in loving-kindness, and wishing to benefit all sentient beings, one recites three hundred thousand times before a stūpa containing relics and an image.

Then one should have the noble Avalokiteśvara painted on fine, unworn cloth: white as an autumn cloud, seated on a lotus, holding a lotus in his hand, adorned with every ornament, wearing a crown of matted locks, with a lower garment of silk and cotton. Having installed the painting before a stūpa containing relics and an image, one should recite three hundred thousand times. Then, on the full moon, one makes great offerings to the Buddha, the Blessed One, and then fasts for three nights, and should perform twenty-four thousand fire offerings of ariṣṭa kindling sticks smeared with curd, honey and ghee. Rays of light come forth from the noble Avalokiteśvara, the earth quakes, the sound of great drums resounds, the flames of the butter lamps grow tall, the bunches of flowers sway, and the painting moves. Then one is accomplished. From then on, one's rites become auspicious. He bestows wealth. One delights in all the accomplishments. Everything remains under one's power.

Then, if one wishes to accomplish an eye salve, one wraps srotāñjana salve in aśvattha leaves and recites until the three kinds of accomplishment occur.

One should have a staff made of red sandalwood, sixteen finger-widths or ten finger-widths long. Before the noble Avalokiteśvara one should recite three hundred thousand times, until the three kinds of accomplishment occur. Then one should have it carry out whatever is to be done.

Beginning from the month of miracles, one who keeps the poṣadha vows should bathe at the three times of day, change clothes three times, and recite a hundred thousand times. One should have the deity painted on smooth cloth: white as an autumn cloud, holding a lotus in his hand, adorned with every ornament, at a stūpa containing relics, as though breathing in its fragrance, both hands filled with jasmine, wearing a crown of matted locks, with a white water pot, and holding a garland of lotuses. Then, beginning from the eighth day of the bright fortnight, one should make fire offerings of white lotuses before the stūpa containing relics and the painting, and recite one million two hundred thousand times.

Another rite: for the vidyādhara who wishes to practice, the king of rites for destroying the vināyakas is this. One performs eight thousand fire offerings of mustard seed smeared with pungent sesame oil, and they flee a thousand yojanas. Then one should accomplish the vidyā. Used otherwise, it destroys poison.

If one wishes to bind another's vidyā, one names it by name, consecrates the fringe of a cloth eight hundred times, and ties a knot. Even if the Buddha, the Blessed One, were to come in person, even he could not untie it until the vidyādhara unties it.

One who wishes for pacification should offer eight thousand jasmine flowers, and there will be peace. Living on alms, one should recite ten million times, and one will directly see the Blessed One Amitābha seated on a lotus seat. By reciting this vidyā ten thousand times, one destroys illness that has struck another. If, living on alms, one recites ten million times, one sees the Blessed One, and he grants three boons: power over all beings, invisibility, and entry into the dwellings of the asuras. If one climbs to a mountain peak and recites ten million times, all the gods come under one's power and always grant one sight of them. At a lotus lake one should perform ten thousand fire offerings of white lotuses, and the king comes under one's power. By merely reading it, everything is accomplished, except what is undertaken out of craving.

Fasting for three nights, one recites over a mirror and shows it, with ash from the fire offering, to a boy or a girl, and they see without end. Smearing a thumbnail with nail dye and scented sesame oil, one should show it to children. Filling a vessel with water, one should show it to everyone; everyone sees, and one brings all beings under one's power. By reciting seven times, one brings them under one's power.

If, having entered a village, one seeks food, one should recite a thousand times, and one will obtain food. In fear of robbers, by reciting one paralyzes them. By reciting ten million times, one becomes capable of every rite.

When the moon is seized by the eclipse, during that interval one takes a root of hakamika, presses it between one's joined palms, and recites until the three kinds of accomplishment occur. When the sun is seized by the eclipse, one should recite before the noble Avalokiteśvara until the three kinds of accomplishment occur.

If one goes to a river and, eating milk and barley meal, recites ten million times, all the nāgas come and come under one's power. Then the practitioner should bring forth the accomplishment of the nāga realms: in all the abodes of the nāgas he roams as he pleases, as if in his own home. Going to an abode of the nāgas and filling an alms bowl with milk porridge, one should recite the vidyā until a seven-headed nāga comes. They also give jewels. They bring out the royal treasures in the earth, or seal them. Then one should accept it wholeheartedly; if one does not accept, the five bonds of the nāgas will come.

With this very mantra one should offer twenty-one thousand recitations on the bank of a river. If the flowers on the great flowing river circle to the right, the vidyādhara should know, "I am accomplished." Then he comes and goes within the water.

One should recite ten million times at a stūpa containing relics or near a bodhi tree. One becomes a king endowed with moral discipline and perfect eloquence, lord of Jambudvīpa, a universal monarch of vidyādharas with great miraculous powers and great might, for as long as the practice lasts. This is the second. In this second, a lotus comes forth from the mouth of the Buddha, the Blessed One, with joyful petals and a delightful fragrance. By taking that lotus, one feeds on joy as one's food, is endowed with youth, has curling, coiled hair, has the appearance of a sixteen-year-old, and has more splendor, bliss and happiness than the young gods. One lives for a hundred thousand koṭis of years and flies.

One should perform a hundred thousand fire offerings of vāsaka flowers, and one obtains a thousand gold coins. If one kindles a fire of khadira wood and performs eight thousand fire offerings of aśoka flowers smeared with ghee, the yakṣas come under one's power. If, while reciting, one performs eighty thousand fire offerings mentally, one becomes a vidyādhara whose mind is one-pointed, whose body is like fire, and whose strength and power to overcome others are unobstructed. Again one should recite ten million times; one will directly see Avalokiteśvara and obtain whatever one wishes. Through eight million recitations in the mind, one becomes invisible. One flies eight yojanas. One also travels a hundred yojanas below. One also brings things up out of the earth. One sees all treasures.

One who wishes to bring the yakṣiṇīs under his power should smear a maṇḍala beneath an aśoka tree and say, "Please partake of this!"

Furthermore, it becomes the rite of Trailokyavijaya. One should first carry out the preliminary practice, and, observing the poṣadha, one should bathe at the three times of day. Having made a maṇḍala for the Tathāgata, the arhat, one should recite three hundred thousand times. When the recitation is complete, still observing the poṣadha, one should make offerings as far as one is able, and on the full moon of the month of Āṣāḍha one should eat the almsfood prescribed by the Saṅgha. With very fine food free of meat, having smeared a maṇḍala in a perfumed chamber, one should make offerings of scents, flowers and incense to a reliquary containing relics, or to an image. Then, sitting cross-legged on spread kuśa grass, one should offer, with the almsfood, the immeasurable recitation of the rite. Up to this point is the second accomplishment. At that time one sees the Blessed One, and one obtains whatever one wishes and desires.

The rite of Trailokyavijaya, the rite of the great king of vidyās Trailokyavijaya from the root rite of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā Ūrdhvajaṭā, is complete.

Then again the Great Being, once more entering into the meditative absorption that fully stirs all the vidyās, spoke the chapter on the vidyā of the ritual of the means of accomplishment. By reciting it, accomplishment is swiftly achieved: one is accomplished by oneself, and one's aims are achieved even when distracted. In short, however it is applied, just so will it be accomplished, and one should employ it accordingly.

Moreover, here the vidyā is:

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo vidyādevatāya namo vidyādevatānāṃ nama sarvasyaiva vīdyākulavaṃśasye tadyathā sarva artha vighna vināśaya āhari hare hare vihare pihātejavimale abhaye calo stambhani puṣkare śuddhe mukke mukke vikurvite prabhāsvare ālokitebhyaḥ vilākala sarva satva avalokani svāhā

These rites are accomplished by this vidyā. At the time of approach and at the time of accomplishment, one should first of all protect oneself with it. Companions bound by the precepts, too, are protected in every way when water over which it has been recited seven times or three times is poured on the crown of their heads. Scents, flowers, incense, praises and the rest should also be done with this very vidyā. When one has taken up the painted cloth, it is also with this very vidyā that one protects the deities and the painted cloth on every side, keeps the site of the painted cloth unmixed with other colors, offers the welcoming water to the invited deities, and establishes them; and oneself and one's helpers should perform the binding of the liquid with it. Through this binding all vināyakas are crushed and every place is protected.

With this very vidyā one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of white mustard seed smeared with warm sesame oil. Oneself or one's helpers may do it, twenty-one times, without fail in whichever direction is used for the prior approach, for accomplishment, or for the pacifying, enriching or fierce rites. Or else, elsewhere, on an open plain, or on a piece of ground where the Blessed One is to be accomplished, or where other rites are to be done, one should first clean that place. In this way, for purifying the torma, protecting oneself, protecting others, pouring water, and in short for accomplishment and whatever rite there may be, one should perform the protection and the rest with this.

The protection vidyā is:

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya namo bhagavatyai tārāyai āgaccha devi padmahastena vade padmahaste yaśovati roṣaṇa śīghraṃ āgaccha mahadevigi mahāvigi hara hara sara sara cala cala āgaccha āgaccha bhagavate idaṃ gandha puṣpa mālya sarvanīyaṃ prayacchatha buddha satyena dharmastyena saṃgha satyena svāhā

With whichever is the first vidyā, one should apply it to the maṇḍala according to the maṇḍala ritual. With this vidyā one offers aloeswood incense; with the vidyā stated earlier, recited three or seven times, one does the cleaning; and having consecrated with it twenty-one times, for accomplishment one should recite the vidyā.

One should invite the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā:

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhīsatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavatyai ārya tārāyai arhatte sugandha mālya priye cantra cantramati gandhanulepanāṃ pratīcchi svāhā

With this one offers the welcoming water, and also scent and a seat.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya nama ārya tārāyai hili hili mili mili mahāprabhāye prahmasumanonuruha hara hara sara sara kara kara devi prasādha kuru pratīcchatha puṣpa svāhā

This is the flower vidyā; with it one should offer the flowers.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavatyai ārya tārāyai bodhisatvāya mantra manusmar sarva deva priye bhagavati avalokini siddha siddha prathāne buddha satyena dharma satyena saṃgha satyena svāhā

This is the incense vidyā.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgataya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavate ārya tārā dūte vajra dhuna anujai vegi vegi dhuru dhuru sarva jīva priye buddhā satyena dharma satyena saṃgha satyena svāhā

This is the torma vidyā.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākaruṇikāya namo bhagavatye ārya tārāyai apratihate bhagavate āhare hare padmabhasini śītāṃge śetaphuje dhume dhume buddha satyena dharma satyena saṃgha satyena svāhā

This is the lamp vidyā. In the same way, one should apply this vidyā.

The vidyā of the ritual of the means of accomplishment of Tārā, the same for all, for the prior approach and for accomplishment, is:

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavate ārya tārāyai tadyathā āgama āgama gaganatala saṃpraco dityai sarva vidyā dhara viśodhani svāhā

Having recited this vidyā twenty-one times over water, one should sprinkle oneself from a vase or the like: this is the bathing vidyā. This same one is also the vidyā for bathing the deities.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavate ārya tārāyai dhudhume dhudhume khukhume khukhume nāśuddha siddhikañcani śuddhikāre śucani svāhā

The practitioner should always recite this vidyā over his clothes once or seven times and then put them on. Otherwise the vināyakas will certainly show themselves. The practitioner must do this without fail.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavate ārya tārāyai śāntiṃ me karohi śantimāte śiśānta niśānta kalyāṇiniśānta vijaye devi varade svāhā

Having recited this vidyā seven times over oneself, one should go to sleep. Then one will not see vināyakas in one's dreams.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavati ārya tārāyai sūryata upari travyaṃ dharaṇi bandhiti kardhaśodhani kucamālini śutraviśodhani svāhā kuśaviśodhani svāhā

When one has tied twenty-one knots with kuśa grass, the binding of the liquid is accomplished.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavata ārya tārāyai haripiṅgali hari hari hibhagaphapati acala pratiṣṭhate rakṣa rakṣa māṃ kuśapiṇḍama basthitasya buddha satyena dharma satyena dharma satyena saṃgha satyena svāhā

Having consecrated a mat of kuśa grass with this vidyā, one should sit down on it.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavate ārya tārāyai diśiva diśibandhani sudevi suprasāste suru suru muru muru hasta kalabala kalabala baba hela hela kuru kuru buddha satyena dharma satyena saṃgha satyena gandha gandha vimale svāhā

This is the binding of the maṇḍala.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya namo bhagavate ārya tārāyai jala jala jala kṣobhaya naśani jalaśodhani samiriṇi jalahāsiṇi viśodhaṇi svāhā

This is the vidyā for rinsing the mouth (ācamana). The practitioner who desires accomplishment must apply this vidyā to himself.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavate ārya tārāyai sarva devāsumante asaṃgatāre asaṃgavimu asaṃgatimukta vimukta vijaye nirmālyai aparikalpeni puṣpa gandha viśodhani viśoṣaya hidamaṇi damani svāhā

With this vidyā one should clear away the remains of the offerings.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya namo bhagavate ārya tārāyai sarva satvā krita prikrita prau kdya krita sakaledase sakalo viśodhani svāhā

With this vidyā one should offer the food offering.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśrarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya namo bhagavati ārya tārāyai svapnapaṇi barjā garjā mirśaya pratyakṣaṃ bā evaṃ byāhāra kathāya svāhā

Having made offerings to the Blessed Lady with this vidyā, one should kindle a fire with khadira wood. If one then performs one thousand eight hundred fire offerings of nūlakavarti smeared with ghee, she will make revelations in dreams.

namo ratnatrayāya namo bhagavate amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavate ārya tārāyai ehi bhagavāna ārya avalokiteśvarā bhatīna ma bhayaṃ kara bālā nāma bhāyaṃ dada bhaktanā marthaṃ kara atraṇīnāṃ trayaka duḥkhitānāṃ saukhyaṃ kara mama bhagavate manukaṃsaṃ karehi bhagavāna āgaccha āgaccha imaṃ gandha puṣpa bali dhupañceta gṛhna tadyathā prasāde prasādevati mahā devi mahāprabhe sūryaprabhe amoghe amoghasati yaśovati amoghasaṃdarśana amoghavimalaṃ amoghahalaṃ cala cala sar sar hara hara traye himaṃ siddhirame dad svāhā

A capable practitioner should offer scents, flowers and torma with this vidyā, and at the time of approach and the time of accomplishment, or whatever else there may be, such as fruits, all of it should be offered with this very vidyā. With it one purifies the deities; and the virtuous dreams, the offerings, the praises, the practitioner's reading of the scripture, the work on stūpas and all the rest should be offered with this very vidyā.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāyatathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya namo bhagavate ārya darāyai tadyathā mara mara bandha bandha hana hana pura pura lala lala rara rara cala cala khakha khakha paca paca tiṣṭha tiṣṭha buddha satyena dharma satyena saṃgha satyena svāhā

With ash empowered by this vidyā, the practitioner's maṇḍala is bound.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya namo bhagavate ārya tārāyai tadyathā hiri hiri miri miri kiri kiri ghiri ghiri ghuru ghuru vara vara dara dara gaccha gaccha bhagavāna ārya avalokiteśvaraya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya yathāsukhaṃ

With this vidyā, together with the mudrā of a handful of flowers, the deity is bidden to go: it is the vidyā for requesting departure.

namo ratnatrayāya namaḥsarva devani namo vidyādevānāṃ nama ārya avalokiteśarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya ehi bhagavate mahārakṣasi caseṭi īṭi miṣṭi asurapramardani ekajaṭi tirākṣasi sahita devi ma ca ma sā vihethiya kirisiti rākapāli karapari kāmārikaṃ para kālicchaṭa priye mahākapāli caṇḍali mahācaṇḍali mahācaṇḍali siddhi sarva artha sādhani sarva vighna praṇāsani svāhā

This is the rākṣasī called Ekajaṭī. In her presence one should smear a maṇḍala, and each day, having consecrated scents, flowers, torma and incense with this vidyā, one should make offerings to her. One should speak these words: "May all obstructors become unable to move against me! And deal with the obstructors for me!" For such a practitioner there will be no obstructors. Whatever accomplishment the practitioner undertakes will be free of obstructors. Otherwise, she crushes them.

These vidyās of the ritual of the means of accomplishment are accomplished through reciting the King of Ritual Manuals. However they are applied here, so do they accomplish all the practitioner's rites. Thus it should be understood.

The chapter on the sequence of the ritual of the means of accomplishment, from the root ritual manual of the Blessed Lady, the noble Tārā Ūrdhvajaṭā, is complete.

Then again the Great Being gazed upon the maṇḍala of the assembly, filled with all sentient beings, and, all sentient beings having become fully visible, he entered into the meditative absorption that stirs all the vidyās and spoke the vidyā of the means of accomplishment of the Great Being:

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya hāre svāhā

With this vidyā, living on alms on a mountain peak, one should recite the vidyā eight thousand times in three sessions at a stūpa or at home. Keeping silence, eating milk and barley meal or living on alms, and sleeping on spread kuśa grass, within three months or one month one sees the goddess Tārā together with the noble Avalokiteśvara. Whatever boon one asks for, whether kingship, invisibility, entering into caves, the transfer of treasure, or lordship of a country, whatever one asks for, one obtains, and always obtains. Even without having accomplished it, the vidyā serves for utterly destroying, for reducing to dust, for suppressing, for expelling, for bearing weapons, and for destroying all the mechanical devices of caves; and having protected oneself with it, if one goes into battle one is victorious. If one protects others with it, it performs every deed of accomplishment.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya podhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre tāre svāhā

With this vidyā, at the time when the moon is seized by Rāhu, keeping a fast for three nights, whether one has done the prior approach or not, one should kindle a fire with kindling sticks of the bodhi tree at a stūpa containing relics. If one performs eight thousand fire offerings of white jasmine flowers, one obtains a hundred thousand pieces of silver, or else one has a vision.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre tuttāre ture svāhā

With this vidyā, beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight, one should make the excellent painted image described earlier. At the end, on the day of the full moon, having offered scents, incense, torma and flowers, one should recite it eight thousand times in three sessions. Keeping a fast for three nights, one should kindle a fire with kindling sticks of a tree with milky sap and perform eight thousand fire offerings of blue utpala flowers smeared with curd, honey and ghee. Then the sound "Accomplished! Accomplished!" will arise in the sky, or else the painted cloth will move. By such signs one becomes accomplished, and one obtains lordship over a country, a village, a town or a kingdom, each in turn.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā ture ture svāhā

Having recited this vidyā a hundred thousand times, when the moon or the sun is seized by Rāhu, one should place the substance inside seven aśvattha leaves, press it between one's radiant joined palms, and recite until it grows warm, gives off smoke, and blazes. When it has grown warm, one brings others under one's power. While it is smoking, one becomes invisible and seizes a sixth share. When it blazes, one travels through the sky. One will be born among the gods of diverse bodies, with unobstructed strength and vigor, the color of the rising sun, with hair curled and coiled, having the form of one who is twice eight years old, and living for ten thousand years.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā ture ture svāhā

With this, having made a ring of iron obtained under Puṣya, one should recite a hundred thousand times at a stūpa containing relics, perform the rite of scents, flowers and torma, and accomplish it. Taking it up while it is smoking, one becomes invisible. One seizes a sixth share. One will live for five thousand years.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre tārāyai bhagavati svāhā

If one consecrates sesame oil with this vidyā eight times and anoints with it, it makes wounds vanish, takes away feeling of pain, and removes stabbing pain.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākaruṇikāya tadyathā tāre tāre tuttāre svāhā

Having fully recited this vidyā a hundred thousand times, one should scatter water over which it has been fully recited seven times. The jaws of makaras, turtles and the like are then bound.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalogiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre tāre svāhā

This vidyā performs all the courses of action of the great rites. Having recited it a thousand times over sesame oil, one should have the oil given. If it is given for colic, for diseases of the private parts, for retention of urine, and for cramping of the loins, one becomes free of disease.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā ture svāhā

With this vidyā, by means of a cord, one frees people from the fevers of piśācas, from the fevers of bhūtas, and it serves to crush the grahas. For a woman in labor, if one recites it eight hundred times over sesame oil and anoints her navel or loins, she will be free of pain.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre muḥsvāhā

Having consecrated them with this vidyā eight hundred times, one should place kumbhira, vāraṇi, ananta, betaśi, brāhmī, sweet flag and brihati, well mixed with honey, in a copper vessel, and recite from the time the eclipsed moon is seen until it is released. By eating this one becomes supremely intelligent. When going into battle, recite this vidyā eight hundred times and tie it on the arm! One will have great strength.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre tāre mulu mulu svāhā

With this vidyā, beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight and keeping a fast for three nights, one should perform, beneath an aśvattha tree, a hundred thousand fire offerings of yutika and karṇikara flowers smeared with milk, curd and ghee. One obtains a hundred pieces of silver, or else one has a vision. On the full moon, keeping a fast for three nights, one should go to a river at midnight and perform a hundred thousand fire offerings with fragrant flowers. One obtains five hundred coins, or else one has a vision. With this, at the time when the moon is seized by Rāhu, at a stūpa containing relics, one should grind somarāja fruits into a fine powder and make pills mixed with ghee and honey. Wrapping them inside seven aśvattha leaves and pressing them with the hand, one should recite until they blaze. Eat them! One will retain whatever one hears.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre tāre ture ture dara dara svāhā

With this vidyā, keeping a fast day and night, one should perform the rite of offering in the presence of the Blessed One. Then, going to a river that flows to the ocean, eating milk and barley meal and keeping the poṣadha in that place, one should offer a hundred thousand white lotuses in bloom. One will see treasures.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhaya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā tāre tāre tuttāre tuttāre svāhā

This is the vidyā of the noble Tārā called She Who Is Endowed with Eloquence.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāyi arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākaruṇikāya tāre tāre tuttāre tuttāre svāhā

This is the vidyā of the noble Tārā called Bestower of Twofold Light.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tāre ture ture svāhā

This is the heart essence of the Lamp.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā tāre tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is the vidyā of the noble Tārā called Accomplisher of All Great Rites.

Then, with these vidyās, there is a partial ritual of supreme accomplishment: however they are applied, just so do they accomplish. Thus it should be understood just as it is. In short, for great dangers and for minor rites as well, accomplishment comes through reciting them. In this ritual too, one who wishes to accomplish the vidyā should purify the whole body with the five products of the cow, using that vidyā, and, beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight, should recite eight thousand times in three sessions in the manner described.

or else, up to the full moon, even a hundred thousand times will do. Then the prior approach will have been accomplished. After that, at the end, keeping a fast day and night and making vast offerings, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings into a fire of khadira wood, using kindling sticks of black aloeswood six finger-widths long smeared with curd, honey and ghee, or smeared with turuṣka sesame oil. One then becomes capable of all rites.

Then one turns to the rites. At the end, keeping a fast for three nights, one should consecrate a thread spun by a maiden ten thousand times, at a stūpa containing relics or in one's own house. If one ties it on one's arm, one becomes invisible.

If one installs the painted cloth at a stūpa containing relics, kindles a fire with khadira charcoal and performs fire offerings of thirty thousand lotuses, one sees the goddess in her own form. Whatever one asks for, one obtains.

Beginning on the first day of the month and continuing up to the fifteenth, keeping a fast for three nights, one should make vast offerings to a stūpa containing relics. If one then kindles a fire with kindling sticks of udumbara and performs a thousand fire offerings with oblations of ghee, one obtains a village.

At a river that flows to the ocean, one should have a thousand stūpas made. Each day one consecrates them at the stūpas eight thousand times and offers scents, flowers and the like to them, until the last stūpa blazes; then one should know that the Blessed One has come. When the Blessed One comes, the earth shakes and a fragrant breeze arises. As long as she remains near in her own form, one should recite. She grants whatever boon one asks for. In the presence of the Blessed One one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of pieces of khadira leaves. Each day one obtains a village.

Going to a wilderness, one should recite the vidyā ten million times. Living on alms, one should perform twenty thousand fire offerings with the dung of wild cattle smeared with curd, honey and ghee. Then the gods will come, having taken the form of does; one should not be afraid of them. They will also bestow treasure, and one should accept it. One should say, "Enjoy it yourself!" They give kingship, wealth, grain and jewels; one should always dedicate these to the Three Jewels and offer them to the Blessed One.

Having entered a wilderness, one should recite the vidyā a hundred thousand times. If, in the presence of the Blessed One installed on aloeswood, one performs a thousand fire offerings of patsalaṇḍika wood smeared with curd, honey and ghee, a tawny wish-granting cow will come. One should again perform twenty thousand fire offerings of patsalaṇḍi. When it has come, it is accomplished, and it gives milk for a thousand years.

In front of the painted cloth described earlier, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of jasmine flowers smeared with ghee and honey. Within six months one obtains a thousand gold coins, or else more than a thousand paṇas. One should perform eight thousand fire offerings of kumuda lilies. Through devotion to stūpas containing relics and to the Buddha, the gods grant boons.

Having made offerings to the noble Avalokiteśvara, one should consecrate white mustard seed seven times and scatter it in battle; and by reciting this same vidyā a thousand times one becomes able to bring all beings under one's power.

On the thirteenth day of the bright half of the fortnight of miracles, having made offerings of scents, flowers and incense, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings with blossoming flowers and oblations of ghee. Taking the ash, one makes a mark on the foreheads of others and enters villages and towns; all come under one's power.

From the fourteenth of the dark half up to the fifteenth, keeping a fast for one day, one should smear a square maṇḍala beneath a vaṭa tree, offer scents and incense, make offerings to the noble Avalokiteśvara, and offer torma to the yakṣas. Then one should take a human bone and have a trident made of it. Throwing it seven times with the left hand, and keeping a fast for three nights, if one performs eight thousand fire offerings of jasmine flowers, the trident will blaze. Then one becomes accomplished, and whatever one emanates at will comes to be.

In a temple, when the moon or the sun is seized by Rāhu, at a stūpa containing relics or in a house of images, one should take one palam of ghee from a tawny cow with a calf of the same color, and place it in a golden vessel at the stūpa containing relics. Having made offerings to the Blessed One, one should cover it from above with kuśa grass, so as not to look at the moon, and recite. While it is warm, one should drink it: one brings all beings under one's power. When it has thickened, one should drink it: one becomes invisible. When it is blazing, one should drink it: one travels through the sky.

For six months, having done the preliminary practice, eating cow's urine and barley meal, one should practice the vow of silence. By constantly reciting the vidyā of the Blessed Lady, one obtains a hundred gold pieces without asking.

One should begin in the fortnight of miracles and continue for a year. Making offerings in the presence of the noble Avalokiteśvara and likewise presenting scents, flowers and incense, and observing the eightfold poṣadha, when the year is complete one will be accomplished. The Blessed One binds the painted cloth.

Having made offerings to the Blessed One, from the first day of the month up to the full moon one should make especially abundant offerings and live on alms; then the words "It is accomplished!" are uttered. By performing eight thousand fire offerings with oblations of ghee, one's adversaries are pacified.

In the fortnight of miracles, having made offerings to the Buddha, the Blessed One, and likewise presented scents, flowers, incense and the like to the noble Avalokiteśvara, one should perform fire offerings of a hundred thousand flowers of the conch-flower plant smeared with iguta oil. Villages, towns, regions, elephants, horses, cattle and buffalo come under one's power.

Then again, if one wishes to bring down a divinatory vision (prasena), for seven nights one should eat milk and barley gruel. For one night, observing the poṣadha fast, one should fill a lamp to the brim with pure ghee, light the lamp with fresh white butter, and show it to a boy or a girl. In that same place, having set up the painted image, one should sleep on a spread of kuśa grass. In a dream one sees twenty thousand measures of wealth. Half of it should be devoted to the Three Jewels; so it is said.

Before the painted image, beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight until the full moon, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings each day. One should make offerings with scents, flowers, incense and the like. At the end, fasting for three nights and keeping the vow of silence, one should recite the vidyā; then, in the fortnight of miracles, one should go to a highway and stay at a dwelling of bhūtas. One should say, "Bestow!" Taking a measure of white mustard seed and empowering it with mantra twenty-one times, one should scatter it in the ten directions and below. Then the supreme is revealed to oneself.

Likewise, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, one should enter a temple and recite the vidyā a thousand times before the Blessed One. Having made offerings of scents, flowers and the like and performed the torma rite, one then sees in a dream the Blessed One wearing a crest of matted locks.

In the bright fortnight of the month of Vaiśākha, eating milk and barley gruel, one should make offerings of scents, flowers and the like to a stūpa containing relics, and hold a feast each day. Four vases full of water, filled completely with all the medicines and seeds, should be set out. Each night one should empower them eight thousand times, and then bathe a boy and a girl, until young are born in a crow's nest. The aim of kingship or the aim of wealth is accomplished within half a month.

On the eighth day of the dark fortnight, having worshiped the Blessed Lady and presented scents, flowers, incense and the like, one should kindle a fire with kindling sticks from a milky-sap tree and perform eight thousand fire offerings of hundred-petaled flowers. For a month, inexhaustible food and drink will appear.

Taking ash from a charnel ground, one should recite over it seven times and place it on one's own forehead or on the head of another; if one then enters a village, everyone comes under one's power. By recitation one frees from bonds. It breaks shackles. It wears through seven layers of hide.

One should perform a hundred thousand fire offerings of mālikā flowers smeared with curd, honey and ghee. Eating cow's urine and barley gruel, within six months one obtains as many coins as one wishes.

Beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight, one should perform a thousand fire offerings of the hearts of blue utpala lotuses; pronouncing the person's name, within seven days that person comes under one's power. One should perform fire offerings with campaka and karṇikā flowers at the three times of day; if one pronounces a name, whomever one wishes comes under one's power.

In the fortnight of miracles, eating milk and barley gruel, one should recite eight thousand times at the three times of day, and before the painted image perform three hundred thousand fire offerings with kindling sticks of aloeswood. On the fifteenth one should fully undertake the practice and recite until the Blessed One comes. When the earth trembles, or the tip of the lamp flame grows, or the painted image moves, it is accomplished. If the words "It is accomplished!" are uttered, one obtains kingship or lordship over a region.

Having done the preliminary practice, at a stūpa containing relics, before the noble Avalokiteśvara, within six months one obtains five thousand on each occasion. Having made offerings to a stūpa containing relics and recited a hundred thousand times, one obtains a thousand pieces of silver. One should recite a hundred thousand times at a stūpa containing relics; all one's desires will be granted.

One who wishes to pacify all illnesses should empower eight thousand times a thread spun by a maiden, then take it and wind it around oneself; one obtains good fortune. Entering a river that flows to the ocean, one should recite eight thousand times over black sesame; likewise with a thread, with sesame and with charcoal.

At a stūpa containing relics, beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight, on the fifteenth, having fasted for three nights, one should kindle a fire with udumbara wood and perform a hundred thousand fire offerings of white mustard seed smeared with curd, honey and ghee. One becomes the lord of five districts.

Kindling a fire with kindling sticks of the bodhi tree, one should perform a hundred thousand fire offerings of sesame smeared with curd, ghee and honey. Having fasted for three nights on the fifteenth, if those sesame seeds scatter in every direction, then it is accomplished, and one brings all sentient beings under one's power.

First one should recite a hundred thousand times before the noble Avalokiteśvara. Then, when the moon is seized by Rāhu, having offered sesame oil seventy times, one should recite over it until bubbles appear. If one drinks it, one will retain whatever one hears.

Having recited eight thousand times over kunduru resin and taken it, one obtains a village. One should recite eight hundred times each day before the noble Avalokiteśvara; one becomes endowed with prosperity. If one smears kindling sticks of apāmārga with curd, honey and ghee and performs eight thousand fire offerings each day, one obtains a village.

Kindling a fire with kindling sticks of the bahuputrā plant, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of sweet flag. With that ash one should make a mark on the forehead. One becomes invisible. If this does not happen, one should perform the practice again, up to three times.

When the moon is seized by Rāhu, one should go to the bank of a river, kindle a fire with kindling sticks of bilva, and perform a hundred thousand fire offerings of bilva flowers smeared with ghee; then a young yakṣa will come. At midnight, having recited the vidyā a thousand times, one of them comes, and he does whatever one asks of him in words, whether treasures or making one a lord of wealth.

On the eighth day of the dark fortnight, one should worship the Blessed One with scents, flowers, incense and the like; then on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight one should perform the torma rite and recite the vidyā eight thousand times. The piśācas come. One should say, "Dig up treasure!" Then they bestow treasure. Having taken it, one should oneself offer it to the Three Jewels.

Likewise, for the rite of binding the painted image as well, one should kindle a fire with wood of the beleric myrobalan tree before the Blessed One, and each day perform a thousand fire offerings of sesame and thick rice gruel. To bring a minister under one's power, he comes under one's power through a fire offering of white mustard seed. Through a fire offering of lac and resin, the king comes under one's power. To bring women and men under one's power, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of chaff. Kindling a fire with wood of the chebulic myrobalan tree before the Blessed One, one should perform a thousand fire offerings each day with torchwood; one obtains a hundred coins. Living on alms, one should perform fire offerings of palāśa each day at the three times of day; one obtains a hundred pieces of gold each time. Going to the ocean, one should recite the vidyā a hundred thousand times; then it gives jewels. They should be taken, and they must be devoted to the Three Jewels.

With this very mantra, on the full moon of the month of Vaiśākha, one should recite without interruption through the whole night. At the foot of the bodhi tree, having worshiped the Blessed One, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of apāmārga kindling sticks smeared with curd, honey and ghee. She reveals herself, and by means of white mustard seed one becomes free.

If one wishes for pacification, by performing eight hundred fire offerings with oblations of parched rice, there will be pacification. If one wishes for increase, one should kindle a fire with kindling sticks from a milky-sap tree and perform eight hundred fire offerings of sesame and thick rice gruel in three sessions. For three days, kindling a fire with mango kindling sticks, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of dūrvā grass and the thorny plant. One becomes the foremost speaker among those who wish to debate. Each day, having performed fire offerings of moist grain and chaff with the left hand, if one pronounces a person's name, within seven nights that person comes under one's power.

Kindling a fire with kindling sticks of the royal tree, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of sesame and thick rice gruel at the three junctures of the day. For three days, kindling a fire with mango kindling sticks, one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of dūrvā grass and the thorny plant. Within seven days great men come under one's power.

Eating milk, cow's urine, barley gruel and alms, or constantly keeping the vow of silence, being pure and wearing clean clothes and garments of bark, one should undertake the practice. In a clean place, free from the sound of the pestle, one should take earth from both banks of a river and make four lumps of earth for a site seven cubits wide; in the center one should make a thousand-petaled lotus. Upon it one should set a wheel made of the five metals, measuring one span of the Sugata, and one should practice in the center of the maṇḍala, before the painted image. Having worshiped with fragrant scents and with white and red sandalwood, and having offered māndārava flowers, incense and a hundred garlands, one should make offerings to the Blessed One of scents, flowers, incense and the like. One should offer seven rows of ghee lamps. In the four directions one should light four vessels of ghee. In the four directions one should set four vases filled with all the seeds, having placed jewels inside them. One should offer incense of aloeswood, kunduru resin, pounded śrīveṣṭaka and guggulu. Having performed the torma rite, one should offer in the four directions, with what was stated before, curd rice together with the first portion. In the south one should give ni na bhu taktra ra, that is, buttermilk, mixed with water. In the north one should make offerings with a torma filled with milk broth. One should let offerings flow without interruption to all sentient beings in the four directions.

Kindling a fire with palāśa kindling sticks, smearing apāmārga kindling sticks with ghee and empowering them seven times, one should perform eight hundred fire offerings. The one whose name is pronounced comes under one's power. Kindling a fire with kindling sticks of the bodhi tree, one should make an effigy of salt, and, beginning from the head and going down to the feet, empowering each oblation seven times, one should perform eight thousand oblations. The king whose name is pronounced comes under one's power.

On the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, observing the eight-branched poṣadha and fasting day and night, one should smear a maṇḍala the size of a cowhide with cow dung that has not fallen to the ground. Before a stūpa containing relics and at the feet of the noble Avalokiteśvara, one should take, in a vessel of gold or silver, ghee from a tawny cow whose calf is of the same color, churned by a maiden, and sit on a mat of kuśa grass. Holding the vessel in the left hand, one should stir it with the ring finger of the right hand until it becomes warm. Then one should drink it; one's mind becomes clear. Hearing something once, one retains what one has heard. In this rite, if smoke arises, one gains the power to bring others under one's sway; if it blazes, one becomes invisible.

One who wishes to pacify illness in all the limbs should, observing the poṣadha, begin on the eighth day of the bright fortnight in the morning. Facing the east and the other directions, one should smear a maṇḍala the size of a bow and set bricks for the patient in the center. In the four directions one should recite eight hundred times over four vases filled with water and set them down. On the bricks one should lay a cloth dyed with lac. It is to be wound round with thread of five colors spun by a maiden and filled with fragrances. Outside one should make a maṇḍala. In the four directions one offers tormas of liquor and meat. Having worshiped with fragrant flowers, one offers the smoke of guggulu. A copper vessel filled with ghee should be set down. Then, holding green kuśa grass, one should brush the patient, who is dressed in white, all the way down to the feet. One should throw the kuśa onto the ghee. One should do this a hundred and eight times. Then, after the ghee has been eaten, one should examine the patient. Then one should take the green kuśa grass and set it down while reciting. Having provided vessels and clothes that have been purified, one should have the patient bow at the feet of all the buddhas and bodhisattvas. Then, combining the four, priyaṅgu, nāgakesara and madhuka, in equal measure, if the patient eats the finest food together with ghee, he will naturally remain free of illness.

Having empowered a blue thread seven times, one should tie it around the waist. It pacifies spreading swellings. Likewise one should tie it around the neck; difficulty in breathing is pacified.

Observing the poṣadha, one should smear a maṇḍala before the noble Avalokiteśvara, worship with fragrant flowers, and offer ghee lamps. Then one should kindle a fire well with kindling sticks of the bodhi tree. Having kindled it, one should perform a fire offering of eight thousand oblations of lac and resin, each empowered seven times. It pacifies illness. With the vidyā one pacifies obstructors.

One who wishes to do so should take earth from both banks of a river that flows to the ocean and make a hundred and twenty-one figures of various kinds, with the faces of lions, tigers, pigs, sheep and so on. Then, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, observing the poṣadha, one should stretch a red canopy at night in a clean place and properly begin the rite. One should place the obstructors on fourteen cloths dyed with lac. In the center one should place the vināyaka, chief of the obstructors. With powders of five colors, each empowered once, one should make seven maṇḍalas. Having worshiped with red scented flowers, one offers fourteen ghee lamps. One offers guggulu incense. One offers fourteen tormas with meat. One should also scatter fourteen portions of lac juice. Then, with a red thread empowered seven times, one should bind the boundary marks. One should also bind the bhūtas and the king of obstructors. Then, kindling a fire with udumbara kindling sticks and saying, "The obstructors are to be bound," one should perform eight thousand fire offerings to those of the maṇḍala with the syllables svāhā. Thereupon the obstructors and vināyakas become bound.

When one is accomplishing any of the vidyās, the obstructors work their deceptions. Therefore, of the obstructors and vināyakas, all the obstructors should be put into a single earthen vessel, and into another the great vināyaka. Then one should offer all kinds of flowers to all the obstructors, and offer red sandalwood and red karavīra flowers to the great vināyaka. To all the obstructors one offers incense of all substances. To the great vināyaka one offers guggulu incense. One offers it mixed with ghee. Then one should put each of them into a pit as deep as the navel. In this way all the obstructors cease to be.

Observing the poṣadha, on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, at a stūpa containing relics, one should smear a maṇḍala with cow dung that has not fallen to the ground and worship with flowers, scents, incense, ghee lamps and the like. Then, kindling a fire with udumbara wood, one should perform a fire offering with kindling sticks of the brahma tree; if one eats what has been offered to the deity, one's mind becomes clear. If one performs a fire offering of milk, brahmins come under one's power. If one performs a fire offering of what has been offered to the deity, kṣatriyas come under one's power. If one combines barley, curd and what has been offered to the deity and performs a fire offering, vaiśyas come under one's power.

If one recites while looking at an enemy, he becomes paralyzed. Water empowered seven times brings everything down and brings wealth. It is also smeared on all poisons. Having made a pill of refined collyrium and empowered it seven times, one removes eye disease. One should tie a thread on the sick person; no grahas will arise. By tying the topknot one protects oneself. With ash the maṇḍala is bound. By reciting seven times over a clod of earth, the directions are bound.

For a woman who cannot bring forth her child, one should recite thoroughly over sesame and give it to her; she will give birth easily. When, through some confusion, the term of the months in the womb has passed, she should bathe; one should empower a hundred and eight times milk from a cow whose calf is of the same color and give it to her to drink, and she should eat the finest food mixed with ghee. Then she will give birth to a child. One should perform a hundred and eight fire offerings of bahuputrā. One portion of the ash each should be mixed thoroughly into four vases of water, and these should be set down.

Having recited eight hundred times over sweet flag and tied it to the right hand, for as long as it is worn one becomes supreme among all speakers. If one performs eight thousand fire offerings of aparājitā flowers, one becomes invincible to others in battle. Having tied knots in a thread spun by a maiden and empowered it seven times, one should tie it on the hand. Poisons, whether stationary or moving, will not arise. Then, pronouncing the name of the fanged one that is vicious, one empowers water seven times; by drinking a handful of that water, even one who has died in this way rises up. Likewise, having empowered it fourteen times, one should give it to drink. Even the bite of Takṣaka is to be healed. Having empowered the dregs of liquor seven times, one should give it in the case of a death, if the child does not come forth.

Then the Great Being again entered into the samādhi called Fully Urging All Vidyās and spoke the general vidyā of the means of accomplishment:

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya rijuke tāre śānte tuttāre anabhi sāle ture svāhā

This is called the noble Tārā, Tārā of the Crown. With this vidyā, one should enter the water of a river that flows to the ocean up to the shoulders and recite the vidyā a hundred thousand times, until one sees an opening in the disk of the sun in the sky. By doing this the rite is accomplished. If one does not see it, one should practice again. Then, having gone downstream seven times, one should perform the rite of scents, flowers, incense and torma, and, pressing down with the right hand, recite through the whole night, until the words "I breathe out" are spoken. Each day she gives a hundred pieces of silver, and these too should be spent entirely.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya rijuke tāre śānte tāre anabhi lāsye tuttāre agra dharmanityāte ture svāhā

This is called the noble Pure Tārā. With this vidyā one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of the dung of a forest cow smeared with curd, honey and ghee. At the three times of day one obtains a hundred cattle.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahākāruṇikāya lambe pralambe lambe vīrya sarva siddhimme kuru svāhā

This is called the noble Pendent Tārā. With this vidyā one should perform eight thousand fire offerings of karavīra kindling sticks smeared with ghee; as long as one does so, the king comes under one's power and comes to one. Even one who expounds the Piṭaka and has been placed under guard, for release from bonds and the like, he too is made to undertake the purification. Until he is released, for many accomplishments, the attainment of all siddhis, one adds to the vidyā stated before the words sarva siddhiñca me kuru svāhā, and by reciting it constantly one frees from bonds. Or else, having become pure, one should recite through the whole night; it frees from bonds.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya rijuka dharme tāre śānta dharma tuttyare anabilasye dharme ture svāhā

This is the vidyā called the noble Peaceful Tārā. With it one should perform fire offerings in a fire of citron wood, dhālan and straw; then the vināyaka comes, and one should speak to him. Each day he gives one a coin. That too should be spent entirely. He should be made to touch the feet of the Blessed One. Then it is accomplished. Otherwise he does not stay.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhato samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya rijuka dharmamityāte tāre śānta dharmanityāte tuttāre anabhilāsye dharmanityāte ture svāhā

This is the vidyā called the noble Upright Tārā. With it, at a stūpa containing relics, one should kindle a fire with vikaṅkata kindling sticks and perform eight thousand fire offerings of bilva fruits smeared with curd, honey and ghee. Through this one's undertakings become glorious, or one becomes lord of a region.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya agra dharmanityā tāra rijuka dharmanityāte tuttāre anabhīlāsye dharmanityāte tāre svāhā

This is the vidyā called the noble Supreme Tārā. With it one should enter a river that flows to the ocean and perform eight thousand fire offerings of kikirādhā flowers. Each day, or each day and night, one obtains seven or eight measures. Or else one sees a hundred pieces of silver. With that same vidyā, before the noble Avalokiteśvara, one should kindle a fire with wood of a milky-sap tree and perform fire offerings of ghee. One becomes endowed with prosperity.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāye bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya agre tāre rijuke tāre śāmte tuttāre anabhilāsye ture svāhā

This is the vidyā called the noble Tārā Who Proclaims. By reciting it constantly one becomes free of illness.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya agre tāre anabhilāsye dharma tuttāre anabhilāsye dharmaniryāte ture svāhā

This is the vidyā called the noble Tārā of Deliverance. By reciting it constantly one brings one's wishes to fulfillment.
