namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya agre tāre rijuka dharma tuttāre anabhi lāsye dharme ture svāhā

This is the vidyā called the noble Tārā, the Dharma Beyond Expression. By reciting it constantly one is supremely victorious over all enemies.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya agre tāre śānte dharme tuttāre śānta dharmaniryāte ture svāhā

This is the vidyā of Her Who Brings Forth the Peaceful Dharma. By reciting it constantly one obtains whatever one wishes.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya agre tāre rijuka dharma niryāte tuttāre anabhyilāsye dharmaniryāte tuttāre svāhā

This is the vidyā of the Upright One's Supreme Deliverance of the Dharma. By reciting it constantly one attains all one's aims, and one finds the Blessed Lady, or jewels.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya agre tāre rijuke dharmaniryāte tuttāre rijuka dharmaniryāte tuttāre svāhā

This is the vidyā called the noble All-Upright Tārā. By reciting it constantly all people become glad.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya agre dharmaniryāte ture svāhā

This is the vidyā called the noble Tārā, Supreme Deliverer from Poverty. By reciting it constantly one makes one's births continue without interruption.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya agre tāre anabhilāsye tāre anabhilāsye tuttāre anabhilāsye dharmaniryāte ture svāhā

This is the vidyā called the noble Supreme Tārā. By reciting it constantly she grants the supreme fruit.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya śānte dharme tuttāre śānta dharmaniryāte ture svāhā

This is the vidyā called the noble Tārā Endowed with Peace. By reciting it constantly one gives rise to a peaceful mind.

nama ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya rijuke tāre rijuka dharma tuttāre rijuka dharmaniryāte ture svāhā

This is the vidyā called the noble Tārā Endowed with Uprightness. By reciting it constantly one gives rise to an upright mind.

These vidyās, which are called All Dharmas, are accomplished by reciting them: they protect oneself, protect others, and grant every happiness. By reciting them a hundred thousand times one should accomplish all the rites stated before. Reciting them ten thousand times increases merit. By reciting them thirty thousand times one becomes endowed with merit. If one recites them three hundred thousand times, even one who has committed the deeds of immediate retribution will succeed. In short, for one of compassionate nature who unerringly gives the intention of accomplishing benefit, by reciting them constantly all illnesses disappear. No epidemics arise. No harms of any kind will arise. This is how it should be understood.

Now the ritual for this is given in part. By reciting a hundred thousand times one becomes invulnerable to all hostile rites. By reciting two hundred thousand times one's misdeeds are exhausted. By reciting three hundred thousand times one accomplishes the supreme attainments. By reciting four hundred thousand times one obtains the superknowledges one by one. By reciting five hundred thousand times one obtains divine knowledges one by one. By reciting six hundred thousand times one obtains the precious wish-fulfilling jewel. By reciting seven hundred thousand times one comes to have the five superknowledges. By reciting a million times one obtains great kingdoms one by one. By reciting one million one hundred thousand times one becomes a vidyādhara.

Then, wrapping eye ointment with orpiment inside seven leaves of the aśvattha tree, one should recite before the Blessed One until it becomes warm, gives off smoke and blazes. If it becomes warm, one brings others under one's power. If it gives off smoke, one becomes invisible. If it blazes, one travels through the sky. If one performs a fire offering of a hundred thousand oblations of ghee, whatever one wishes is granted. One should recite one million three hundred thousand times; one sees the noble Avalokiteśvara. Having seen him, one finds whatever one seeks.

One should perform eight thousand fire offerings with kindling sticks of white sandalwood. One gains the power to bind speech or feet and becomes lord of a region. One should perform a hundred thousand fire offerings with kindling sticks of black aloeswood. The king comes under one's power. One obtains great abundance. One should perform a hundred thousand fire offerings with kindling sticks of red sandalwood; in all one's accomplishments one obtains thousands gathered together. One should recite seven hundred thousand times beneath the bodhi tree. One obtains essences and rejuvenating elixirs. By eating them, white hair and wrinkles are left behind. By reciting constantly one drives away vultures. By reciting two hundred thousand times one sports by magical display with the king's chief queen.

If one constantly performs fire offerings of royal mustard seed, the king comes under one's power. For this one should perform fire offerings with it smeared with ghee. One constantly obtains wealth. Observing the poṣadha, one should recite a hundred thousand times. Delicious food and drink will appear. One should perform a hundred thousand fire offerings with arka kindling sticks. One obtains a hundred pieces of gold. One should perform fire offerings of oil cake. All people become glad. One should recite while holding it in mind; by reciting constantly one overcomes all illnesses, all grahas, all torments, harms and all fears. One should perform eight thousand fire offerings of guggulu pills smeared with ghee. Wealth will come. With three hundred thousand one obtains a kingdom.

Against harm from the lunar mansions, one should perform fire offerings of curd mixed together with milk; it will be pacified. By a fire offering of jasmine flowers, made by oneself or by another, one brings the king under one's power. One should perform fire offerings of dūrvā shoots; there will be pacification. If one wishes increase for oneself and others, one should perform fire offerings of sesame and thick rice gruel; one will obtain great wealth.

Having empowered bāla and kāla eight hundred times each, one should have them shown to all beings struck by the harm of bhūtas. On seeing them, the bhūtas go to their own abodes. If one recites eight hundred times over the eyes, it takes effect on whoever one sees first. Having recited thoroughly over water, one should wash one's face; all people become glad. By reciting constantly over a crow that does not fly away, one obtains whatever one wishes. Each day at dawn one should drink a handful of water empowered seven times. One becomes free of illness.

Then one who wishes to bring a woman under one's power should make an effigy of salt, press it down with the left foot, and recite eight thousand times over its head; within seven days she comes under one's power.

These accomplishments of the means of accomplishment, and these ways of accomplishing every aim that is accomplished in the mind, should also be applied wholeheartedly as causes of awakening. Likewise, from what has been shown here only in part, one should make it become the special power of applying the means of accomplishment.

By the mere melody of verses
one enjoys the true accomplishment of practice.
Neither entirely empty nor full,
food should be given in every way.
Of flavors such as pungent, sweet and sour,
free from their objects, even the five,
since in one possessed of craving
craving for flavor will arise,
recitation, fire offering and the like done with craving
should not be undertaken here at all.
Delighting here, discerning here,
licking the hands and the rest that is spoken of,
are to be abandoned, or not to be abandoned.
Within, the attendant deities
should be carefully examined as abiding in the kīla.
In a temple of the gods,
or an empty house, or within a cave,
at a solitary tree or a charnel ground,
on a mountain or in a thicket,
recitation, fire offering and practice
are to be done with a one-pointed mind.
For the impure, the impure, and the wholly pure,
it is the pure that purifies.
With both, and for both,
one who speaks of accomplishment should practice.
Whatever has a corpse's thread,
leftovers, and what is stale after that,
whatever a menstruating woman has touched,
what people of caṇḍāla birth have cooked,
what smells putrid, and what is served again,
one who desires merit should give away.
From approaching the deities in due measure
one becomes endowed with such qualities and the rest.
Food or bedding and the like,
whether taken by the practitioner himself
or not, should be resorted to.
Drinkers, places of amusement,
together with beings who are base people,
taken by being bound outside,
perpetrators of the five deeds of immediate retribution,
those who cause disease and the great elements,
whether they have nothing or have much,
those overcome by food and laziness,
those hostile to the Saṅgha and the shameless,
those devoted to avarice, who pierce with weapons,
others who always hold wrong views,
those endowed with such qualities as these,
all this is taught as fitting.
Even if one is unable to bathe at an untimely hour,
for one who is not able by oneself,
one's own wind is proclaimed supreme.
That which exists apart from the three times,
wholly free of the three vehicles,
faults in bathing, and within a river,
destroys what are called the three faults;
bathing is proclaimed supreme.
Therefore, having considered the time,
by that fire, or else after that
by water, bathing is shown
to the practitioner as every accomplishment.
Then, for the sick,
baths with secret mantra
have been proclaimed.

Here, again, the mantra is: namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya buddhāśuci dharmaśuci saṃghaśuci anenaparya vākyena aśuciśucir bhavāmi svāhā

Having recited this mantra once over water, one should wash. Beforehand, at the time of approach and of accomplishment, and for a sick person, bathing with this mantra makes one clean.

In the first part of the night, through three sessions, one becomes tired from reciting the sublime Dharma and the like; then at midnight, on a seat of kuśa grass or the like, having fully arranged cleanliness, the rite of protection and the mudrā, one should perform the rite of the means of accomplishment. At that time protection will have been made.

On a lion's bed, the practitioner, always in the lion's posture, should point the head toward the south or the east. If in a dream there occurs a fire offering with a pacifying or an increasing fire, then, remaining to the east and to the south of the south, one should stretch out the feet. Placing the head toward the west, one should lie facing south.

For one fully endowed with the vidyās, if in a dream one sees sandalwood, bilva and the like, nyagrodha, udumbara and so forth, it is a sign of one's own true and noble accomplishment. If geese, kāraṇḍava ducks, cranes, peacocks and rohana birds appear in a dream, the accomplishment of that will quickly come to one. If one sees oneself appearing clad in white garments, and one's life increasing, accomplishment will occur without doubt. Being covered with garlands of victory banners, and climbing or pressing down upon a palace and the like in a dream, are marks of accomplishment; so too are boarding a boat, and likewise holding its vīṇā. If in a dream one touches victory banners, pennants and the like, or touches a little water with sesame oil, it is a mark of true accomplishment. If in a dream one sees donkeys, she-camels, chariots and the like, or touches them and so forth, know that they obstruct accomplishment. This is also held to be certain.

Endowed with such qualities as these,
virtuous action and actions other than virtue:
in order to accomplish all of these,
therefore act after understanding dreams.
Dream protection and the mudrā
together uphold the vidyā.
Obstructors are always active in sleep;
the destroyer of what is to be destroyed
is truly present. For that reason,
for all recitation, fire offering and the rest,
one should apply the protection spoken of before.
Among the divisions of the rite of protection,
it is held that by this one truly succeeds.
Gods who move in the sky, yakṣas,
self-arisen pretas and rākṣasas,
and wanderers, in order to destroy,
stir up all their own places and minds.
Therefore what is to be done from the very start,
protecting oneself and the signs,
indicating them closely and so forth,
takes place at the time of every practice.
If there are no signs,
for the fruit that arises from the obstructors:
a dog going out from the left,
a cow giving, and a beautiful
hundred-petaled one and an eared one,
deer, jackals and crows,
and likewise domestic pigs,
lizards, parasols and victory banners,
pennants and all the rest:
of all these, the chief are said to be auspicious.
By knowing the auspicious and the rest,
the inauspicious of the inauspicious,
and likewise distinguishing the excellent and the not excellent,
having understood, one should act first.
Bilva and arka flowers
are not desired, and arampa;
by a special action, give that!
For all actions the wise mantrin
should make three kinds of hearth.

Facing toward the south,
the syllables hūṃ phaṭ
should be placed where svāhā would stand;
having fully contemplated it with the mind, one should act.
The one performing a fierce rite should do the rite thus.
Facing toward the north,
one recites together with the syllables svāhā;
having contemplated with the mind, one should perform pacifying.
For what is virtuous and beautiful,
one should act facing the east.
The pacifying and the increasing
are to be stated distinctly:
having faced downward as well,
one should apply oneself to increasing.
For a fierce rite one sits cross-legged on the seat;
for pacifying and increasing, it is said,
one squats upon one's own seat.
The conduct of nonvirtuous action
that is spoken of regarding hair and nails:
they should not be bound up, because
if the practitioner is endowed with celibacy,
then at that time there is no fault;
in performing recitation, fire offering and the rest,
no strife will arise.
As the hair is being fully purified,
the wise, in just that manner,
should shave the hair with a razor;
nor should it be allowed to accumulate.
One who stays desiring accomplishment
is proclaimed to be worshipping the gods.
Though not desired, strength that is accumulated
for that very reason becomes faulty.
Keeping the nails long,
and likewise teeth, body hair and the like,
filth should not be kept.
Lice and the like are born,
and from them nits and the like arise.
One should not look into a well
while the sun is seized by Rāhu.
One who desires accomplishment
should not let the vehicle of the Tathāgata decline.
At the time of worshipping the gods, too,
to gods for whom food has not been set forth
the wise should not make offering.
If it is otherwise, one strays
from the command of the guru and from the commitment.
In earlier times, all the dharmas
are worshipped by listening and so forth.
With awareness, having emanated the form,
one should praise and extol it.
Then one should think one-pointedly and focus.
In the proper order of speech, oneself
should utter these words from one's own mouth:
"Buddhas and bodhisattvas
possessed of great miraculous power,
please turn your minds to this ocean of existence!"
Having repeated just this,
the dream at the dawn of the day
is always highly praised.
Fire offerings of butter and the like, honey,
reciting without purpose:
the beautiful fire offering
is to be prescribed for the sake of destroying obstructors.
For the purpose of averting each thing,
the peaceful mind is praised;
one should do it for the sake of the accomplishment one desires.
The increasing is also to be explained:
likewise, contemplating fully and truly,
the practitioner should practice well.
Then the beautiful fire offering
is to be performed always with effort.
Most certainly miraculous power arises,
for the sake of empowerment in this very life.
Bilva, aśoka and the like,
the renowned palāśa,
aśvattha and pajāka:
all these are for fire offerings of increasing.
The kindling sticks to be used for it
are udumbara, nyagrodha,
and aśvattha, together with milky trees,
whatever is renowned for pacifying.
As kindling sticks for all the rites
of accomplishment, khadira, ariṣṭa,
nimba and thorny trees are taught.
Likewise elsewhere, what is beautiful
truly accomplishes, without doubt.
For accomplishing substances
such as gorocanā, eye medicine and the like,
one uses the cleansing of the five products of the cow;
then, by one endowed with awareness,
or else in divine water,
fragrances, perfumes and the like are properly combined.
Fresh leaves of udumbara,
or those that come from aśvattha,
within the mantra of the flowered one,
on a vānatra or with a delay,
having performed the rite of full protection,
one should accomplish it according to the rite.
One keeping the poṣadha, for as long as
it takes until the dawn arises,
certainly accomplishes; or else this observance
should be taken up in order to undertake it.

In the interval here, "Please turn your mind to me" means: "From killing any living being, from always stealing the wealth of others, from impure conduct, from taking what is not given into the hand, from always drinking intoxicants, and from whatever sequence makes people fight with one another; from garlands, colors, the aims of dance, music, arrogance, great beds and high ones I turn away, and so now I become endowed with the poṣadha of the arhats, possessed of eight branches." Thinking that there is something to be said, namely "I shall gather them in," one should invite them as guests for the sake of all sentient beings as well. Having said this, one should gather them in with the awakening mind. Always having truly generated it, preceded by going for refuge whose nature is the Jewels, the practitioner should practice by linking everything together in this sequence. So it is said.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arta arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya subhagetāre dāntetutāre avaivartakesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Endowed with Good Fortune. By always reciting it, one becomes endowed with good fortune.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya sugatadharmatāre dānādharmatuttāre avaivartikadharmakṣānti kadharmaturesvāhā

This is the irreversible vidyā of Noble Tārā called Bestower of Happiness. By always reciting it, gifts of clothing will come.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya sukhadharmaniryāte tāre dāntadharmaniryāte dāntadharmaniryātetuttāre avaivartika dharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Who Easily Bestows All Wealth. By always reciting it, one paralyzes all the vicious.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya buddhetāre avaivartikadharmetuttāresvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Who Bestows the Happiness of the Buddhas. By always reciting it, one's household becomes prosperous.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya buddhetaresugadharmatāre dāntadharmaniryātetuttāre avaivartikadharmetuttāresvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Tamed by the Buddhas. By always reciting it, an increase of the harvest will come about.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatasamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya buddhetāre nidāntadharmaniryātetuttāre avavartikadharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Endowed with the Buddhas. By always reciting it, food that is utterly without a fixed abode will come.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya availokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya buddhatāre buddhadharmeteture burmeniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Intelligence of the Buddhas. By always reciting it, one gives rise to understanding of skillful means.

namo ratnadrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya sukhadevatāre sukhadharmetuttāresukhadharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Endowed with Happiness. By always reciting it, one brings about an increase of barley.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya manetāredāntadharmaniryāte tāreturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Tamer. By always reciting it, one tames all enemies.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāye bodhitvāya mahāsatvāya anantatāre debyetuttāreanutpantaketuttāresvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Infinite. By always reciting it, one gives rise to infinite merit.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya anantadharmatāre dibyidharmetuttāreanutpantikadharmeturesvāhā

This is called Infinite and Boundless. By always reciting it, one gives rise to infinite merit.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya anantetāreanantadharmatuttāre anantadharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Who Attains the Infinite. By always reciting it, one obtains wealth.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya anantadharmaniryātetāre debyidharmaniryātuttāre anutpantikadharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Who Makes Things Infinite. By always reciting it, the prosperity of one's household becomes infinite.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya siddhetāre siddhādharmetuttāre siddhādharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Accomplished. By always reciting it, one brings about the accomplishments one desires.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya siddhatāreanantatāre dibyituttāreanutpantikeśuturasvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Infinite Accomplishment. By always reciting it, one tames infinite sentient beings through the taming of one skilled in means.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya siddhesiddhetāre anantetāredibyituttāresvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Accomplished in Knowledge. By always reciting it, one attains rebirth among the gods.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya siddhetāreanantāreanantadharmetuttāre debyadharmetuttāre dibyadharmetuttāre anutpantituttāresvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā of the Accomplished Dharma. By always reciting it, one will not fall into hell.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya siddhetāre anantadharmaniryātetāredibyadharmaniryātetuttāreanutpantakadharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Unborn Accomplishment. By always reciting it, no fear of poison will arise.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dibyatāredibyadharmeture niryādharmeniryāteturesvāhā

By always reciting this vidyā, sentient beings become gods.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya siddhitāre anantadharmature anantadharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Endowed with Accomplishment. By always reciting it, one obtains horses.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya siddhitāre dibyadharmeturedibyadharmeniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Accomplished. By always reciting it, one obtains elephants.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya siddhetāre avaivartikadharmeniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Swift Accomplishment. By always reciting it, one comes to have cattle in full abundance.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya anutpantikadharmetuttāre anutpantikadharmaniryātetuttāreturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Unborn. By always reciting it, one comes to have clothing in abundance.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya advayetāre advaye dharmetuttāre advayedharmeniryātetuttāresvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Nondual. By always reciting it, king and minister become undivided.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya adāyetāre maitrituttāreśūraṃgametuttāresvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Nondual Loving-Kindness. By always reciting it, one comes to have a nature of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya advayedharmaniryāte tāremaitri dharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Nondual Heroine. By always reciting it, one becomes full of enthusiasm and brave.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya advayedharmeturemaitridharmetuttāre śūraṃgamayadharmeturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā of the Nondual Dharma. By always reciting it, one becomes unassailable.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya kṣāntetāreadvayetāre maitrituttāre śūraṃgametuttāresvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Patient. By always reciting it, one has a peaceful mind.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya kṣāntetāreśūraṃgama dharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Heroine of Patience. By always reciting it, one becomes invincible.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya kṣāntetāre maitridharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā of the Dharma. By always reciting it, one gains mindfulness.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya kṣāntetāreadvayedhartuttāre advayedharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Nondual with Patience. By always reciting it, one becomes the king's chaplain.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya kṣāntetāreadvayedharmatāre maitridharmatuttāreśūraṃgamadharmeturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Patience. By always reciting it, one becomes greatly favored by the king.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya kṣāntetāre advayetāremaitrituttāre śūraṃgametuttāresvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Endowed with Patience. By always reciting it, one becomes the foremost of speakers in the royal palace.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya artatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya kṣāntetāre kṣāntetāre kṣāntidharmetuttāre kṣāntedharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Who Goes Forth through Patience. By always reciting it, one comes to hold all wealth.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya advayetāre advayadharmetuttāre advayadharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Who Through Nonduality Rescues from Poverty. By always reciting it, one becomes undivided from all sentient beings.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya maitritāre dharmetuttāre maitridharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā of Loving-Kindness. By always reciting it, one comes to have a nature of loving-kindness toward all sentient beings.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya śūraṃgametāreśūraṃgamedharmetuttāre śūraṃgamadharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Who Goes Heroically. By always reciting it, one finds ease, as at the water's edge.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya śaraṇetāre bodhituttāre pūraseturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Worthy of Refuge. By always reciting it, one becomes truly worthy to be a refuge for all sentient beings.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya śaraṇedharmetārebodhidharmetuttārepūrāśa dharmeturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma of Refuge. By always reciting it, one comes to comprehend all dharmas.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya śaraṇetāre tuttāresvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Supreme Refuge. By always reciting it, no sentient being who has become an ordinary person will be reborn as cattle.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya śaraṇerharmeniryātetāre bodhiniryātetuttāre pūraśadharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Swift Refuge. By always reciting it, one is greeted with "Welcome!" by each and every one, everywhere.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya amṛtetāre saumyetāre asaṃskṛtadharmeturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā of Nectar. By always reciting it, one comes to bestow nectar on all sentient beings.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahāsatvāya amṛtadharmaniryātetāresaume dharmaniryātetuttāre asaṃskṛtadharmaturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Who Goes Forth through the Dharma of Nectar. By always reciting it, one comes to possess nectar and attains happiness.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya amṛtādharmaniryātetāresaumedharmaniryātetuttāre asaṃskṛdharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Happiness Itself. By always reciting it, one pacifies attachment.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dṛḍhitāre śāraṇetāre bodhetuttāre surāseturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Steadfast. By always reciting it, one becomes free of illness and firm in body.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dṛḍhatāreśaraṇedharmaniryātetāre bodhidharmaniryātetuttāre bodhidharmaniryātetuttāre pūrāsadharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Who Goes Steadfastly. By always reciting it, one becomes long-lived, and one's life increases through the work of building stūpas and the like.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dṛḍhotāre bodhidharmatuttārebodhiśaraṇedharmaniryāte pūrusedharmaturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Steadfast Dharma. By always reciting it, one removes all poisons, both those that are prepared and those that are not.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dṛḍhatāre dṛḍhadharmetuttāre dṛḍhadharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Endowed with Steadfastness. By always reciting it, one dispels great fears.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dharmetāre amṛtādharmaniryātetāre saumyedharmaniryāteturesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Well-Mixed Nectar. By always reciting it, one frees those who are bound.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avaloketeśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya saumyetaresaumyedharmetuttāresaumyesvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Nectar of Peace. By always reciting it, one cures all leprosy.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahāsatvāya dharmetāre amṛtedharmetāre saumyatuttāre saṃskṛtetuttāresvāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma. By always reciting it, one overcomes all diseases of the fingers.

namo ratnatreyāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dharmetāre dharmadharmatuttāre dharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma and Non-Dharma. By always reciting it, one obtains gold.

namo ratnatrayaya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhaya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dharmetāre amṛtādharmetāresaumyedharmebhutaitāre asaṃskṛtadharmeture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Conditioned Dharma. By always reciting it, one obtains silver.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya amṛtātāre amṛtedharmetuttāre tureamṛtadharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma of All Nectars. By always reciting it, wealth comes forth.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dharmetāre amṛtādharmetāre amṛtādharmatutāre amṛtādharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Attainment of Dharma. By always reciting it, one comes to see all who roam about.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya asaṃskṛtetāre saṃskṛtetāretuttāre asaṃskṛtadharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Conditioned. By always reciting it, one frees those seized by ḍākinīs merely by looking at them.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dharmatāresaumyedharme dharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma of Peace. By always reciting it, one frees all those seized by the pūtana graha merely by looking at them.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dharmetāre asaṃskṛtadharmetuttāreasaṃskṛtedharmaniryāteture svāhā

By always reciting it, one frees those seized by the rākṣasa graha merely by looking at them.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya araṇadharmaniryātetārevidyādharmatuttāre ādarśanadharmaniryāte svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma Without Flow. By always reciting it, one removes all poisons, the stationary, the moving, and the rest.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya aruṇetārevidyetuttāre adidarśaniture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā First Sight of Dawn. By always reciting it, one is granted lands.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya araṇedharmetārevidyadharmetuttāre anidarśanadharmeture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma. By always reciting it, every year's harvest will be abundant.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya traividyetārearaṇetāre vidyātuttāre anidarśanature svāhā

This is the one called Noble Tārā Dharma of the Three Knowledges. By always reciting it, one comes to see the farthest limits.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya traividyātāre araṇadharmatārevidyādharmetārevidyādharmetuttāre traividyādharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā of the Three Knowledges. By always reciting it, one will be called forward into the presence of the king.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya traividyātāre vidyetārearaṇadharmetāre vidyādharmatuttāre anidarśanadharmeture svāhā

This is the one called Noble Tārā Three Knowledges Free of Affliction. By always reciting it, one becomes the great favorite of all women.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya traividyātāre anidarśani dharmetuttāre anidarśanadharmeniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Indemonstrable Three Knowledges. By always reciting it, all estates come under one's control.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya traividyetāre araṇadharmaniryātedāre vidyādharmaniryātetuttāre anidarśaṅharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma of the Three Knowledges.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya traividyetāre vidyātāre vidyādharmetuttāre vidyādharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Three Knowledges. By always reciting it, one obtains a domain of a thousand villages.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya traividyetāre araṇedharmetuttāre araṇadharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Knower of the Three. By always reciting it, one becomes the great favorite of everyone in the king's palace.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvārāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya arhatetāre araṇadharmetuttāre araṇadharmeniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Without Conflict. By always reciting it, one becomes the foremost of speakers.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya vidyetāre vidyādharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā. By always reciting it, knowledge arises once again for all sentient beings.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatasamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya araṇatāre dharmetuttāre amitābheture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Certain Knowledge. By always reciting it, one becomes lord of the land.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya ariṇetāre dharmenireṇetāreniraṇe dharmetuttāreture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Free of Debt. By always reciting it, one brings others under one's power.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya nirinadharmatāre śāntadharmetuttāreamitābhādharmeture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma Free of Debt. By always reciting it, one brings the gandharvas under one's power. Then they bestow divine medicines, and by eating these one lives for a thousand years. It is the same in every case.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya nirriṇadharmaniryātetuttāre amitābhādharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Amitābha Rite of Freedom from Debt. By always reciting it, one brings the brahmarākṣasas and their companions under one's power.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya satvetāreniraṇa niraṇa niṇidharmeniryātetāredharmadharma niryātuttāre amitābhādharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Courage. By always reciting it, one gains mastery over others, over the substances one has made oneself, and over all substances.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya satvetāreniriṇetāre dharmetuttāreamitābhetuttāre svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Amitābha of Courage. By always reciting it, one brings all bhūtas under one's power.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitabhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya satvetāresatvādharmetuttāre satvādharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma of Courage. By always reciting it, one brings all pūtanas under one's power.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya satvetāreniriṇedharmaniryāte dharmadharmaniryātetuttāre amitābhādharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Attainment of Courage. By always reciting it, one masters all vidyās and also becomes invisible.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dharmatāre dharmetuttāre dharmadharmaniryateture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā All-Illuminating Dharma. By always reciting it, one brings gods and ḍākinīs under one's power.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dharmetāre dharmedharmetuttāre svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Possessor of the Reasoning of Dharma. By always reciting it, one brings all nāga maidens under one's power.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dharmetāre dharmedharmetuttāre svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Eternal Dharma. If one always recites it, one becomes the master of a great household.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dharmetāre dharmeniriṇe dharmaniriṇa dharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma of Amitābha. By always reciting it, one summons whatever one desires.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya dharmatāre dharmadharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Mind of Dharma. By always reciting it, one becomes inconceivable to sentient beings.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatasamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya amoghetāre saṃghetuttāre sukhavatīture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Unfailing. By always reciting it, strength and splendor arise without fail.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya amoghadharmaniryātetāre saṃghadharmaniryāteture sukhavatīdharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Destroyer of Death. By always reciting it, one gains entry into the abode of the asuras.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya amoghatāre amoghadharmatuttāreamoghadharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Destroyer of Death. By always reciting it, one accomplishes miraculous powers.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya savalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya acintyetāreamoghadharniryātetuttāre sukhavatīdharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Lady of Vidyā-Mantras. By always reciting it, one becomes invisible.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya acintyetāre amoghatāre sukhavatīture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Inconceivable Nectar. By always reciting it, one sees a treasure in one's own house, and it becomes inexhaustible.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya acintyetāre acantyetuttāre acintyedharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma of Inconceivable Nectar. By always reciting it, one obtains the elixir of the gods.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbudḍhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya acintyetāre acintyedharmetuttāre acintyedharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Endowed with the Inconceivable. By always reciting it, one averts untimely death.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya amoghadharmetāresaṃghadharmetuttāre sukhavatīdharmeture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Inconceivable Saṅgha. By always reciting it, one becomes long-lived.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya acintyetāre saṃghadharmatuttāre saṃghadharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma of the Inconceivable Saṅgha. By always reciting it, one becomes invincible to others in battle.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya acintyetāre amoghadharmatuttāre amoghadharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Inconceivable. By always reciting it, one comes to know directly the time of one's own birth and death.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya acintyetāre sukhavatīdharmetuttāre sukhavatīdharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Inconceivable Bliss. By always reciting it, one comes to know one's own death.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama arya āvalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya sukhavatīdharmetāre sukhavatīdharmetuttāre sukhavatīdharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Lady of Sukhāvatī. By always reciting it, one will be reborn in Sukhāvatī.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya saṃghetāre saṃghadharmatuttāre sighadharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Saṅgha. By always reciting it, even one who commits evil deeds will be reborn among the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-Three.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya avalokitetāre īśetuttāre anaṃginature svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Avalokiteśvara. By always reciting it, at the time of death one sees Avalokiteśvara, and then one sees all the divine destinies.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya avalokitedharmaniryātetuttāre īśadharmaniryātetuttāre anaṃgadharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Dharma of Avalokiteśvara. By always reciting it, one becomes possessed of wealth.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya avalokitedharmatāreīśvarādharmetuttāre anaṃganadharmeture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Bodiless Avalokiteśvara. By always reciting it, one obtains fragrance.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya āryatāre avalokitedharmaniryātetūreīśadharmaniryātetuttāreanaṃganadharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Noble One. By always reciting it, one obtains kingship, the Dharma, the gods, and wealth as well.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhataisamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya avalokitetāre īśeanaṃganeture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the All-Seeing. By always reciting it, one becomes ruler of the land.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya āryatāre avalokitedharmetāre īśadharmetuttāreanaṃganadharmeture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Deathless. By always reciting it, one becomes irreversible.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya īśetāreīśadharmetuttāre īśadharmeniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Lord. By always reciting it, one is not born among the hooded serpents, and one will not be reborn.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya āryatāre anaṃgadharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Bodiless. By always reciting it, one becomes fortunate among gods and humans.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya āryatāre avalokitedharmetuttāre svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Endowed with Nobility. By always reciting it, one becomes the foremost of speakers in every debate.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya īśetāredharmatuttāre īśetāredharmaniryāteture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Supreme Lord. By always reciting it, one becomes a mighty lord.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya īśetāre īśadharmaniryāture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Attainment of Lordship. By always reciting it, one unfailingly sees everything.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā rijukarmaāryetāre tārayabhagavati tuttāresarvabhaya mocani svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Liberation from Fear. By always reciting it, one comes to remember one's past births.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāretaraṇi trāsaya śatrabhaya nāśanimocaniture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Crossing Beyond Battle. By always reciting it, one becomes invincible to others in battle.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tāretāre tārāya bhagavatibandhamocani svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Liberator from Bonds. By always reciting it, one frees sentient beings.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya namo ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya atuttāretuttārevaravajramokṣani svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā She Who Frees from the Vajra. By always reciting it, one wards off thunderbolts.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tārerijukadharmaniryātetuttāre śāntaniryātetāretāreanabhilasya dharmaniryātetāretāreturehinatrāsanivitrāsaniṭekani mohani jambhani stambhani prabhecandraprabhe hilihili milimili vegaśaṅsnikuṇḍikuṇḍamahākuṇḍa dharedhare dhanapatitāre huru kurukuru ahaṃyāṃyaṃ cintaya sintāntāsādhāya svāhā

This is the root vidyā. By always reciting it, one accomplishes everything. It becomes the vidyā for the rite of the means of accomplishing this.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā suresurāpitiharahara svāhā

This is the vidyā for inviting with guggulu.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāretāravati sarvaarthasādhani tiṣṭhatiṣṭha yāvarkārya saddhamahāma svāhā

This is the vidyā of the welcoming water.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvaya mahāsatvāya tadyathā harahara kurukuru gandharavāsini svāhā

This is the vidyā of perfume.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā amoghe amogha vāsivarade svāhā

This is the vidyā of flowers.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā meghasvārakuru svāhā

This is the vidyā of incense.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāretāre danidani hanahana kurukuru diśvabali svāhā

This is the vidyā of the torma.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā etajvalini jvalajvala deva svāhā

This is the vidyā of the lamp.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatasamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā hirihiri surusuru murumuru sarvasatvākāruṇikā gacchatisvabhuvanaṃ āryaavalokiteśvarāṃsamayamanusmarāya svāhā

This is the vidyā for requesting departure: with white flowers and welcoming water one requests the deity to depart.

These are the vidyās of the rite of the sādhana of the root vidyā.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā śaraṇetāre svāhā

This is going for refuge to Tārā.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā dharmetāreture svāhā

As the fruit of flowers and the rest, through Dharma Tārā one brings sentient beings under one's power.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā satvātāreture svāhā

Through this, Noble Tārā brings delight to sentient beings.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā satvāniristitāre svāhā

Noble Tārā, liberator of sentient beings, bestows every happiness.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā satvesatvavatītāre svāhā

One brings courageous people under one's power.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā śāstedṛḍhetāre svāhā

Through the practice of constant recitation, Noble Tārā bestows lands upon the teachings.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā riṇiriṇitāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Free of Debt.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā saumisaumitāre svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Happiness Itself.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā dharmedharmavatitāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Lady of Dharma Intelligence.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā suredha sukhavatītāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Bliss.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā avyavacchintetāreture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā the Uninterrupted.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā dṛḍhe dṛḍhe pratijñāvati tāre svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā of Steadfast Vow.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā jñāna jñānamaticara tāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Wisdom.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā sūkṣme sūkṣmavati tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā the Subtle.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā vīryamati vīryamati tāre bhagate svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Diligence.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā prabhe prabhavatī tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Light Rays.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā dharme dharmavati ture ture svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Endowed with Dharma.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā īśe īśavatī ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā the Sovereign Lady.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā avalokitevahī tāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with the All-Seeing Gaze.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā candra candramatī tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with the Moon.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā sūrye sūryavatī tāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with the Sun.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā jvāle jvālavati bhagavati tāre svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Endowed with Blazing Light.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā buddhā buddhāvati tāre svāhā

This is Noble Tārā the Buddha.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā dharme dharmavatī tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Dharma.

namo rattrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā saṃghe tāre saṃghevati tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Saṅgha.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā jaye tāre jayavati bhagavati tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Victory.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā dāne dānavatī tāre tuttāre svāhā

It is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Generosity.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā vyūhe vyūhe vatī tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Array.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā āḍhye aḍhye vatā tāra bhagavati tuttāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Wealth.

namo ratnatrayāya namo amitābhāya tathāgatāya arhatesamyaksaṃbuddhāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā āvati avati tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā the Protectress.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā ante antapatī trāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with the Limitless.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā avalokini avalokavatī tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with All-Surveying Vision.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā śīle śīlavati tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Moral Discipline.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā kṣānte kṣāntavatī tāre bhagavatī ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Patience.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā vīrye vīryavatī tāre tāre ture ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Diligence.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā dhyane dhyanavati tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Meditative Concentration.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā prajñāparaprajñāvatī tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Supreme Wisdom.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā upāye upayavati tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Endowed with Skillful Means.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā kauśalyavati tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Skill.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā jyoti jyoti vatī tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Starlight.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā bodhyaṅge bodhyaṃgavati tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is the vidyā called Noble Tārā Endowed with the Limbs of Awakening.

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Blazing Light.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā brahme tāre brahmesame tāre brahmaṇisame tāre brahmamati ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Endowed with Brahmā.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā indre tāre indrasame tāre indrapati tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Mistress of Indra.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā anna tāre annavati tāre tāre tuttāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Mistress of Food.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokitaśārāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā ākāśe tāre ākāśapati tāre ture ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Mistress of All-Encompassing Radiance.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā gagane tāre gaganavati tāre tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Mistress of the Sky.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā jaye tāre jayapatī tāre tāre tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Mistress of Victory.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā sarvadevatā svare tāre abhisvarapati tāre ture ture tāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Mistress of Clear Light.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā pradhānaprati tāre pradhāni tāre ture ture pradhānapati svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā the Foremost.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā sarvadeva tare sarvadevapati tāre tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Mistress of All the Gods.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā samante tāre samantaṃvati tāre samantamati tāre ture tāre tāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā the All-Endowed.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā samṛdharmati tāre ture ture tāraya tāre tare svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Mistress of Perfect Accumulation.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā īśe tāre īśvati tāre tāre tute īśa tāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā the Powerful.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre tāre tāre tāre sutāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, the Excellent Tārā.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre tāre bhagavate bhayamocana trāse trāsaya tāre tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Who Frees from Fear.

namo ratnatrayaya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvaya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre tāre āre āre tuttāre tuttāre ture svahā

This is called Noble Tārā the Heroine.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre tāre tāraya botāre mahābhaya tāre tāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Who Frees from Great Fear.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāraṇi niravikalpe tāre nirvikalpa samuṅgate tāre tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Free of Conceptuality.

namo ratnayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā buddhakalpe tāre buddhakalpa niryāte ture ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Ordinance of the Buddha.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre tāre dharmakalpe tāre dharmakalpa niryate ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Ordinance of the Dharma.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre saṃghakalpe tāre saṃghakalpa niryāte ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Ordinance of the Saṅgha.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā svate bhagavate tāre abhave tāre tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā Free of Entities.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā abhavadāne tāre tāre kutāre kuru kuru muru muru svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Intrinsic Nature of All.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā sarvabhave tāre sarvasva niryāte tāre ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Definite Emergence of All One's Own.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā sarva aṃgera tāre sarvarijuki tāre tāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, the Primal Dharma.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā sarvapāramitā tāre sarvabārāmitā niryāte ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Perfection of All.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā sarvadāne tāre tāre sarvadānapāramitāni tāniryāte ture tura svāhā

This is Noble Tārā, Perfection of All Generosity.

namo ratnatraṃyāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā śīle tāre śīlablaramitā tāre ture ture śīlapāramitā niryāte ture svāhā

This is Noble Tārā, Perfection of Moral Discipline.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā kṣānte tāre kṣāntepāramite tāre kṣāntepāramitā niryāte ture ture svāhā

This is Noble Tārā, Perfection of Patience.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā vīrya tāre vīryapāramitā tāre vīryaparamitā niryāte ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Perfection of Diligence.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā dhyāne tāre dhyānapāramitā tāre dhyānapāramitā niryāte ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, She Who Has Perfected Meditative Concentration.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā prajñā tāre prajñāpāramitā tāre prajñāpāramitā niryāte ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, She Who Has Perfected Wisdom.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā sarvapāramitā niryāte ture ture sarvadharmma avabhāva sarvapāramite ture ture ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Definite Emergence of the Dharma of All the Perfections.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre sarvabuddhāniryāte ture ture sarvabuddhapāramite ture tāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, She Who Has Reached the Perfection of All Buddhas.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā sarvadharme tāre sarvadharma niryāte tāre tāre sarvadharma niryāte nivaraṇi varaṇi tāre svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, She Who Has Reached the Perfection of All Dharmas.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre saṃghe saṃghe tāre ture sarvasaṃghadharma niryāte ture saṃgha pāramite ture ture svāhā

This is called Noble Tārā, Perfection of the Entire Saṅgha.

namo ratnatrayāya nama ārya avalokiteśvarāya bodhisatvāya mahāsatvāya tadyathā tāre tāre sarvapāramitā tāre sarvadharme tāre sarvarijukadharma niryāte ture ture anabhilābya tāre tāre ture ture svāhā

These Tārās, down to the one called Noble Tārā the Inexpressible, are the definite emergence of all phenomena, without intrinsic nature and inexpressible. They accomplish every aim and heal every illness. They are accomplished by being recited in any circumstance. Against all fears and all harms, and in all minor rites, in whatever way they are applied, in just that way they bring about accomplishment.

I shall now set out briefly the rite for these. Beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight, observing the poṣadha vows, or even without the poṣadha, one should make offerings each day with perfumes, flowers and so forth, and recite one hundred thousand times. At the end, having fasted for one day and night, one sits on a mat of kuśa grass before a painted cloth or an image, and, in the sequence that was taught, facing east oneself, one should make eight thousand fire offerings of the previously mentioned sticks of black agaru wood, four finger-widths long, smeared with curd, honey and ghee. One who, in this king of ritual manuals or in any other, recites with the knowledge mantra of Tārā and trains toward liberation will accomplish limitless knowledge mantras.

If one wishes to proceed other than with a painted cloth, one observing the poṣadha should, on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, at a stūpa containing relics, smear a maṇḍala with cow dung that has not fallen to the ground, and make offerings with flowers, incense, butter lamps and so forth. Then, kindling a fire with udumbara wood, one should make eight thousand fire offerings with sticks of palāśa wood; and by eating the caru, one becomes keen-minded.

By making fire offerings of milk, brahmins are brought under one's power. One should make fire offerings with caru food: kṣatriyas are brought under one's power. Mixing barley with curd and combining it with caru, one should make fire offerings: vaiśyas are brought under one's power. Gazing at an enemy, one should recite: he becomes paralyzed. Sprinkling with water empowered seven times dispels everything; so too does sprinkling it on any poison. A digestive pill empowered seven times dispels eye disease. One should bind the sick with a thread: it dispels all grahas. Binding one's topknot protects oneself. With ash one seals the maṇḍala. Reciting seven times over a clod of earth seals the directions.

For a woman who cannot deliver her child, one should recite over sesame oil and give it to her: she will give birth easily. If, because the fetus is obstructed, the term of the pregnancy has passed, then after she has bathed, one should empower the milk of a cow of matching lineage eight thousand times and give it to her to drink. Otherwise, one should mix it with an equal measure of ghee and give it to her. Then she will give birth to the child. Then, if she wants many children, one should mix the ash from eight thousand fire offerings with four pots of water and set them in place.

If one binds on one's right hand a thread recited over eight hundred times, then for as long as it is worn one becomes supreme among all speakers. Making eight thousand fire offerings with aparājitā flowers, one becomes invincible by others in battle. Tying knots in a thread spun by a maiden and empowering it seven times, one should bind it on the hand: one becomes lord of all that is stable and moving.

Then, speaking the name of one struck down by violence, one empowers water seven times and gives it to drink from cupped hands: even one who has died is made to rise. Likewise, having empowered it toward the four directions, one gives it to drink: whoever has been seized by the fangs of Takṣaka is revived. If one empowers lumps of the breast and tumors seven times and gives the remedy, they are released, and the person feels no pain.

For epidemics, calamities and battle: in the middle of the city, or at night, having smeared the ground over the extent of an arrow's range and given a white torma offering, one kindles a fire with sticks of a milky-sapped tree and makes fire offerings with a thousand oblations of milk. This pacifies the epidemic. Then, if it is not pacified, at another time, when one has resolved to paralyze it, one kindles a fire with sticks of śleṣmāntaka and makes eight thousand fire offerings of siddhārtha wood smeared with akṣa and sesame oil. This immediately pacifies all epidemics. By this rite one binds poison. By looking upon all beings while reciting, one makes them become one's subjects.

Making eight thousand fire offerings with sticks of kuṣmāṇḍa, kumbhāṇḍas are brought under one's power. Making eight thousand fire offerings of sesame paste, pretas are brought under one's power. Making eight thousand fire offerings of bela and khaṇḍaka in a charnel ground, piśācas are brought under one's power. To bring yakṣas under one's power, one makes eight thousand fire offerings of vaṭa sticks smeared with curd, honey and ghee; this brings apasmāras and oppressor spirits under one's power. One should make eight thousand fire offerings with oblations of wool. To destroy obstructors by means of the knowledge mantra, one should make eight thousand fire offerings of khadira tips smeared with pungent sesame oil. Making eight thousand fire offerings of guggulu pills smeared with ghee, the followers of the Great God (Śiva), and the Great God himself, are brought under one's power.

Taking realgar bought at a hero's price, one kindles a fire with sticks of the king tree and recites until it becomes a mass of fire. Then, from the milk of a tawny cow of matching lineage, one has ghee churned by a maiden and places the realgar in that ghee. Likewise, one does the same with a vessel filled with curd and a vessel filled with ghee and honey. Then, having performed the protection, one places them in a casket, and when the moon is seized by Rāhu, having fasted for three nights, before a stūpa containing relics or at the feet of noble Avalokiteśvara, one makes offerings as one can afford. Facing north, one sets out the four vessels and recites until they become warm, give off smoke, or blaze. This brings beings under one's power, makes one invisible, and carries one into the sky.

Likewise, to produce a superior eye ointment, one oneself, particularly on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, places it on a lotus-fiber thread at the feet of noble Avalokiteśvara, takes it up with joined palms, and recites until it becomes warm, gives off smoke and blazes. In this very rite there are three signs.

Having a lotus made of the five metals, one grinds saffron, gorocanā and camphor with rainwater and places them in the lotus. Then, on the eighth day of the bright fortnight, one keeping the poṣadha bathes three times a day, puts on clean clothes, and, before a stūpa containing relics or at the feet of noble Avalokiteśvara, takes up the lotus in the right hand and recites until it blazes. Then, by taking it up, one becomes a vidyādhara and lives for ten thousand years. The same holds for bracelets, diadems and chains.

Likewise, one has red mountain sandalwood, guggulu, the root of the coiling joy plant, the five metals, girikarṇikā, grain husks, costus, rgya spos, honey, long pepper and turuṣka, in equal parts, combined and ground into a fine powder. Then, taking the milk of a tawny cow of matching lineage, one combines the ghee churned by a maiden with fresh butter, and with the powder one has pills made. One should offer a lamp with the powder in arka sesame oil. Then, on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, fasting day and night, one keeping the poṣadha places the pills inside seven aśvattha leaves and recites before noble Avalokiteśvara until they become warm. By putting one in the mouth, one becomes invisible. Then, by making them blaze, one travels in the sky.

Next, another rite: at a stūpa containing relics, before an image, one keeping the poṣadha makes extensive offerings, kindles a fire with sticks of the fire tree, and makes eight thousand fire offerings with khadira sticks smeared with curd, honey and ghee, beginning on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight and continuing until the fifteenth. Then it is accomplished. Likewise, one keeping the poṣadha should always do three thousand recitations. Afterward it serves for all rites.

Or else, if one wishes to bring a king or a minister under one's power, one makes offerings to the Blessed One and then makes eight thousand fire offerings of sticks of the king of trees smeared with iṅguda oil, beginning on the fourteenth and continuing until the fifteenth. By this rite, even one whose moral discipline is broken succeeds just the same. For killing and for expelling, one makes eight thousand fire offerings of nimba sticks smeared with pungent sesame oil: within seven nights one expels the enemy.

One who wishes to bring the four castes under one's power makes fire offerings of water with caru and of what is called yakṣa's bowl: they are brought under one's power. At night one should make eight thousand fire offerings of pucirajata. By recitation one frees from bondage. For obstructors, by fire offerings of husks and sesame, or of anything else, they are fully pacified.
