Then one makes a son of Vāsuki out of anthill earth, sits close by it, and recites until it moves. In this way it will be accomplished. The son of Vāsuki himself gives food worth twelve māṣas. He reveals matters of the past, the future and the present. Eating milk and barley gruel and reciting eight thousand times before the image, one obtains enjoyments of every kind.

For one month one eats alms food, and on the eleventh day of the bright fortnight one keeps a fast for one night. Having made a great offering before the image, one should take hold of the feet of the noble Avalokiteśvara, of the image, and recite until the image moves. When it moves, one will see whatever one wishes. One becomes a king of all accomplishments. Whatever one conceives in one's mind, one can bring about. One will live for five thousand years.

Entering the Ganges, one should recite one hundred thousand times. Afterward, for the same length of time, one makes a stupa of sand before the image, combines honey and milk, and makes fire offerings. All the nāgas will come. They will do everything one says. Climbing to a mountain peak and setting up the painted image, one should make fire offerings of sandalwood chips smeared with sesame oil, and the yakṣas will come. They will do everything one says. Setting up the painted image in a forest, one should make eight thousand fire offerings of honey and long pepper combined, and all the vidyādharas will come. They will carry out every command. Setting up, beneath a solitary tree, a stupa containing the essence of dependent origination, one should recite a hundred thousand times.

When the hundred thousand recitations are complete, one who keeps the poṣadha vows should have a trident made of bodhi-tree wood, well formed and possessing the proper characteristics, and perform fire offerings until a full thousand is reached. On the day of the full moon, one anoints it thoroughly with fine perfume, makes offerings to the painted image as one's means allow, and takes it in the right hand. One should practice with it through the whole night, until it blazes. When it blazes, one becomes a second lord of bhūtas, a tamer of the hard to tame, the Great God whom no sentient being can withstand.

Entering the ocean, one recites a hundred thousand times. One then sees whatever nāga one wishes, Sāgara the nāga king and the others. He also bestows a precious jewel upon one. By taking it one becomes a vidyādhara, the king of all the nāga vidyādharas. Eating milk and barley gruel, one should recite seven hundred thousand times. Then one who keeps the poṣadha vows should have a craftsman make a copper vessel, and on the full moon of the month of miracles fill it completely with every kind of grain and medicine, set it before the painted image, and recite until it blazes. Putting one's hand into it, whatever one desires will come forth. This is the sādhana of the excellent vessel.

Entering a river that flows into the ocean, one should recite a hundred thousand times. Afterward, on the full moon, one makes a stupa of jewels or of earth and has a painted image made in that very place. On the full moon of the month of miracles one fills vessels completely with every kind of grain and medicine and sets each before the painted image. Having made a great offering, one takes up with the right hand the stupa of jewels or of earth that was set there, sits close by in the cross-legged posture, and should recite until it blazes. One becomes a vidyādhara who holds the wish-fulfilling jewel.

Setting up the painted image at a stupa that contains relics, one should recite a hundred thousand times. On the full moon of the month of miracles one makes offerings of every kind and sets out long rows of lamps as well. Holding in the right hand a banner from which white cloth hangs, one should recite until it blazes. One becomes a vidyādhara of the banner, and goes everywhere without hindrance.

On the full moon of the month of miracles, having made a great offering to the painted image, one anoints a volume of the Blessed Mother, the Perfection of Wisdom, with the scent of fine perfume, winds garlands of fragrant flowers about it, holds it in the left hand, sits close by in the cross-legged posture, and should recite until it blazes. One becomes a king of vidyādharas, and goes wherever one wishes.

Having a very beautiful maiden who practices the conduct of a bodhisattva bathe well and adorn herself with ornaments, one makes offerings before the painted image as one's means allow. Holding her firmly with the left hand, one should recite until the right hand blazes together with her. Just as she is, together with her, one becomes a vidyādhara.

Placing one's hand upon a single sign, one should recite until one no longer sees the retinue. When it is no longer seen, all beings come and bestow all three accomplishments.

When the moon is seized by Rāhu, or when the sun is seized by Rāhu, one wraps cow bezoar in leaves of the bodhi tree and, at a stupa containing relics in a temple of Maheśvara, should recite until smoke rises from it. Making a tilaka mark with it, one becomes invisible.

Eating milk and barley gruel, one should recite a thousand times in three sessions on the shore of the ocean or at the foot of a tree. Within seven nights one sees the treasures that lie in the ocean, and should take as much as one wishes. Eating lentils, one climbs a mountain and should recite eight thousand times. Within twenty nights the gold and precious jewels that lie in the mountain are shown and spoken of to one, and one should take as much as one wishes. On the bank of a river that flows to the ocean, or at the edge of a wood, one should recite day and night for one month. One sees all of them on the bank of the river, and should take as much as one wishes.

To bring a man or a woman under one's power, draw an effigy on the ground with charcoal, sit upon it, and recite eight thousand times in three sessions for three days and nights. They will come under one's power.

One who desires the king, or the king's garments, should put fully pleasing white flowers into water that has been recited over once. Within seven nights one obtains garments. Merely by reciting eight thousand times over cow's ghee one becomes fortunate. Through the recitation one causes the stationary and the moving to shift in a special way.

Taking an iron sword about a finger in length, one sets up the painted image at a stupa that contains relics and makes a vast offering. Surrounding the sword clockwise with leaves of the aśvattha tree, one sets it down and should recite until it blazes. By taking it up one flies together with one's retinue, surrounded by a thousand vidyādharas, known to all the vidyādharas, and lives for an intermediate eon. Eating milk and barley gruel, one should recite seven hundred thousand times.

Having done the preliminary practice, on the eighth or the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight one makes a vast offering to the painted image. Either living on what the Saṅgha provides or eating alms food, one takes realgar bought at a hero's price, and with it, as described, draws on the ground a lotus with a hundred petals. Sitting close by the lotus petals, one should recite day after day until the lotus breaks through the ground and rises upward. Twenty vidyādharas seated on the lotus petals will appear. A divine celestial palace will appear as well. Then he, together with his retinue, ascends that celestial palace and flies. It becomes a divine celestial palace adorned with many precious lotuses. He lives for an intermediate eon. He goes even to Sukhāvatī and returns again. He obtains births in various different bodies.

If one sprinkles a dry tree with water consecrated by eight thousand recitations, it will come to abound in flowers and fruit.

Entering a dried-up river, one should recite a hundred thousand times, and water will spring forth. If one recites in a river that is full and flowing, it becomes dry ground.

If one wishes to bring a king or a king's minister under one's power, one should present, before the painted image, eight thousand flowers of whatever kind one can find, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight. One should also make eight thousand fire offerings with oblations of salt. The king will surely come under one's power. With that same rite, from the eighth day through to the eleventh, one recites eight hundred times in three sessions over bezoar; if one makes a tilaka mark with it, whoever one wishes comes under one's power.

If one wishes to bring a boy or a girl under one's power, one should make eight thousand fire offerings of white mustard seed before the image. If one takes ash from that place and makes an effigy, whoever's name one speaks comes under one's power.

For the sake of purity, one takes cow's ghee and, at the time when the moon is seized by Rāhu or the sun is seized by Rāhu, puts it in a copper vessel and should recite until the three kinds of accomplishment come about. If it stirs, one becomes able to retain whatever one hears. If it smokes, one gains the power of rejuvenation. If it blazes, one becomes invisible and remembers one's former births.

If one makes fire offerings with a hundred thousand arka flowers, one is granted a hundred thousand coins. One should present eight thousand flowers before the image, and one obtains eight coins. If one makes eight thousand fire offerings of śāli rice and thick gruel smeared with ghee before the image, one obtains five hundred coins. Having done the preliminary practice, one should make eight thousand fire offerings smeared with curd, honey and ghee before the painted image. One obtains three hundred coins. One should make eight thousand fire offerings before the image. One obtains more than a hundred coins.

One who wishes to bring the lord or the lady of a household under his power should make eight thousand fire offerings with kindling sticks of arka before the image, in three sessions over seven nights. The lord of the household comes under one's power. One who wishes to become the lord of a household oneself should make eight thousand fire offerings of dūrvā grass before the image, in three sessions over seven nights, and one becomes the lord of the household. One who wishes to bring the noble Saṅgha under his power for as long as he lives should present eight thousand arka flowers before the painted image. For seven nights one should declare whatever aim one desires and pursues. By reciting constantly one obtains riches.

One should make eight thousand fire offerings of guggulu pills before the painted image. One obtains a thousand pieces of gold. Before the image, for one month, one should make a thousand fire offerings of kunduru incense. One obtains treasures of various kinds. Before the image, one should make eight thousand fire offerings of arka kindling sticks smeared with curd, honey and ghee. One obtains a thousand coins.

One who wishes to bring an enemy under his power, keeping the poṣadha vows, should make eight thousand oblations of mustard seed in a fire of palāśa wood before the image, in three sessions. The enemy comes under one's power. Over the space of one month, one should make eight thousand fire offerings with lac. All people will be delighted. One makes eight thousand fire offerings of śāli rice and thick gruel, and in three sessions one obtains a hundred kārṣāpaṇas. Eating milk and barley gruel, one should recite a hundred thousand times.

Having done the preliminary practice, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight or the eleventh day of the dark fortnight, one takes an undamaged corpse of a man, washes it, adorns it with ornaments, and dresses it in the guise of a courtesan taken as a bride. Having worshipped it with scents, flowers and incense, one presses down firmly on its chest with the left foot, recites the vidyā again and again at the crown of its head, and strikes it with the flat of the hand, until it rises. Having risen, it reveals the past, the future and the present. Then one should strike it with a sword made of iron forged under Puṣya. It turns into the substance of silver and gold. Then one should say, "I do not want this. Give me what I desire!" Then it vomits forth a wish-fulfilling jewel. Taking that, one becomes a vidyādhara of the wish-fulfilling jewel, swift as thought, and lives for an intermediate eon.

Beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight, keeping a fast day and night, one enters a river that flows to the ocean and, for about a month, should let fall into it a hundred thousand jasmine flowers, each the size of a māṣa bean. One obtains ten districts. Beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight, one should offer a hundred thousand lotuses into a river that flows to the ocean, and one finds a hidden treasure. Having done the preliminary practice, one enters that same river and should offer a hundred thousand jasmine flowers. At the end, one should make a hundred thousand fire offerings of black sesame. One obtains ten districts together with their lands.

If one makes pills of aśoka wood, each about the size of a camedaka pulse, and makes a hundred thousand fire offerings of them smeared with curd, honey and ghee before the image, one finds whatever one seeks. By this very rite, using kindling sticks of apāmārga, one obtains a thousand pieces of gold. If one mixes aśoka and ḍeḍeka and makes a hundred thousand fire offerings smeared with apāmārga and the three kinds of rice grain, one obtains a king's daughter and queen.

One who wishes to bring kings together with their ministers under his power should kindle a fire before the image with kindling sticks of aśoka, and for one month make eight thousand fire offerings of aśoka flowers alone, smeared with curd, honey and ghee; one will see treasure in one's own house.

Entering a river that flows to the ocean until the water reaches one's waist, one should offer a hundred thousand hundred-petalled flowers. Then, having recited eight thousand times over a hundred-petalled flower, whoever holds it, or is given it to look at, comes under one's power. One who wishes to bring a king or a king's minister under his power should make eight thousand fire offerings of mustard seed smeared with curd, honey and ghee for one month, and he comes under one's power.

He does whatever one says. To bring a king fully under one's power, one should make eight hundred fire offerings before the image, for one month, in three sessions, in the order just stated: first of mustard seed together with curd and honey, then together with lita, and then together with honey. He will come under one's power.

One who wishes to bring the king's purohita under his power should make fire offerings with puffed rice together with ghee. For a kṣatriya, with it mixed with milk porridge. For a vaiśya, with it together with milk. For a śūdra, with offerings smeared with sesame oil. For all three, with fire offerings of salt. For a widow, with fire offerings of māṣa beans. All sentient beings are brought under one's power with sesame seeds smeared with pungent sesame oil. For all of them there are eight thousand fire offerings in a fire of palāśa wood, at a single sitting, over one month.

Having become pure and keeping a fast day and night, one kindles a fire before the image with kindling sticks of bilva and should make a hundred thousand fire offerings of bilva. One will see treasure. For twenty nights, eating milk and barley gruel, one makes fire offerings of white mustard seed in a fire of palāśa wood, and one finds riches. Eating milk and barley gruel, one should recite five hundred thousand times. Then, before the painted image, for one month, in three sessions, one makes eight thousand fire offerings of white mustard seed smeared with ghee, and causes a stream of riches to fall wherever one wishes. Keeping the fast with regard to food, one should make fire offerings with white mustard seed. This pacifies harm from the lunar mansions.

Before the image, for eight nights, one kindles a fire with bilva wood and should make a hundred thousand fire offerings with sesame. This reveals treasure. Or else one obtains lordship. Having made a vast offering before the image, beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight, for one month, one should make a hundred thousand fire offerings of hundred-petalled flowers in a fire of palāśa wood. One obtains riches as one desires. At a stupa containing relics, one kindles a fire with palāśa wood and should make a hundred thousand fire offerings smeared with curd, honey and ghee. One obtains the enjoyment of ten districts. Before the image, beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight, eating milk and barley gruel, one should offer a hundred thousand lotuses. One finds treasure. Or else one obtains lordship. These alone make up the rite of the kumuda lily; one obtains from the king whatever one seeks.

Before the image one should make a hundred thousand fire offerings of bilva and sesame mixed together. This reveals treasure. Before the image, beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight, one should make a hundred thousand fire offerings of chips of priyaṅgu wood smeared with curd, honey and ghee in a fire of bilva wood. One comes to great wealth. Before the image, keeping a fast day and night, beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight, one should make fire offerings with a hundred thousand lotuses smeared with curd, honey and ghee. One obtains lordship.

Before the painted image one should recite three hundred thousand times. Then one should make three hundred thousand fire offerings of sugarcane kindling sticks, each one finger in length. The painted image will move greatly. Its clusters of flowers will sway, and then one obtains the rank of a kṣatriya, or else whatever one has thought of in one's mind.

To bring a great man under one's power, one should make eight thousand fire offerings before the image of jasmine flowers smeared with curd, honey and ghee, at a single session, over one month. He will come under one's power. To bring a country under one's power, one should make a hundred thousand fire offerings before the image of karavīra flowers smeared with curd, honey and ghee. One obtains lands. One who wishes to become governor of a country should make three hundred thousand fire offerings of cassia flowers smeared with curd, honey and ghee. One becomes lord of the country. This is done in a fire of palāśa wood. One who wishes to become a commander should make a hundred thousand fire offerings before the image of kunda flowers smeared with curd, honey and ghee, and one obtains command. Before the image, in a fire of palāśa wood, one should make ten thousand fire offerings of tangzung flowers smeared with curd, honey and ghee. One becomes lord of a district. Before the image, if one makes three hundred thousand fire offerings of karavīra flowers smeared with curd, honey and ghee, one comes to wear the triple diadem.

Before the image, each day, with offerings made first, beginning at whatever session one likes, one then kindles a fire with arka wood and should make eight thousand fire offerings, each of about a pinch of tree-gold powder smeared with fragrant sesame oil. Within six months one obtains kingdoms. Wealth not yet arisen will arise. Within three years one obtains great kingdoms. By this very same rite one should make fire offerings of iron filings, and within three years one becomes able to bind weapons. By this same rite one should make a hundred thousand fire offerings of oblations of saffron smeared with fragrant sesame oil. One becomes a great lord of wealth. One should make a hundred thousand fire offerings with oblations of every kind of fragrance and oblations of ghee. One becomes governor in whatever place one wishes, or else obtains whatever lands one desires. If one makes a hundred thousand fire offerings of camphor oblations smeared with ghee in a fire of palāśa wood itself, the king will be pleased. In a fire of palāśa wood one should make a hundred thousand fire offerings of sandalwood kindling sticks smeared with fragrant sesame oil. One becomes governor of a great country. One should make a hundred thousand fire offerings of oblations of gold in a fire of palāśa wood. One becomes such that no being can withstand one. If one makes a hundred thousand fire offerings of aguru kindling sticks smeared with ghee, one becomes able to retain whatever one hears. If one makes a hundred thousand fire offerings of pāśaka kindling sticks smeared with fragrant sesame oil, great illness is pacified. If one makes a hundred thousand fire offerings of neem fruit smeared with fragrant sesame oil, one releases whatever bondage one wishes.

Take ghee from a cow whose calf is of the same colour, consecrate it with a hundred thousand recitations, and drink it: one will become supremely sharp of mind.

In a fire of arka wood one should make a hundred thousand fire offerings of arka flowers smeared with fragrant sesame oil. One will find great favor with all beings. All of these fire offerings should be made before a stupa containing relics and before the image. If one consecrates a flower or a fruit with seven recitations, whoever it is given to will be pleased.

One who keeps the poṣadha vows, on the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, at a stupa containing relics, should smear a maṇḍala with cow dung that has not fallen to the ground and make offerings with scents, flowers, incense and the like. Then, kindling a fire before the image with udumbara wood, for one month, at a single sitting, eating the caru oblation food, one should make eight thousand fire offerings with kindling sticks of the brahma tree. One becomes sharp of mind.

To bring a brahmin under one's power, one should make fire offerings of milk before the image for one month. He will come under one's power. To bring a kṣatriya under one's power, if one makes fire offerings of caru before the image, he will come under one's power. To bring a vaiśya under one's power, one should make fire offerings of barley mixed with curd, and he comes under one's power as before. To bring a śūdra under one's power, one should make fire offerings of barley smeared with fragrant sesame oil, and he comes under one's power as before. For others, those whom no one else can overcome, one should make fire offerings smeared with poison, and they come under one's power. By looking at an enemy and reciting, he becomes afraid. With water consecrated by eight hundred recitations, whether the vidyā is applied once or seven times, one's word prevails in the king's palace.

Beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight, one should make eight thousand fire offerings of guggulu pills smeared with ghee before the image in a fire of khadira wood, in three sessions. One obtains whatever one wishes. At a stupa containing relics, eating milk and barley gruel, recite a hundred thousand times; then one should make a hundred thousand fire offerings of sugarcane kindling sticks, each one finger in length. One comes to wear the triple diadem.

One who wishes to accomplish the pills should combine the stamens of cassia flowers, nāgakesara and white sandalwood, make pills the size of a juniper berry, and wrap them in three unequal metals: first in copper, then in silver, then in gold. Then one puts the pills in a casket and, before the Blessed Mother, at a stupa containing relics, keeping a fast day and night, at the time when the moon is seized by Rāhu, performs the rite of offerings and torma, sets them in front, and should recite until they sound forth khaṭa khaṭa. Then one should offer one to the deity who gives prophecies. The others should be given to the servants. One should offer them to the Buddha, the Blessed One, because he is the guru of gurus. Then one should buy them back at a price. Whenever one places one in one's own mouth, one becomes invisible. One should watch for the supreme proclamation. One will live for ten thousand years.

If one makes eight thousand fire offerings before the image of kadamba flowers smeared with curd, honey and ghee, whoever one thinks of comes under one's power. Entering a river that flows to the ocean and keeping a fast, one should offer eight thousand nāgakesara flowers, and one obtains some clothing. Before the image one should offer eight thousand jasmine flowers smeared with curd, honey and ghee. All beings will be pleased. With these kumuda lilies alone the king will be pleased.

To bring a king under one's power, in every case one should make fire offerings smeared with sandalwood powder for one month, and the king comes under one's power. To bring a brahmin under one's power, one should make eight thousand fire offerings of kuruṇṭaka flowers. To bring a vaiśya under one's power, one should make eight thousand fire offerings of saugandhika flowers. To bring a śūdra under one's power, one should make eight thousand fire offerings of kiṃkarāṭa flowers. To bring a girl under one's power, one should make eight thousand fire offerings of yūthikā flowers. These fire offerings should all be made before the image in a fire of vikaṅkata kindling sticks. For a widow, one should make fire offerings of vikaṅkata kindling sticks smeared with ghee.

At a stupa containing relics, before the image, one makes a tilaka mark with bezoar consecrated by seven recitations and should go to the royal palace. Everyone will be pleased. Having recited eight hundred times over one's face, one should go to the royal palace. Everyone will be pleased.

Before the image, one should first make fire offerings of sprouts smeared with ghee in a fire of palāśa wood. Within seven nights the other is pacified. For pacifying oneself, one should make fire offerings of milk together with ghee in that same palāśa fire, in three sessions. Within seven nights there will be pacification.

Before the image, one places ghee in a copper vessel and, at the time when the sun or moon is seized by Rāhu, performs the torma rite and should recite. The vessel stirs. The ghee too becomes accomplished. One should make a tilaka mark on the forehead. All people will be pleased. Drink it, and one becomes sharp of mind.

To gain powers, before the noble Avalokiteśvara, place cow's ghee in a vessel of silver and copper and recite a hundred thousand times according to the rite. Then one should accomplish it at the time of an eclipse, and it becomes accomplished. If one drinks it, powers arise: one gains swiftness, flight, being unobstructed and the like. If one anoints the body with that same ghee and enters a fire, one is not burned. If one enters water, one's feet do not sink in any water at all. If one anoints the hands, it renders red-hot iron harmless.

Eating lotus roots, one takes realgar before the image, places it in one's joined palms, and should recite until the eclipse is over. By making a tilaka mark with it, all living creatures will be pleased. By this same rite, one puts a single māṣa bean in the mouth and should recite until a sprout appears. With the powder of the sprout one brings beings under one's power.

For summoning another, one renders him immobile with the sprout.

One who wishes to accomplish the rite with realgar should place it on an aśvattha leaf before the image and recite a hundred thousand times. When the sun or the moon is seized by the planet in an eclipse, one should accomplish it by the rite. When it is accomplished, if one makes a tilaka mark with it, one becomes invisible.

One who wishes to bring satisfaction should kindle a fire with kindling sticks of a milky-sapped tree, and then make a fire offering of eight thousand kindling sticks of a milky-sapped tree smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. Then the vidyā, together with all that belongs to it, is satisfied.

Go to a solitary place where a brahmarākṣasa or some other being dwells apart, and recite a hundred thousand times. By that it will be accomplished here. It bestows treasure.

Eating milk and barley gruel, install a painted scroll at a stūpa containing relics, and recite for one year. Then, on the eighth or the eleventh day of the dark fortnight, observing a fast day and night, one should make extensive offerings and present torma. To the yakṣas one presents the yakṣa torma: cooked legumes, kākamoṭika, curd, dried cheese, cakes, sokhavadhi, and the like. Outside, having presented a torma for all the bhūtas, one should then, before the painted scroll, in a fire of milky-sapped kindling sticks, make a fire offering of eight thousand kindling sticks of a milky-sapped tree, each a cubit long, smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. As one sits on a mat of kuśa grass, a wealth-giving yakṣa will come. When he stands before one, one should offer him a guest offering of scented water. Then he declares, "Tell me what I am to do for them." If one says, "Yakṣa, carry out my command; let it be so," he becomes invisible. Then he bestows on each of many hundreds in the retinue, one by one, immeasurable divine food. The gods bestow ornaments such as jeweled crowns, elixirs and rejuvenating elixirs, and medicines. Or else, whatever one seeks.

In a place where yakṣiṇīs dwell, make a maṇḍala with cow dung that has not fallen on the ground, and recite a hundred thousand times. Then, on smokeless embers of khadira wood, one should make a fire offering of eight thousand pellets of guggulu smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, continuing until dawn, until the gods one longs for come. Together they bestow a boon. Or else they bestow divine medicine. If one eats it, one lives for an eon.

Gathering śārthi, dūrvā grass, and thorns, one should make a fire offering of eight thousand of them smeared with ghee. One obtains clothing.

Having empowered sweet flag with eight thousand recitations, if one puts it in the mouth, one becomes the foremost speaker in whatever disputes one wishes. Recite over fragrant sesame oil and anoint the mouth with it: one becomes the foremost of speakers in the royal court. Having empowered eye ointment with eight thousand recitations, one should apply it to the eyes as an ointment. One becomes the foremost of speakers in disputes.

When the sun or the moon is eclipsed, put antimony in the mouth and recite until the eclipse is over. Then, having protected it, one should grind it according to the proper rite. Having empowered it with eight thousand recitations, one should apply it to the eyes as an ointment. One becomes invisible, to all beings.

Before the painted scroll, one should make a hundred thousand fire offerings. One sees Śrī. One obtains the boon of her who bestows boons. Keeping silent and eating alms food, recite a hundred thousand times. One becomes invisible. Before the painted scroll, holding the left hand clenched in a fist, recite a hundred thousand times. Then it is accomplished. By clenching the fist one becomes invisible, and by opening it one becomes visible.

At a stūpa containing relics, or on the bank of a river, install the painted scroll and make a fire offering of a hundred thousand lotuses, and one sees Śrī. With māṣa beans, likewise, she bestows a boon. By this same rite, make a fire offering of a hundred thousand blue utpala lotuses, and one sees treasure. Make a fire offering of a hundred thousand pellets of guggulu, and one obtains a hundred thousand gold coins. Make a fire offering of a hundred thousand fragrant flowers, and one obtains ten million garments. With guggulu incense eight hundred times, one obtains what the mind longs for. Before the painted scroll, each day make a fire offering of eight thousand white mustard seeds, and in three days one obtains twenty-five gold coins. By this same rite one should make fire offerings for seven nights. One truly obtains gold coins.

Make an effigy of salt and, cutting it again and again, make a fire offering of it. The man or woman one desires comes under one's power. Even with a quarter of it, one obtains clothing.

One should make a fire offering of eight thousand white mustard seeds smeared with ghee. In three days it pacifies all obstructors.

Placing one foot in water and the other likewise on dry ground, one should recite until the foot standing in the water becomes light. One is freed from evil.

Kindle a fire with arka wood and make a fire offering of eight thousand mustard seeds; in seven days this exhausts the obscuration of karma.

Take equal parts of powdered brāhmī, guḍūcī, sweet flag, and long pepper, and with honey recite over it twenty-one times before the noble Mañjuśrī. Having consecrated it further, do likewise for seven days, and one becomes intelligent. By two weeks of days and nights, one becomes supremely intelligent. By two months of this practice, one retains whatever one hears. Doing eight thousand recitations before the painted scroll or before the image, one is afterward able to read. Likewise, each day one should recite in silence. One becomes intelligent.

Whether one is bound or imprisoned, merely by reciting one is freed. By reciting while looking at robbers, one cannot be harmed by robbers. Having empowered sesame oil with eight thousand recitations, anoint the head with it, and all people will be pleased.

Before the Buddha, the Blessed One, smear a maṇḍala, strew it with flowers, empower a palmful of water with seven recitations, and one should drink it. In seven days one becomes intelligent. It removes earlier faults of speech.

Recite eight hundred times over one measure of brāhmī juice, one measure of milk, and one measure of honey, and one should drink it each day, for as long as twenty-one nights. One becomes intelligent, able to grasp five hundred verses, to hold them, and to preserve them.

Reciting seven times over water and pouring it on the head binds the protective circle. Reciting twenty-one times over a khadira peg, together with guggulu incense, causes it to be revealed. For curing poison, use water and a knife. With a leafy twig recited over seven times, one overcomes grahas. With white flowers or guggulu incense, this is for those seized by grahas. With bathing or with a thread, one binds oneself in protection. At night one should make a fire offering of white mustard seed mixed with sesame and smeared with ghee, and it will grant a boon.

At a stūpa containing relics, on the full moon, first smear a maṇḍala; then, with eight full vases and eight garlands, and burning incense of aloeswood, turuṣka, sandalwood, and kunduru, one should recite. One is granted bodily accomplishment.

At a stūpa containing relics, eating milk and barley gruel, and having made offerings as one can afford, one should recite a hundred thousand times. One becomes able to perform rites such as stupefying and bewildering.

Eating flour and entering the water of a river, one should recite a hundred thousand times. One becomes able to perform subjugation, invisibility, and accomplishments with realgar and the like.

At an abode of nāgas, one should make a fire offering of gathered karbāpa. The nāgas come under one's power. One finds whatever one seeks.

Having empowered the fingers of the right hand with protection, recite in the king's presence. He comes under one's power. By this very rite alone one frightens kings, buffaloes, tigers, leopards, and the like. By a fire offering of sesame one brings the rasavatī under one's power. By selling flesh one protects oneself and protects others. Empowered with seven recitations, one binds the crown knot. By reciting in battle, and in a dispute at the royal palace, one becomes victorious.

One who wishes to consecrate with water should take four vases free of flaws at the base, of blackening, and the like, adorn their mouths with leafy twigs, put in flowing water, scents, and all kinds of seeds, and empower them with eight thousand recitations. If one consecrates oneself with that water, one is freed from all obstructors and misleading forces. For thirst and fever, empower scented water with eight hundred recitations and sprinkle it, and one returns to one's natural state.

For a vetāla, by the application performed with a khadira peg, having strenuously and properly prepared the device, place four men holding swords in the four directions, sit close at its heart, and make a fire offering of iron filings with an iron ladle. Its tongue will certainly come out of its mouth. Cut it off with a sharp sword, and it becomes a sword like a blue utpala. By taking it, one rises up together with one's retinue and becomes a king of vidyādharas. One lives for a hundred and ten million years. When the time comes, one is reborn among the gods.

Having made a forehead plate of iron possessing the proper characteristics, one should recite a hundred thousand times before the painted scroll. Having remained in retreat for seven nights, make a burnt offering completing a thousand. Then, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, observing a fast for three nights, make extensive offerings, perform the rite of torma, and carry out the protection, the boundary, the binding of the maṇḍala, and the like. Having offered a feast to the noble Saṅgha as best one can, and having bowed at their feet, one should request permission from the noble Saṅgha. Before the painted scroll make a heap of white mustard seed, and over it one should offer recitation upon recitation.

For all incursions of grahas, use guggulu incense. It fully pacifies all untimely death. For suppressing all winds and clouds, use recitation. Reciting over white mustard seed and pressing it, one should scatter it into the sky, and water becomes still. Reciting seven times over a khadira peg, one should drive it into the ground. All enemies or weapons are suppressed.

For all fights, disputes, and quarrels, empower a five-colored thread with eight hundred recitations and tie it on a hidden place of the body; unrest, fights, disputes, and quarrels are subdued. For all poisons and mantras, reciting seven times over water, one should make a fire offering, and they become harmless.

One who desires wealth, being pure and wearing clean clothes, observing a fast day and night, should offer kunduru incense before the painted scroll. In a dream it shows what is virtuous and nonvirtuous. By reciting seven thousand times, it gives silver. For causing division among all, use ashes.

One who seeks wealth should install the painted scroll at a confluence of rivers or at a pond, in a clean spot, and begin recitation and fire offering. One should make a hundred thousand fire offerings of lotuses smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, or else two hundred thousand. Then one obtains all one desires. By three hundred thousand fire offerings one becomes invisible. By three hundred thousand fire offerings one obtains a kingdom of one's own. By two million one hundred thousand fire offerings one becomes a great lord of wealth. One obtains whatever one undertakes. One accomplishes travel through the sky, invisibility, driving in the ritual dagger, and the like.

One should burn a hundred thousand dūrvā grasses smeared with ghee. In seven days one prospers. One should make eight thousand fire offerings smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. In twenty-one nights one prospers. One obtains a thousand gold coins.

One should set it upon molasses, and all enemies become paralyzed.

Having made a maṇḍala of cow dung, place a thread in the center of the secret maṇḍala, offer guggulu incense, and one should recite the mantra. If the person will live, the thread dances. If the person will not live, it does not dance.

Having made a maṇḍala of cow dung four cubits across, offer flowers and incense, and remaining there one should recite. For enemies, reciting over it seven times each, one should bury it in the ground.

All curses and hostile sorcery come to nothing.

Against the army of an enemy, recite over a staff and one should throw it there. There will be no harm.

For possession by the forgetfulness-causing spirit, kindle a fire with apāmārga kindling sticks and make a fire offering, burning black sesame and white karavīra flowers. It destroys the forgetfulness-causing graha. For all grahas one should tie on a black thread. For cutting off sudden fright, tumors, blisters, foul sores, and mange, use white earth, and there will be no harm to any being.

When the sun or the moon is eclipsed, observe a fast, recite over sesame oil, smear the face with the sesame oil, and one should enter the house of an enemy. He will come to have a mind of loving-kindness. By this same rite, having empowered a protective cord with eight hundred recitations, tie it on the hand, and one should enter battle. One becomes invincible to others.

Rising at the proper time, make a maṇḍala at a stūpa containing relics, recite seven times over each of three palmfuls of water, and one should drink them. One should cook while reciting mentally, until it is done. Then recite three times over the first mouthful of food, and, having recited eight hundred times outside the proper time, one should set it aside. All the obscurations of karma are purified. Speech too becomes completely pure, and each day one retains a hundred ślokas. Likewise, for seven days, by reciting seven times over water.

Wrapping realgar inside an aśvattha leaf, one should recite before the painted scroll until the three kinds of accomplishment appear. Before the image one should make a fire offering with eight thousand apāmārga kindling sticks. The king, together with the king's ministers, comes under one's power.

One observing the poṣadha vows, drinking only milk or eating leaves, should recite three hundred thousand times at a stūpa containing relics. Then, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight or the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one should make a fire offering of eight thousand black sesame seeds. One obtains a thousand kārṣāpaṇas.

Before the image make a fire offering of eight thousand pellets of guggulu. Whatever man or woman one desires comes under one's power. Make a fire offering of eight thousand pellets of guggulu. All people are pleased. Or else, one commands speech in the royal palace.

Putting sweet flag in the mouth, one should recite until the three kinds of accomplishment appear. When it grows warm, it brings others under one's power. When it gives off smoke, one becomes invisible. When it blazes, one travels through the sky.

If, having installed the painted scroll at a stūpa containing relics, one makes a fire offering of a hundred thousand lotuses, beginning on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, the king comes under one's power.

Have a craftsman who observes the poṣadha vows make a wooden staff of red sandalwood, sixteen finger-widths long. Then, before the painted scroll, observing a fast day and night, one should recite three hundred thousand times. On the full moon, having made extensive offerings, take the wooden staff in the right hand, and one should recite until the three kinds of accomplishment appear. When it grows warm, all whom one wishes to have speak will quickly speak. When it gives off smoke, one becomes invisible. When it blazes, one travels through the sky.

Having covered the painted scroll entirely with a white cloth, one should recite until it blazes. One flies up together with a retinue of a thousand.

Before the painted scroll, eating milk and barley gruel, keeping silent, on a seat spread with kuśa grass, beginning on the first day of the month and continuing until the full moon, one should recite one million six hundred thousand times. Making a fire offering of eight thousand udumbara kindling sticks dispels all illness.

Then, having made an iron lotus six or eight finger-widths across, install the painted scroll at a stūpa containing relics, and one should recite at the three times of day. One should recite five hundred thousand times. Afterward, having made extensive offerings and observing a fast for three nights, place the lotus before the painted scroll, and one should recite until it blazes. Merely by taking it up, one's hair, together with that of one's retinue, becomes curled and coiled. Recite ten million times mentally, and it will be accomplished. Whatever one thinks of is brought to perfection, lacking nothing.

In whatever direction one travels, recite seven times over a clod of earth and one should throw it. All the vicious are suppressed. Having empowered a garment, one should wear it. One becomes unobstructed in every undertaking. If one wipes the face with it, one becomes the foremost of speakers. It makes one gravely poisoned rise up again. It frees one from bhūta grahas. It renders obstructors powerless.

If the painted scroll is installed in a house, one becomes the master of the house. If it is installed on a heap of grain, the grain increases. Likewise, if one installs it on a leaf, that brings its accomplishment. In the same way, immeasurable praise of one's qualities arises.

Then, if one wishes to perform pacifying, make a fire offering of eight thousand fragrant flowers smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. One becomes supremely at peace. For increasing, kindle a fire with kindling sticks of a milky-sapped tree, and make a fire offering of eight thousand portions of sesame, thick rice gruel, peas, lentils, and the like, smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. There is supreme increase.

Whether with the painted scroll or without it, one observing the poṣadha vows, having taken up the three refuges, generates the awakening mind. One should recite ten thousand times. Then, on the full moon, when the moon is eclipsed, having given torma to all who have desires, observe a fast day and night, and one should recite throughout the night. Then one becomes able to perform all rites. One takes up all distinctions by oneself. Merely by wiping with it, one restores life. Empower water with seven recitations. If it is quickly drunk, one returns to one's natural state.

For grahas and living creatures, make a fire offering of a thousand white mustard seeds. Having settled oneself at the entrance of an asura cave and remaining there steadfastly, one should recite a hundred thousand times. An asura maiden will surely come and lead one inside. Dwelling there, one finds whatever one seeks. One dwells wherever one wishes.

On the shore of the ocean, install the painted scrolls one by one, and by reciting a hundred thousand times over the painted scroll, even Sāgara the nāga king will admit one into his own abode. There one should seek the wish-fulfilling jewel. Having taken it, one will enjoy all that one desires. One will travel in the fields of the tathāgatas. One will live for an eon and become unobstructed.

Having empowered a thread spun by a young girl with eight thousand recitations, one ties knots in it. All obstructors and misleading forces become bound.

At a river or on an island, eating alms food, one should recite three hundred thousand times. One becomes invisible. Eating caru, recite a hundred thousand times at a confluence of rivers. One becomes invisible. One becomes lord of all the invisible ones.

One who is properly restrained should take an alms bowl in the right hand, sit in the cross-legged posture, and recite before the painted scroll until it blazes. One becomes a vidyādhara. One lives for an eon and is honored by all the hosts of vidyādharas. For the alms bowl, the ringed staff, and the like, it is by this same rite. When the sun or the moon is eclipsed, a monk should accomplish it, doing everything by this alone. He lives for an eon, practicing pure conduct, travels without obstruction, and acts just as he wishes.

Eating cow's urine and barley gruel, one should recite three hundred thousand times. One obtains eight districts, each of one's own.

With pusīlāka leaves one destroys scorpions, spiders, and all poisons. By reciting two hundred thousand times one averts at all times the hour of death by snakebite. One becomes an abode of jasmine flowers.

Smear mallikā, utpala, kumuda, saugandhika, and the like with curd, honey, and ghee, and make eight thousand fire offerings at the three sessions. Whether it be a king, a king's minister, or a brahmin chaplain, in seven nights one brings him under one's power.

For one whose vidyā has declined, write with saffron on a leaf of birch bark, and one should recite a hundred times before the Blessed One at a stūpa containing relics. By dawn it will be restored to fullness.

Recite seven times over white mustard seed and scatter it in a village or a town. The beings there will fall asleep like logs until the sun rises.

If one wishes to bring a woman or a man under one's power, face the direction in which that person's house lies, and if one recites eight thousand times at night, one is granted a sight of the person in a dream, and in seven days the person comes under one's power.

By reciting seven times over water, one binds the lips of all fanged creatures. One binds treasure. For binding treasure, recite twenty-one times over a khadira peg and drive pegs at the four corners of the place of the treasure. The treasure will be bound.

If one empowers a palmful of water with seven recitations and sprinkles it on water, fierce outcastes will be unable to kill the fish. Make a fire offering of eight thousand śephālikā flowers. It makes one invisible. By reciting seven times over horse dung, one gives it as fumigation. It destroys frogs. By reciting seven times, whether over flowers or fruits, one destroys flies. For subjugation, at the king's gate, give a tooth-stick to one who chews tooth-sticks, give fruit, and give scent.

For binding the ground, binding robbers, paralyzing all fanged creatures, breaking bolts, paralyzing fire, drawing out poison, transferring poison, binding poison, bringing bhūtas under one's power, freeing from the graha of ḍākinīs, sending fever, protecting oneself, protecting others, raising a vetāla, entering a cave, and binding the boundaries, it is by mere recitation.

One who wishes to become invisible should empower the root of the śatāvarī plant with a thousand recitations; hold it in the hand, and one becomes invisible.

Having recited before the painted scroll, afterward take eight flowers bought at a hero's price, and one should make a fire offering of them smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. By doing it to the measure of the original price, one obtains a hundredfold price.

Then, when the moon is eclipsed, having made offerings of scent, flowers, and incense beneath a bodhi tree, take one measure of realgar and place it on seven aśvattha leaves. Having subdued the body, one should set it down. In that very instant it arises, and one becomes a vidyādhara. One becomes unobstructed by all gods, nāgas, and yakṣas. Having the divine ear, swift as thought, with the color of the rising sun, one becomes much sought after by all vidyādharas. One is surrounded by hundreds of vidyādharas.

One who wishes to accomplish gorocana should recite a hundred thousand times while eating milk and barley gruel. When the moon is eclipsed, placing it upon leaves of the saptaparṇa tree, set out the gorocana at a stūpa containing relics, and one should accomplish it by the rite as it has been taught, until it blazes. If one makes a tilaka mark with it, one becomes a vidyādhara adorned with ornaments, taking whatever form one desires. One lives for a thousand years.

One who wishes to accomplish the eye ointment should take one measure of sauvīra, heat it well with fire, and become versed in the practices of eye ointment. When the moon is eclipsed, entering the water, one should recite until it becomes a kumbhāṇḍa. Merely by applying it for an instant, one becomes a splendid vidyādhara, fully adorned with every ornament, unharmed by the vidyādharas who wear earrings and crowns, and one flies up together with one's retinue. One lives for five thousand years.

One should make a fire offering of a hundred thousand lotuses or utpalas. One obtains a thousand gold coins each time. One should make a fire offering of a hundred thousand palāśa kindling sticks. One obtains a thousand gold coins.

Observing a fast for three nights and eating milk and barley gruel, one should accomplish it. It brings the king under one's power.

Kindle a fire with kindling sticks of a milky-sapped tree, and for seven days, with white mustard seed smeared with curd, honey, and ghee, for seven days or for twice seven, at the three sessions, make eight thousand fire offerings. Even those of superior understanding come under one's power.

For bringing a king's minister under one's power, kindle a fire with arka wood and make a fire offering of black mustard seed for seven days, and he comes under one's power.

For bringing the four castes under one's power, before the painted scroll, for seven days, at the three sessions, make eight thousand fire offerings of black sesame smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. All beings come under one's power. By this same rite make a fire offering of sesame. It brings all beings under one's power.

Make a fire offering of a hundred thousand arka kindling sticks. One obtains a hundred measures of gold. Make a fire offering of pināka wood. All people become pleased. Make a fire offering of a hundred thousand portions of betel powder. One will have a crown bound on one's head. With the right hand one dispels diseases of the eye. For one stricken with fever, by sweeping with kuśa grass. Recite eight hundred times over a thread spun by a young girl and tie it on. One becomes fortunate.

Kindle a fire with arka wood and make a fire offering of a hundred thousand sesame seeds. Inexhaustible food will appear. Gather all the grains in one place and make a fire offering of a hundred thousand. All the grains become inexhaustible. Make a fire offering of the banyan tree with its hanging roots. One's goods will never run out. Make a fire offering of a hundred thousand pieces of the honey tree. Wealth will arise.

Combine realgar, ox bile, and bamboo manna, empower the mixture with eight thousand recitations before the painted scroll, place it on a leaf of the bodhi tree, and recite. Then by that the gorocana will be accomplished. Whatever woman or man it is given to comes under one's power.

Make a fire offering of eight thousand oblations of parched rice, for as long as seven days. One becomes free of obstructors. Before the painted scroll make a fire offering of a hundred thousand dongka flowers. One obtains a hundred and twenty million fine garments. Make a fire offering of barley flour together with curd. For as long as one lives, one will never lack food. Make a fire offering of a thousand oblations of ghee. One obtains a village. By reciting ten million times one becomes a vidyādhara with a retinue of a hundred.

One who wishes to bring a woman or a man under one's power should recite twenty-one times over pellets of guggulu and make a fire offering of them. The person whose name is spoken comes under one's power. If one recites twenty-one times over sweet flag and puts it in the mouth, one becomes the foremost of speakers. Recite a hundred thousand times on the road. One obtains whatever delicious food and drink one takes. Make a fire offering of a hundred thousand. One becomes endowed with glory. Make a fire offering of a hundred thousand portions of sesame and thick rice gruel together with māṣa beans. One brings under one's power whomever one wishes.

Kindle a fire of sindhuvāra and make a fire offering of the first portion of everything cooked. As it is accomplished, one's food never runs out. One obtains the crown one desires. Make a fire offering of a hundred thousand nimba flowers. All people become pleased. Make a fire offering of unbroken śāli rice and thick gruel. One obtains a village.

Kindle a fire with aśoka wood and make a fire offering of a hundred thousand divine oblations. One obtains, each in turn, whatever maiden one seeks. Before the painted scroll, burning incense of aloeswood, one recites a hundred thousand times. Then the king of that land will do as one commands.

One observing the poṣadha vows, eating alms food or caru, should recite five hundred thousand times, and one obtains a kingdom on earth. Eating milk and barley gruel, one should recite eight hundred thousand times and offer a hundred thousand white lotuses. One obtains kingdoms everywhere.

If one makes a fire offering of a hundred thousand dūrvā grasses and coral, one becomes long-lived. Make a fire offering of a hundred thousand white mustard seeds. One is freed from illness. With a vessel of milk, make a fire offering of a hundred thousand mango leaves. One is freed from all illness. Making a fire offering of a hundred thousand priyaṅgu kernels, one obtains gold coins to that same measure. Make a fire offering of eight thousand oblations of milk. One is freed from illness. If one seeks food, make a fire offering of food.

Climbing to the summit of a mountain and eating alms food, one should recite three hundred thousand times. At the end, observing a fast for three nights, kindle a fire with aśvattha wood and make a fire offering of sesame smeared with curd, honey, and ghee throughout the night. One becomes a king. By a fire offering of sesame and ghee one accomplishes everything. Make a fire offering of honey. All people become pleased. Make a fire offering of ghee. One becomes endowed with splendor. Make a fire offering of milk. There will be peace. Make a fire offering of curd. There will be increase.

On the summit of a mountain, at a stūpa containing the essence of dependent arising, a stūpa containing relics, remain there and offer a hundred thousand lotuses. One becomes a king or the lord of a land. Even if the rites are not accomplished, one obtains a hundred districts.

For bringing a king under one's power and for drawing him in, when the moon is eclipsed, have the ghee of a tawny cow placed in a copper vessel, and one should recite over a copper spoon until the three kinds of accomplishment appear. When bubbles arise, one will retain whatever one hears. When it gives off smoke, one becomes invisible. When it blazes, one travels through the sky.

Having done the preliminary practice, beginning on the first day of the bright fortnight and continuing until the full moon, hang garlands of flowers and a canopy all around, make a maṇḍala one span across with fragrant scents, make offerings of various kinds of scents and flowers, present torma, and one should offer eight thousand lamps of ghee.

Then, on the full moon, one should sit cross-legged and recite until one hears from somewhere the sound baghastanita. Then signs will quickly arise: the flower garlands sway, the tips of the lamp flames grow, rays of light appear, and the painted image moves. When one has seen these, whatever one is practicing will be accomplished, and one's negative deeds will also be exhausted.

One who wishes to bring under control gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas should, before the painted image, for seven nights in three sessions, kindle a fire with charcoal of acacia wood and make eight thousand fire offerings of salt, sesame, and white mustard seed mixed with curd, honey, and ghee. They will come under control.

Empower any one of water, ash, or white mustard seed with eight thousand recitations and scatter it in the four directions. The binding of the maṇḍala will thereby be accomplished.

Before the painted image, offer torma of various kinds and make vast offerings; place gorocanā on a lotus petal, sit cross-legged, and one should recite until the three kinds of accomplishment occur. From an unusual scent, one brings all beings under control and lives for a thousand years. When it grows warm, one lives for a thousand years, travels thousands of yojanas, and returns to that very place. One becomes king of all the accomplished ones, accomplishes things by mind alone, and produces food by mind alone. Then, when it blazes, one appears with the color of the rising sun, in the form of a sixteen-year-old, with hair of a bronze hue, living for an eon, and, surrounded by many hundreds of thousands of vidyādharas, one goes wherever one wishes.

Having done the preliminary practice, before the painted image, in the fortnight of the Month of Miracles, bathe three times a day and change one's clothes three times, and recite eight thousand times in three sessions, until the full moon. At the end, fasting for three nights, one should accomplish the outer robe. Anoint it thoroughly with all kinds of scents, light eight thousand lamps, and sit cross-legged; smear a maṇḍala with scents, place the robe upon it, press it down with the left hand, and one should recite until it flies up. At once it flies up to the height of a palm tree. While it stays at just that height, one should pay homage to all the buddhas and bodhisattvas and take it. As soon as one has taken it, one becomes a vidyādhara. Gods, nāgas, yakṣas, garuḍas, and mahoragas will line up before one, pay homage, and become one's servants. When one constantly recites over the robe, then, by directing one's mind, one makes a person of malicious mind fall down; by reciting again mentally, one makes him rise.

Make a pellet of fresh butter, place it on four aśvattha leaves, and one should recite until it becomes warm. Eat it without touching it with the teeth. Merely by eating it, whatever one thinks of will all come about: many objects of desire, the strength of ten men, and one lives for ten thousand years.

Having done the preliminary practice, on the full moon, before the painted image, fasting for three nights, make offerings with scents, flowers, and so on to a stūpa containing relics. Then place a sword made of kuśa grass on seven aśvattha leaves, take it up in the fingers of the fist, and one should recite until it emits light. By taking it up, one travels through the sky, and no being will be able to do one harm.

With ash, a fence of fire is made. With water or gravel, the directions are bound.

Take natural collyrium, recite over it twenty-one times, and apply it to the eyes: all people will be pleased with one. Empower collyrium, tagara, costus, sweet flag, lotus filaments, gorocanā, nāgakesara, and musk with eight thousand recitations and anoint oneself all over: everyone will be pleased.

Empower salt with twenty-one recitations; if one scatters it facing toward someone's house, within seven days that person will come under control. If one empowers a handful of water seven times, whoever bathes in it or drinks it comes under control. By reciting twenty-one times over whatever one sees, one brings under control all that one sees. With a hundred thousand fire offerings of guggulu, one wins over the kṣatriyas, each one. By offering blue lotuses, white water lilies, white lotuses, and so on, one brings under control whomever one wishes.

During an eclipse of the moon, fasting for three nights, make offerings for one night; then, to the right of one's body, smear a maṇḍala with red sandalwood, press the maṇḍala with the right hand, and one should recite while calling out, or until the earth of the maṇḍala turns black. The hand becomes accomplished. By clenching the fist, one becomes invisible.

To accomplish the topknot, begin on the first day of the bright fortnight and recite until the juncture of the month. Then, having empowered the topknot with eight hundred recitations, go on the alms round; when one is seen in that way by those who give alms, at that time it is accomplished. On the first day, one round of begging; likewise up to the seventh day. Even one who lacks merit accomplishes it.

During an eclipse of the moon, recite over milk and drink it: it becomes a great elixir. With a hundred burnt offerings of kindling sticks of vāśaka, one brings under control whomever one wishes.

Empower a sword with eight hundred recitations and place it at the door of a cave or of a temple. By bowing toward the cast-metal door panels, one opens the door. Reciting once, one protects oneself. Through burnt offerings of milk, women come under control. By mind alone one paralyzes accomplished secret mantras. One opens all secret mantras. One brings asura maidens under control. Through burnt offerings of all kinds of scents, women of the kṣatriya class come under control. Through fire offerings of pure deodar, tīrthika ascetics and renunciants come under control.

With the hand placed at the heart, recite a hundred times. This thoroughly pacifies all negative deeds and summons all beings. Place the hand on the head and recite eight hundred times. This paralyzes beings and thoroughly pacifies negative deeds. If one recites over a bilva fruit and gives it away, it summons all beings. To the right of the deity's body one should recite countless times. Women and men, boys and old men too will come under control. By empowering ash seven times, one should make it into armor. No being can break through it. Reciting eight hundred times over water, let it be applied to the limbs: illness will be pacified.

Fasting for a day and a night, make a sword of acacia wood, take it up on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, and in a charnel ground one should recite until it blazes. Having taken it up, one will travel without obstruction. One becomes a sword vidyādhara, with bronze-hued, curling hair, living for an eon, and much sought after by all vidyādharas.

Or else, during an eclipse of the sun or the moon, having done the preliminary practice, rise at dawn and make offerings to the painted image; eating food obtained by begging, and with gifts, one should have accomplishment bestowed. Then the activities of speech will be fully accomplished. Make eight thousand fire offerings of dūrvā grass and coral mixed with curd, honey, and ghee. This frees those who are bound.

To make oneself supreme, recite eight thousand times over gorocanā and make a mark on the forehead with it; if one then goes to the king's palace, one will be supremely praised. So too in receiving and in speaking.

To bring a girl under control, make eight thousand fire offerings of jasmine flowers. One obtains the girl. By this same rite one obtains a woman in her full bloom. All fevers, all grahas, and all seals too are released when that word is given. It cures all poisons. It frees from grahas.

The activities of speech itself are these: it turns back elephants; it turns back thorns; it paralyzes bandits and armies, paralyzes weapons, paralyzes chariots, paralyzes fire, and paralyzes boats; it summons; it brings down possession on those with fangs or even those without fangs; it raises the dead; and it dispatches them and fevers.

Eating milk and barley flour, recite a hundred thousand times. Fasting for three nights and wearing clean clothes, at a solitary liṅga (ekaliṅga), set it down on kuśa grass, make great offerings, make a torma for all the bhūtas, and, staying to the right of the deity's body, combine orpiment, realgar, collyrium, madder, and gorocanā, wrap them inside an aśvattha leaf, and one should recite until the three kinds of accomplishment appear: it grows warm, it gives off smoke, and it blazes. When it grows warm, one gains the use of the magic sandals and lives for five thousand years. One brings all beings under control. When it gives off smoke, one becomes invisible and can live for a thousand years. When it blazes, one becomes the vidyādhara who is lord over all vidyādharas. One has a lifespan of an eon, and by reciting a hundred thousand times more and more, one attains supernormal knowledge of speech. One binds above and below and all the directions, seizes with certainty, and one's word too goes unobstructed.

Then, if one wishes to accomplish a vetāla, take a corpse with its limbs intact, and whether in a charnel ground, at a lone tree, at a crossroads, or at a solitary liṅga, honor all the bhūtas with torma, smear a maṇḍala to the right of the body of the Great God, and offer torma. Bathe the corpse and adorn it with ornaments, draw a maṇḍala with ash, lay it in the center with its head pointing east, and cover the body with a white cloth. Having stationed a good companion to guard the directions, sit cross-legged upon it, and in its mouth make fire offerings of sesame and white mustard seed until it brings forth a jewel from its mouth. By taking that jewel from its mouth, one becomes a vidyādhara with bronze-hued, curling hair, the color of the rising sun, possessing the strength of a thousand elephants, taking whatever form one desires, going to the abodes of the gods, living for a great eon, and going wherever one wishes.

Another vetāla rite: by this same procedure, take a man's corpse, empower four pegs of acacia wood, and with this very mantra protect oneself, and likewise guard the directions. Sit upon it and make burnt offerings of ghee until a tongue comes out of its mouth. One should cut it with the sword empowered earlier, and so on until a hundred tongues have come out. By taking that very tongue, one flies together with a retinue of a hundred. One becomes the supreme among vidyādharas, and it becomes a weapon. One lives for a great eon.

On the eighth day of the dark fortnight, or on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one should grind antimony collyrium at night. Empower it with eight thousand recitations and apply it to the eyes, and one brings all beings under control. One should recite over scented paste and anoint oneself, and one brings all beings under control. Recite over incense and fumigate oneself with it, and one brings all beings under control. Recite over a flower and place it on one's head, and one brings all beings under control and delights them. Recite over the crown-knot and tie it: there will be protection everywhere, and the binding of all beings as well.

One who wishes to bring a widow under control should make fire offerings of black gram. She will come under control at once. To bring a yakṣiṇī under control, make eight thousand fire offerings of lotuses. She will come within three nights. If she has not come by then, she is made to come within seven nights. She will grant boons. She fulfills everything just as one wishes. If one wants a girl, make fire offerings of parched rice. One obtains the girl one desires. If one wants Śrī, make fire offerings of lotuses. Padmā or Śrī will come. If one wants victory, make fire offerings of curd. One will always be victorious.

If one wishes for increase, make fire offerings of ghee. One will obtain wealth.

Remaining pure at all times, to bring under control the piśācas within five nights, the yakṣas and rākṣasas within nine nights, the nāga kings within ten nights, the gandharvas and the water-born beings within half a month, the asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and goddesses within twenty-one days, all the hosts within twenty-two nights, and the king's queen within a month, make eight thousand fire offerings of sweet-tasting ears of grain mixed with curd, honey, and ghee. They will come under control.

To bring men and women under control, make a hundred thousand fire offerings of white mustard seed mixed with curd. One obtains wealth. Make a hundred thousand fire offerings of red oleander and cassia flowers. One obtains a princess. Make a hundred thousand fire offerings of bilva fruit mixed with curd. Śrī will arise in one's house. Make a hundred thousand fire offerings of hundred-petaled flowers mixed with curd. One obtains a hundred coins. Make a hundred thousand fire offerings of kindling sticks of the golden-colored tree. One obtains a thousand cattle each time. Make a hundred thousand fire offerings of flowers. One obtains lands one after another. Make a hundred thousand fire offerings of kindling sticks of arka. One obtains a thousand coins. Make a hundred thousand burnt offerings of fresh butter. One obtains five districts, one after another. Make a hundred thousand fire offerings of white lotus flowers. One obtains four koṭis of garments. Make a hundred thousand burnt offerings of milk. One obtains cattle and wealth in full measure. Make a hundred thousand fire offerings of kindling sticks of the bodhi tree. Without having to take anything, it makes one's house prosperous. Make a hundred thousand fire offerings of jasmine flowers. One obtains a hundred pairs of embroidered garments. Make a hundred thousand burnt offerings of milk rice. Within seven nights one brings brahmins under control. Make a hundred thousand fire offerings of white water lilies. One obtains a wife together with riches.

Climb to the summit of a mountain and recite a hundred thousand times. The king of whatever land one recites in will come, and without one's having sought it, one will be fully endowed with sons and with all wealth. He protects one together with one's children.

Enter a river that flows to the ocean and cast in a hundred thousand fragrant flowers. Afterward the flowers will come back against the current. One should eat them without touching them with the teeth. Each day one will take in five hundred passages of scripture and retain them.

Having done the preliminary practice, recite a hundred thousand times before the image. Then go to wherever a treasure lies, smear with fragrant scent vases that are all sound and without blemish, fill them completely with white sandalwood and water, empower them with eight thousand recitations, and one should place them at the site of the rite. All the earth will split open. Even a treasure will be made to rest at the depth of a man's height. Water does no harm; the treasure stays on top. By mere recollection, all harms are pacified.

Naming a woman who does not desire one, recite over ghee and drink it. One will become fortunate in love.

The means of accomplishing the vajra: make a three-pronged vajra sixteen finger-widths long from iron obtained under Puṣya, anoint it with red sandalwood, make vast offerings to the painted image, and, paying homage each day, one should eat alms food. At the end, fasting for a night, at a stūpa containing relics, set up the painted image and make vast offerings, light a hundred lamps, and sit on a mat of kuśa grass; holding both ends of the vajra in the hands, one should recite until it takes hold. One should fly in seven circuits, and one will become a universal monarch among the vidyādharas. One lives for a great eon.

In the month of Puṣya, beneath an aśoka tree, fasting for three nights, make eight thousand fire offerings of black pepper, and put one peppercorn in the mouth: whoever one looks at will come under control.

On the eighth day of the dark fortnight or the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, fasting for a day and a night and wearing clean clothes, offer lamps, banners, flower garlands, and so on before the painted image. Place water that one has prepared oneself in a copper vessel, recite over it for one period and drink it, and again by the same rite throughout the whole night. At dawn one should eat alms food as directed by the Saṅgha. After eating, eat also ghee, flour, and pomegranates, and then sleep will come. The fields of knowledge from the four directions enter one's mouth, and one will retain whatever one hears.

Enter a river that flows to the ocean, clench the right hand into a fist, and recite for thirteen days. One makes all who have died of poison and of fangs rise again. With the fist one makes all grahas enter a person, and also sets the person free.

With cow dung that has not fallen to the ground, smear a maṇḍala four cubits across, and on the eighth day of the dark fortnight make fire offerings of kindling sticks of karśara mixed with curd, honey, and ghee, eight thousand each day, up to the fourteenth. In this rite, one wins the favor of the palace of an angry king. With companions, go into a forest, draw a man with charcoal of kupiti wood, press it with the left foot, and one should recite eight thousand times. Then he will be free of anger.

Having done the preliminary practice, take a six-finger stick of wood struck by lightning and, fasting for three nights, set up the painted image at a stūpa containing relics. Furnish that peg with the three metals, and one should place it upon a thousand-petaled lotus with four vases filled with all kinds of medicines. Then press the peg with the left foot, hold it with the left hand, and one should recite until the hand grows numb. Then the hand is released. Then at dawn give a great torma and one should eat pomegranate: it will be accomplished. One should drive that peg into another house: it will grant what one desires, and all necessities will come about. When it is pulled out, everything will vanish.

Kindle a fire with jasmine wood and make eight thousand fire offerings of flowers mixed with curd, honey, and ghee. One obtains five coins.

Kindle a fire with mango wood, and on the bank of a river one should make eight thousand fire offerings of kindling sticks of arka mixed with curd, honey, and ghee. Within five days one obtains five coins. Beginning on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, make fire offerings of eight thousand kindling sticks of aśoka mixed with milk, up to the fifteenth. One obtains a hundred coins. Kindle a fire with oleander wood, and from the eighth day of the bright fortnight up to the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight make eight thousand fire offerings of oleander shavings mixed with milk. One obtains a thousand coins each time.

Empower well-strained water, and one should use it for seven days. Then a cowherd for whom protection has been made should milk a tawny cow. Then one should place its milk in a vase in a secluded spot and recite over it. Then, having churned it, one should have a brahmin girl grind these substances with her hands. Then have pills made and wrapped all around with the three metals. Put the pills into the five products of that same tawny cow, and one should leave them for one night. Then take them out, and one should wash them with the cow's urine. One should place them on a lotus petal anointed with gorocanā. Then, having invited the painted image to be set up at a stūpa containing relics, perform the rite of purification and make vast offerings, with torma and lamps as well. Then the vidyādhara takes eight pills, goes to a lotus pond with lotus petals folded together, sets up the painted image, and makes fire offerings of lotuses: Śrī will come and grant boons.

Grind lotus seeds, tagara, lotus filaments, and sandalwood together with honey and have them made into pills. Having empowered them together with incense, whoever they are given to will come under control. Having recited over a flower garland, whoever's head it is tied upon will come under control.

Take red sandalwood, campaka flowers, lotus filaments, husks of red śāli rice, girikarṇikā, kurantaka seeds, grain, sprouted pulses, costus, tagara, turuṣka, and sesame in equal parts, combine them, and have them made into pills with the ghee of a tawny cow. One should first undertake all the practices.

One who wishes to bring the king's queen and her retinue under control should make an image of kuśa grass, press it with the left hand, and recite: she and her retinue will come under control. To bring brahmins under control, make eight thousand fire offerings of sesame mixed with curd, honey, and ghee: they will come under control. To bring kṣatriyas under control, make eight thousand fire offerings of barley mixed with curd, honey, and ghee: they will come under control. To bring vaiśyas under control, make eight thousand fire offerings of black mustard seed: they will come under control.
